connections.quote: “Shall we say that this is a refutation of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina? Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina could tell you: I can still say that the Patriarchs instituted the prayers, and the Sages associated them with the sacrifices. For if you do not say so, who, according to Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina, instituted the additional prayer? Rather, the Patriarchs instituted the prayers, and the Sages associated them with the sacrifices.”

connections.hePhrase: וּתְפִלָּה בִּמְקוֹם קָרְבָּנוֹת, וּדְעָנִי נִקְרָא "מִנְחָה", שֶׁחָשׁוּב לִפְנֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַתָּנָה וּמִנְחָה, וְגַם הוּא לְשׁוֹן נִיחָא, כִּי הוּא מְקַבֵּל תֵּיכֶף הַנִּיחָא.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: Why is the meal-offering different, in that “a soul” is stated concerning it? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Who ordinarily brings a meal-offering? A poor person. I account it to him as though he had offered his soul before Me.”

connections.hePhrase: [כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נ.) דִּבִּשְׁאֵלָה: "הַרְחֶב פִּיךָ וַאֲמַלְאֵהוּ" (תְּהִלִּים פא, יא)],
connections.quote: ‘Abaye said to Rav Dimi: But it is written, ‘And from Your blessing may the house of Your servant be blessed forever’! A request is different. But even concerning a request, is it not written, ‘Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it’? That verse is written concerning words of Torah.’

connections.hePhrase: [כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת נ.) דִּבִּשְׁאֵלָה: "הַרְחֶב פִּיךָ וַאֲמַלְאֵהוּ" (תְּהִלִּים פא, יא)],
connections.quote: ‘I am Hashem your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt. Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.’

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה עֲצַת יַעְבֵּץ שֶׁאָמַר: "אִם בָּרֵךְ [תְּבָרֲכֵנִי] וְגוֹמֵר" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ד, י),
connections.quote: ‘Jabez called to the God of Israel, saying: If You will indeed bless me and enlarge my territory, if Your hand will be with me and You will keep me from harm so that it does not grieve me… God brought about what he had requested.’

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ בִּתְמוּרָה (טז.) שֶׁאָמַר: אִם וְכוּלֵי וְאִם לָאו הֲרֵינִי הוֹלֵךְ וְכוּלֵי,
connections.quote: ‘‘If You will indeed bless me’—with Torah. ‘And enlarge my boundary’—with students. ‘And may Your hand be with me’—that my learning not be forgotten from my heart. ‘And keep me from harm,’ mera’ati—that companions, re’im, like me be provided for me. ‘That I not be grieved’—that the evil inclination not overpower me and keep me from studying. If You do this, well and good; if not, I am going down in my grief to Sheol. Immediately, ‘God brought about what he had asked.’’

connections.hePhrase: כְּעִנְיַן "אִם צָדַקְתָּ מַה תִּתֶּן לוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (אִיּוֹב לה, ז), כִּי לַאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַאי נַפְקָא מִינַּהּ בֵּין צַדִּיק לְרָשָׁע, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בָּזֶה.
connections.quote: ‘If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He take from your hand?’

connections.hePhrase: כְּעִנְיַן "אִם צָדַקְתָּ מַה תִּתֶּן לוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (אִיּוֹב לה, ז), כִּי לַאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַאי נַפְקָא מִינַּהּ בֵּין צַדִּיק לְרָשָׁע, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בָּזֶה.
connections.heRef: תניא, חלק ראשון; ליקוטי אמרים מ״ח:ג׳-ד׳
connections.quote: “This is not the place to explain the particulars of the contractions, how and what they are. In general, however, they are the concealment and hiding of the flow of light and vitality, so that it does not shine and flow openly to the lower beings, clothing itself in them, influencing them, and bringing them to life as something from nothing—except for a very minute amount of light and vitality, so that they remain limited and finite. This is an exceedingly small illumination, accounted as nothing in relation to illumination without limit or end; there is no proportion or relation between them at all. The meaning of “proportion” in numbers is known: the number one has a proportion to a million, being one part in a million. But in relation to something entirely without limit or number, no numerical proportion exists. Even a thousand million and myriads of myriads do not have even the proportion of one to a thousand million and myriads of myriads; rather, they are accounted as absolutely nothing. Precisely so is this small illumination, which clothes itself in the higher and lower worlds to influence and give them life, in relation to the hidden and concealed light that is infinite. That light does not clothe itself in and influence the worlds openly to give them life, but encompasses them from above, and is called “that which encompasses all worlds.””

connections.hePhrase: [ריד] כְּשֶׁאָדָם מְבַקֵּשׁ עַל מַעֲלָה, יֵשׁ לוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה יוֹתֵר מִגְּבוּלוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שָׁוְא וּדְבַר כָּזָב הַרְחֵק מִמֶּנִּי" (מִשְׁלֵי ל, ח).
connections.quote: ‘Keep falsehood and lying speech far from me. Give me neither poverty nor wealth; feed me the bread allotted to me.’

connections.hePhrase: [ריד] כְּשֶׁאָדָם מְבַקֵּשׁ עַל מַעֲלָה, יֵשׁ לוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה יוֹתֵר מִגְּבוּלוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "שָׁוְא וּדְבַר כָּזָב הַרְחֵק מִמֶּנִּי" (מִשְׁלֵי ל, ח).
connections.displayRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 5
connections.canonicalRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Lech Lecha 5
connections.quote: “When he returned from Egypt it therefore says, ‘Avram was very heavy.’ After he had been completely clarified in poverty through the first trial, ‘very heavy’ expresses a burden: he feared for himself because of wealth, like Shlomo's prayer, ‘Give me neither poverty nor wealth.’ Of Lot it does not say ‘heavy,’ only that Lot who went with Avram also possessed property. The expression indicates gladness, for he had no fear at all. Of Avraham, by contrast, it says ‘heavy’ because of his fear. Hence, ‘He went on his journeys … and Avram called there’: even now he was concerned about wealth. In this way he clarified himself in every circumstance.”
connections.explanation: Mei HaShiloach reads Avraham's wealth as a new burden of responsibility after the trial of poverty, using the same prayer from Proverbs cited here. Its material setting illustrates the siman's more general distinction: more of a gift is not automatically better unless the recipient can hold it properly. Asking for an enlarged vessel therefore accompanies asking for a greater Torah blessing.
connections.headline: Receiving more also enlarges the work of reception

connections.hePhrase: וְסִיֵּים עַל זֶה: "רֵאשׁ וָעֹשֶׁר [אַל תִּתֶּן לִי]... פֶּן אֶשְׂבַּע וְכִחַשְׁתִּי וְגוֹמֵר" (שָׁם, ח–ט),
connections.quote: “The second request is that You not give me poverty and destitution in understanding, so that I fall short in knowledge of what a human being can attain; and that You likewise not give me wealth, so that I turn to seeking wisdom in what a human being cannot attain. Rather, bestow upon me, in understanding, the nourishment appropriate to the intellect—neither less nor more.”

connections.hePhrase: [וְכֵן דָּרְשׁוּ שָׁם אַחַר כָּךְ: "וְהִרְבִּיתָ אֶת גְּבוּלִי" – בְּבָנִים וּבָנוֹת, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה נַעֲשָׂה כְּלִי קִבּוּל גָּדוֹל לְעִנְיַן הָעֹשֶׁר],
connections.quote: “Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi says: “If You would indeed bless me”—with fruitfulness and multiplication; “and enlarge my border”—with sons and daughters; “and Your hand would be with me”—in business dealings; “and You would keep me from evil”—so that I should have no pain in my head, ears, or eyes; “that it should not grieve me”—so that the evil inclination should not overpower me and prevent my study. If You do this, well and good; if not, I shall go in my grief to the grave. “And God granted him what he asked.””

connections.hePhrase: וְאַחַר כָּךְ: "וְהָיְתָה יָדְךָ עִמָּדִי" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ד, י) – שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּכַּח וְיִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ,
connections.quote: see note 3208.
connections.context: The expression “Your hand would be with me” must remain visible: Rav Tzadok connects it with Torah remaining securely “in his hand,” through the interpretation cited from Temurah.

connections.hePhrase: וְאַחַר כָּךְ: "וְהָיְתָה יָדְךָ עִמָּדִי" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א ד, י) – שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁתַּכַּח וְיִתְקַיֵּים בְּיָדוֹ,
connections.quote: “We find this with Jabez: although he was emptied of all this world’s desires and constantly engaged in Torah, he prayed, “‘That it should not grieve me’—that the evil inclination should not overpower me and prevent my study,” as stated in Temurah 16a. Even while sitting in the study hall he feared that the evil inclination would confuse his mind. For this he needs help from the blessed God.”
connections.explanation: Lech Lecha emphasizes that Yaavetz’s existing devotion did not make him independent of divine assistance. This helps explain why the present siman distinguishes a blessing in Torah from the further requests for retention, companions, and protection from sin. Receiving an insight and becoming a vessel in which it can endure are different needs. The prayer concerns the continuing life of Torah within the learner, including the ability to remain available for study and teaching.
connections.headline: Even established learning needs prayer that it will continue to bear fruit

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי "יָדְךָ", פֵּירוּשׁ: דְּ"יָדְכָה" בְּהֵ"א נִדְרַשׁ יָד כֵּהָה (מְנָחוֹת לז.), אֲבָל "יָדְךָ" הַיְינוּ יָמִין,
connections.quote: ‘This is a dispute among tanna’im: ‘Your hand,’ yadekhah, spelled with a final hei—this is the left hand. Others say: ‘Your hand’ includes an amputee. Another teaching states: One who has no arm is exempt from [arm] tefillin. Others say: ‘Your hand,’ yadekhah, includes an amputee.’

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי "יָדְךָ", פֵּירוּשׁ: דְּ"יָדְכָה" בְּהֵ"א נִדְרַשׁ יָד כֵּהָה (מְנָחוֹת לז.), אֲבָל "יָדְךָ" הַיְינוּ יָמִין,
connections.quote: “Does Rabbi Shimon require both? But was it not taught: Rabbi Shimon says: Wherever “hand” is stated, it means only the right; wherever “finger” is stated, it means only the right!”

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו.): בִּימִינוֹ זוֹ תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי,
connections.quote: ‘‘By His right hand’—this is Torah, as it is said: ‘From His right hand, a fiery law for them.’ ‘And by the arm of His strength’—these are tefillin, as it is said: ‘Hashem will give strength to His people.’’

connections.hePhrase: רַק יַעְבֵּץ – הוּא עָתְנִיאֵל – לְבָבוֹ הָיָה רוֹעֵשׁ עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בַּגְּמָרָא דְּהָיָה מְפוּלְפָּל יוֹתֵר מִיהוֹשֻׁעַ, רַק שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ חֲבֵירִים וְלֹא תַלְמִידִים,
connections.quote: “Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: When Moshe our teacher departed for the Garden of Eden, he said to Yehoshua: Ask me all your doubts. He replied: My teacher, did I ever leave you for a single hour and go elsewhere? Did you not write concerning me, “His attendant Yehoshua son of Nun, a youth, would not depart from the tent”? Immediately Yehoshua’s strength weakened; three hundred laws were forgotten by him, and seven hundred doubts arose for him. All Israel rose to kill him. The Holy One, blessed be He, said to him: To tell you is impossible; go and occupy them with war, as it is said, “After the death of Moshe, servant of Hashem, Hashem said…” A baraita taught: One thousand seven hundred inferences from minor to major, verbal analogies, and precise details of the scribes were forgotten during the mourning for Moshe. Rabbi Abbahu said: Nevertheless, Otniel son of Kenaz restored them through his dialectical reasoning, as it is said, “Otniel son of Kenaz, brother of Caleb, captured it, and he gave him Achsah his daughter as a wife.””

connections.hePhrase: וְנִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב כַּאֲשֶׁר הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הֵם קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּימָא שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה לֹא יָזוּעַ עוֹד, וְשֶׁאֵין עֲבֵירָה מְכַבַּתּוֹ, כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹ דַּי לְפוֹצֵץ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
connections.quote: “Another interpretation: A transgression extinguishes a mitzvah, but a transgression does not extinguish Torah, as it is said, “Many waters cannot extinguish love.” Rav Yosef said: A mitzvah, while a person is occupied with it, protects and rescues; when he is not occupied with it, it protects but does not rescue. Torah, whether he is occupied with it or is not occupied with it, protects and rescues. Rabbah challenged this: If so, did Doeg and Achitofel not occupy themselves with Torah? Why did it not protect them? Rather, Rava said: Torah, while a person is occupied with it, protects and rescues; when he is not occupied with it, it protects but does not rescue. A mitzvah, whether a person is occupied with it or is not occupied with it, protects but does not rescue.”

connections.hePhrase: וְנִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם בָּזֶה יֵשׁ הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב כַּאֲשֶׁר הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הֵם קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּימָא שֶׁמִּמֶּנָּה לֹא יָזוּעַ עוֹד, וְשֶׁאֵין עֲבֵירָה מְכַבַּתּוֹ, כִּי יֵשׁ בּוֹ דַּי לְפוֹצֵץ הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע,
connections.quote: “Is not My word like fire, says Hashem, and like a hammer that shatters (yefotzetz) the rock?”

connections.hePhrase: וְ"הַחָכְמָה תָּעֹז לֶחָכָם" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יט) וּמְסַלֶּקֶת הַיִּרְאָה שֶׁמָּא יִגְרוֹם הַחֵטְא, שֶׁזֶּה נִקְרָא יִרְאָה גַּבֵּי יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם (בְּרָכוֹת ד.).
connections.quote: ‘This is like Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi’s teaching. Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi raised a contradiction: It is written, ‘Behold, I am with you, and I will guard you wherever you go,’ yet it is written, ‘Jacob was very afraid.’ He said: ‘Perhaps sin will have its effect.’’

connections.hePhrase: וּמִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ תְּקִיפוּת מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, הוּא מְסוּלָּק מִכָּל מִינֵי יְרָאוֹת:
connections.quote: “This is called “flying in the air”: the person who fears has nothing clearly established upon which to rely. In every matter he fears and trembles, even in a deed that is clearly good, lest there be some blemish or deficiency. Thus he has no foundation on which his foot can take hold and find support. This is his fear preceding his wisdom, for “the beginning of wisdom is fear of Hashem.” Afterward, through this, his wisdom endures, and “wisdom strengthens the wise person.” A “strong tower” is formed, into which “the righteous runs and is exalted.” Running means expansion without restraint, for “his heart is firm, trusting in Hashem,” and concerning this it says, “His heart is supported; he will not fear.””

connections.hePhrase: [רטו] הַלֵּב הוּא הַכְּלִי קִבּוּל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לא.) דְּיִרְאָה הוּא הָאוֹצָר, וּבְיוֹמָא (עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֶב אָיִן" (מִשְׁלֵי יז, טז) דְּשָׁם הַיִּרְאָה.
connections.quote: see note 1582 (Vol. I).
connections.context: The verse’s word is “heart.” Yoma 72b applies it to learning without fear of Heaven; Rav Tzadok uses that reading to identify the heart as the vessel that receives and preserves wisdom.

connections.hePhrase: [רטו] הַלֵּב הוּא הַכְּלִי קִבּוּל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לא.) דְּיִרְאָה הוּא הָאוֹצָר, וּבְיוֹמָא (עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֶב אָיִן" (מִשְׁלֵי יז, טז) דְּשָׁם הַיִּרְאָה.
connections.quote: “And so too all secular wisdom of the heathen nations is termed: "Why is there a price in the hand of a fool to buy wisdom, seeing he has no heart?" which our Sages expounded in Yoma (72b) as referring to the fear of Heaven, which is the mystical secret of Knesset Yisrael, existing exclusively among Israel whose hearts follow their supernal wisdom, whereupon wisdom receives back from the heart and they gaze face-to-face, and then the divine flow shoots forth like an arrow, parallel to the rainbow granted to Noah after "the inclination of the heart is evil from his youth";”
connections.explanation: Dover Tzedek develops the same verse “to acquire wisdom, when there is no heart” as a failure of living connection between mind and heart. The relationship is reciprocal: the heart follows wisdom, while wisdom also receives from the heart. This explains why the present siman treats yirah and peace as more than preliminary restrictions; they form the capacity by which greater wisdom can be received and expressed.
connections.headline: The receiving heart also gives life to wisdom

connections.hePhrase: וְהַיְינוּ דְּיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם הוּא הַגְדָּרַת חֶמְדַּת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בִּידֵי אָדָם,
connections.quote: “Rabbi Chanina also said: Everything is in the hands of Heaven except the fear of Heaven, as it is said, “And now, Israel, what does Hashem your God ask of you, except to fear?” Is fear of Heaven a small matter? Did Rabbi Chanina not say in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai: The Holy One, blessed be He, has in His storehouses only a treasury of the fear of Heaven, as it is said, “The fear of Hashem is His treasure”? Yes: in relation to Moshe it is a small matter. As Rabbi Chanina said: A parable of a person from whom a large vessel is requested: if he has it, it seems to him like a small vessel; if a small vessel is requested and he does not have it, it seems to him like a large vessel.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהַיְינוּ דְּיִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם הוּא הַגְדָּרַת חֶמְדַּת הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁבַּלֵּב, שֶׁזֶּהוּ בִּידֵי אָדָם,
connections.heRef: תניא, חלק ראשון; ליקוטי אמרים י״ד:ב׳-ה׳
connections.quote: “It is otherwise with a matter entrusted to the heart: that evil should truly be repulsive in the heart and hated with utter hatred—or even with a hatred that is not utter. This cannot be completely true except through the greatness and strength of love of Hashem, in the mode of “love in delights”: delighting in Hashem as a foretaste of the World to Come. Of this our Sages said, “May you see your world in your lifetime,” and so forth. Not everyone merits this, for it is akin to receiving a reward, as it is written, “I give your priesthood as a service of gift,” and so forth, as explained elsewhere. Therefore Job said, “You created righteous people,” and so forth. As stated in the Tikkunim, the souls of Israel have different grades and aspects: the pious, the mighty who overcome their inclination, masters of Torah, prophets, and righteous people, and so forth; see there. This explains the doubled language of the oath, “Be righteous, and do not be wicked.” At first this is puzzling: once a person is made to swear, “Be righteous,” why must he also swear not to be wicked? Rather, because not everyone merits becoming righteous, and a person does not have such complete freedom of choice in this—to delight truly in Hashem and to find evil truly repulsive—he is made to swear a second time, “Do not be wicked,” at least. In this, the power of choice and authority are given to everyone: to govern the desire in his heart and subdue his inclination, so as not to be wicked for even one hour throughout his life, both in “turning from evil” and in “doing good.” “There is no good but Torah”—meaning Torah study, which is equivalent to them all.”

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן כְּלִי מַחֲזִיק בְּרָכָה הוּא הַשָּׁלוֹם, וּבוֹ מְסַיֶּימֶת הַתְּפִלָּה, שֶׁמְּבַקֵּשׁ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל טוֹבָה, וּבַסּוֹף מְבַקֵּשׁ עַל שָׁלוֹם כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כְּלִי קִבּוּל לְרוֹב טוֹבָה.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Shimon ben Chalafta said: The Holy One, blessed be He, found no vessel that holds blessing for Israel except peace, as it says, “The Lord gives strength to His people; the Lord blesses His people with peace.””
connections.context: The Mishnah explicitly calls peace the vessel that holds blessing. This supplies Rav Tzadok’s explanation of why the prayer for peace concludes the petitions for blessing.

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (מז:) וּבְתַעֲנִית (כג.) דְּאֵין יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל רוֹב טוֹבָה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה, וְהַיְינוּ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הוּסַר לֵב הָאֶבֶן.
connections.quote: “Just as they inform him of the punishment for the commandments, so they inform him of their reward. They tell him: Know that the World to Come is prepared only for the righteous, and Israel in the present time cannot receive either an abundance of good or an abundance of punishment. They do not multiply matters upon him or scrutinize him excessively.”
connections.context: These words are addressed to a prospective convert. Rav Tzadok draws specifically on the present inability to receive abundant good and relates it to the heart’s capacity to receive blessing. The statement begins on 47a and continues on 47b.

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (מז:) וּבְתַעֲנִית (כג.) דְּאֵין יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל רוֹב טוֹבָה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה, וְהַיְינוּ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הוּסַר לֵב הָאֶבֶן.
connections.quote: “Master of the universe, Your people Israel whom You brought out of Egypt cannot endure either excessive good or excessive calamity. You were angry with them, and they could not endure; You bestowed good upon them, and they could not endure. May it be Your will that the rains cease and there be relief in the world.”
connections.context: Choni says this after rain becomes overwhelming. The explicit statement about inability to endure excessive good is on 23a; 22b begins the related discussion of praying about excessive rain. Rav Tzadok applies the limited capacity to receive abundance to the heart’s present condition.

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (מז:) וּבְתַעֲנִית (כג.) דְּאֵין יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל רוֹב טוֹבָה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה, וְהַיְינוּ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הוּסַר לֵב הָאֶבֶן.
connections.quote: “It is known that Yitzchak is the quality of restraint: in this world, as long as the inclination is present, people must restrain themselves. As stated in Yevamot, Israel cannot receive an abundance of good. And in Bereshit Rabbah, at the beginning of Vayeshev: Is what is prepared for the righteous in the future not enough for them, that they seek to dwell in tranquility in this world?”

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (מז:) וּבְתַעֲנִית (כג.) דְּאֵין יָכוֹל לְקַבֵּל רוֹב טוֹבָה בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה, וְהַיְינוּ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הוּסַר לֵב הָאֶבֶן.
connections.quote: “I will give them one heart, and a new spirit I will place within you. I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh, so that they may walk in My statutes, keep My ordinances, and perform them. They shall be My people, and I shall be their God.”

connections.hePhrase: וּלְעָתִיד לָבוֹא אֵלִיָּהוּ בָּא לַעֲשׂוֹת שָׁלוֹם בָּעוֹלָם, וְיִסְתַּלֵּק הַקִּנְאָה וְהַשִּׂנְאָה וְגַאֲוָה מִלֵּב, אָז מְקַבֵּל כָּל אֶחָד רוֹב טוֹבָה בְּשֶׁפַע.
connections.quote: “The Sages say: Neither to distance nor to draw near, but to make peace in the world, as it is said, “Behold, I am sending you Eliyahu the prophet,” and so forth, “and he shall turn the heart of fathers toward children, and the heart of children toward their fathers.””

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יד:): רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נִכְנַס בְּשָׁלוֹם וְיָצָא בְּשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי מִדַּת הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאָחַז בָּהּ, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (טז.) "וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרוֹעֵי צֹאן",
connections.quote: ‘Ben Azzai gazed and died. Of him Scripture says: ‘Precious in the eyes of Hashem is the death of His pious ones.’ Ben Zoma gazed and was stricken. Of him Scripture says: ‘If you find honey, eat just enough, lest you gorge on it and vomit it up.’ Acher cut down the plantings. Rabbi Akiva emerged in peace.’

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יד:): רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא נִכְנַס בְּשָׁלוֹם וְיָצָא בְּשָׁלוֹם, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי מִדַּת הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁאָחַז בָּהּ, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּיבָמוֹת (טז.) "וַאֲפִילּוּ לְרוֹעֵי צֹאן",
connections.quote: “He said to him: Are you Akiva, whose name goes from one end of the world to the other? Fortunate are you to have gained a name, yet you have not reached even the cattle herders. Rabbi Akiva said to him: Not even the shepherds of sheep.”
connections.context: Yehonatan ben Harkinas challenges Rabbi Akiva, who answers without asserting his own stature. Rav Tzadok sees this humility and refusal of rivalry as the peace by which Rabbi Akiva could enter and leave safely.

connections.hePhrase: עַל יְדֵי זֶה נִכְנַס וְיָצָא וְהִשִּׂיג חָכְמָה שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ, כִּדְאִיתָא (חֲגִיגָה טו:) דְּבִקְשׁוּ מַלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת לְדָחְפּוֹ, מַשְׁמָע שֶׁהָיָה לְמַעְלָה מִמַּדְרֵגָתוֹ.
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Akiva ascended in peace and descended in peace. Concerning him Scripture says: ‘Draw me after You; let us run.’ The ministering angels sought to push even Rabbi Akiva away, but the Holy One, blessed be He, said to them: ‘Leave this elder alone, for he is worthy of making use of My glory.’’

connections.hePhrase: וּבַגְּמָרָא (שָׁם עַמּוּד א) אִיתָא טָעוּת בֶּן זוֹמָא בַּהֶבְדֵּל שֶׁבֵּין מַיִם עֶלְיוֹנִים לְמַיִם תַּחְתּוֹנִים, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
connections.quote: “Ben Zoma said: I was looking between the upper waters and the lower waters, and there are only three fingers between them, as it says, “The spirit of God hovered over the face of the waters,” like a dove hovering over her young without touching them. Rabbi Yehoshua said to his students: Ben Zoma is still outside. But when was “the spirit of God hovered”? On the first day; the division occurred on the second day, as it is written, “Let it divide between water and water.””
connections.context: The second paragraph identifies the flaw in Ben Zoma’s inference: he used a verse from before the separation to measure the separation. Rav Tzadok’s words refer to that mistake, so the story alone was insufficient.

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ, מַיִם עֶלְיוֹנִים וּמַיִם תַּחְתּוֹנִים יָדוּעַ דְּהֵם הַנִּקְרָא בַּזֹּהַר "מַיִין דְּכוּרִין" וּ"מַיִין נוּקְבִין", הַיְינוּ הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא עַל יְדֵי הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב וְהַמִּלּוּי מִלְּמַעְלָה עַל יְדֵי הַחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ.
connections.quote: “The upper waters are male, and the lower waters are female. At first they were waters within waters, until they were separated so that the upper and lower waters could be distinguished: this is Elohim (another reading: “the upper waters”), and this is Adonai (another reading: “the lower waters”). These are the upper heh and the lower heh. What is written? “God made the firmament.” This extension took the name Elohim—the upper waters—and the lower waters are Adonai. Nevertheless, once the male waters were completed with the female waters, the name Elohim extended through all.”

connections.hePhrase: רַק שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת בְּחֵשֶׁק הָאָדָם, אֲפִילּוּ לְתוֹרָה וְלִידִיעַת אֱלֹהוּת, מֵאַחַר שֶׁאֵין הַלֵּב נָקִי, הַחֵשֶׁק הַטֶּבַע מִמֶּנּוּ גַּם כֵּן אֵין נָקִי לְגַמְרֵי, וְאֶפְשָׁר שֶׁיִּהְיֶה תַּאֲוָה כְּכָל הַתַּאֲווֹת וּכְמוֹ שֶׁחוֹשְׁקִין לָדַעַת חָכְמָה וְכַדּוֹמֶה.
connections.quote: “In the blessing “Who bestows good kindnesses,” a person’s awakening below in the quality of kindness, Abraham our father’s quality, awakens kindness above, as the holy Zohar teaches (III, beginning of 92b). In this blessing we ask, “Subdue our inclination to serve You.” Likewise, in the blessing “With eternal love” we ask, “Unite our hearts to love and fear Your name”: may we have one heart for awe, emptying evil from the foolish heart. This blessing corresponds to love, Abraham our father’s quality, as it is said, “The offspring of Abraham, My beloved.” Our master and teacher Rabbi Ber, of blessed and holy memory, has already written that love comes from above, in the manner indicated by “For such is his way …”.”
connections.explanation: Peri Tzadik identifies a daily expression of the union sought here: the prayer “Unite our hearts to love and fear Your name.” Its account of asking God to subdue the inclination and empty evil from the heart translates Tzidkat HaTzadik’s relation between love, awe, and receptivity into the language of prayer.
connections.headline: Awe prepares the heart to receive love and wisdom

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק "לֹא בָרוּחַ ה' וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א יט, יא), פֵּירוּשׁ: רָצוֹן וְהִתְלַהֲבוּת בְּאַהֲבָה וְרַעַשׁ בְּיִרְאָה – הַכֹּל עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ נָקִי וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְעוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹ.
connections.quote: see note 587 (Vol. I).

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק "לֹא בָרוּחַ ה' וְגוֹמֵר" (מְלָכִים א יט, יא), פֵּירוּשׁ: רָצוֹן וְהִתְלַהֲבוּת בְּאַהֲבָה וְרַעַשׁ בְּיִרְאָה – הַכֹּל עֲדַיִן אֵינוֹ נָקִי וְשֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְעוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹ.
connections.displayRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Numbers, Korach 1
connections.canonicalRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Numbers, Korach 1
connections.quote: see note 2875.

connections.hePhrase: וְהִתְכַּלְלוּתָם הוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָרוֹמֵז לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה וְצוּרַת אָדָם שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Shimon opened again and said: “Hashem said to my lord: Sit at My right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.” “Hashem said to my lord”: the upper grade says to the lower grade, “Sit at My right hand,” so that west may be joined with south, left with right, to break the power of the other nations who worship the stars and constellations. “Hashem said to my lord”: “Hashem said”—this is Yaakov; “to my lord”—this is “the Ark of the Covenant, Lord of all the earth.””

connections.hePhrase: וְהִתְכַּלְלוּתָם הוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָרוֹמֵז לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה וְצוּרַת אָדָם שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת.
connections.quote: “As for the likeness of their faces, they had the face of a man, and the face of a lion on the right side, … and the face of an ox on the left side, … and the face of an eagle.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהִתְכַּלְלוּתָם הוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָרוֹמֵז לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה וְצוּרַת אָדָם שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת.
connections.quote: “Afterward it says: The merit of Yaakov and Yosef is in the west, as it is said, “The likeness of their faces was the face of a human,” and so forth. “The face of a human”—this is the likeness of Yaakov engraved upon the Throne of Glory. “The likeness of an ox”—this is the likeness of Yosef, as it is said, “His firstborn ox has majesty,” and so forth. The matter is that it is written, “The earth is My footstool,” meaning the Temple, where the Divine Presence rests. In the Gemara it is called “the house of the footstool of our God,” and so too in the Midrash Rabbah at the end of Eikhah. This is the Holy of Holies, which is in the west; and “the Divine Presence is in the west,” as stated in Bava Batra. Therefore it places the merit of Avraham and Yitzchak in the east, for from them begins the dawning of the light, and Yaakov and Yosef in the west, for they are the essence of the congregation of Israel: all Israel are called “the house of Yaakov” and “the remnant of Yosef,” after Yosef, as stated in Bereshit Rabbah, section 71.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהִתְכַּלְלוּתָם הוּא מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָרוֹמֵז לְשֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה וְצוּרַת אָדָם שֶׁבַּמֶּרְכָּבָה שֶׁהוּא תַּכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵימוּת.
connections.quote: “Who has seen a compassionate father become cruel? Rather, it was so that the opposition of water and fire might be present and they might be crowned in their places (another reading omits “as is fitting”), until Yaakov came and everything was properly ordered. The three patriarchs then became complete, and the upper and lower realms were properly ordered.”

connections.hePhrase: וְאַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לֹא נִשְׁלַם אֶלָּא אַחַר נִסָּיוֹן עֲשִׂירִי בָּעֲקֵידָה, שֶׁאָז אִתְכְּלִיל בְּמִדַּת יִצְחָק כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, קיט עַמּוּד ב), וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "עַתָּה יָדַעְתִּי כִּי יְרֵא [אֱלֹהִים אַתָּה]" (בְּרֵאשִׁית כב, יב).
connections.quote: “Here one must consider: “God tested Avraham”—should it not say “Yitzchak”? Yitzchak was thirty-seven years old, and his father was not liable for his punishment: had Yitzchak said, “I do not want this,” his father would not have been punished on his account. Why, then, does it say “God tested Avraham,” and not “He tested Yitzchak”? Rather, it is indeed Avraham, who needed to be integrated with judgment, for previously Avraham had no judgment in him at all; now water was integrated with fire. Avraham was not complete until now, when he was crowned to perform judgment and establish it in its place. Throughout his life he had not been complete until now, when water was integrated with fire and fire with water. Therefore “God tested Avraham,” not Yitzchak: He summoned Avraham to become integrated with judgment. When he did this, fire entered water, and each was completed with the other. He performed judgment so that one would be integrated with the other. Then the evil inclination came to accuse Avraham, saying that he had not been properly completed until he performed judgment upon Yitzchak. For the evil inclination is “after these things,” and it came to accuse.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "יַעֲקֹב אֲשֶׁר פָּדָה אֶת אַבְרָהָם" (יְשַׁעְיָה כט, כב), כִּי מִצַּד מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְכַּלְלוּת שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן כְּלוּלָה בְּאַבְרָהָם – נִיצּוֹל.
connections.quote: “Therefore, thus says the Lord to the house of Jacob—He who redeemed Abraham: Jacob shall no longer be ashamed, and his face shall no longer grow pale.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "יַעֲקֹב אֲשֶׁר פָּדָה אֶת אַבְרָהָם" (יְשַׁעְיָה כט, כב), כִּי מִצַּד מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְכַּלְלוּת שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן כְּלוּלָה בְּאַבְרָהָם – נִיצּוֹל.
connections.quote: ““To the house of Jacob, who redeemed Abraham”: Where do we find that Jacob redeemed Abraham? Rav Yehuda said: He redeemed him from the suffering of raising children.”
connections.context: The verse can be read in its ordinary sense with God as the redeemer. The Gemara also reads Jacob as the subject of “redeemed.” Rav Tzadok adopts that latter grammatical reading for his own explanation of Abraham’s rescue; the Gemara’s explanation here concerns raising the tribes.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "יַעֲקֹב אֲשֶׁר פָּדָה אֶת אַבְרָהָם" (יְשַׁעְיָה כט, כב), כִּי מִצַּד מִדַּת יַעֲקֹב שֶׁהוּא הַהִתְכַּלְלוּת שֶׁהָיָה גַּם כֵּן כְּלוּלָה בְּאַבְרָהָם – נִיצּוֹל.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Rav Yitzchak said: Avraham was saved from the fiery furnace only through the merit of Yaakov. A parable of a man who had a case before the ruler, and the ruler sentenced him to be burned. The ruler foresaw through his astrology that this man would beget a daughter who would marry a king. He said: He deserves to be saved through the merit of the daughter he will beget, who will marry a king. So Avraham was sentenced by Nimrod to be burned, and the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that Yaakov would arise from him. He said: Avraham deserves to be saved through Yaakov’s merit. Thus it is written: “Therefore, so says Hashem to the house of Yaakov, who redeemed Avraham”—Yaakov redeemed Avraham.”

connections.hePhrase: דְּמִצַּד מִדָּתוֹ לְבַד, הֲרֵי בְּיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן נֶאֱמַר: "וְהָאָרֶץ הָיְתָה תֹהוּ" (בְּרֵאשִׁית א, ב), דְּעוֹלַם הַתֹּהוּ וְהַשְּׁבִירָה בָּא מִזֶּה: עַל יְדֵי תֹּקֶף הַחֵשֶׁק וְהָאַהֲבָה לְהַשִּׂיג אוֹר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּלֹא יִרְאָה הַמְצַמְצֶמֶת.
connections.quote: ‘The earth was formless and empty, with darkness upon the surface of the deep, and the spirit of God hovering over the surface of the waters.’

connections.hePhrase: וּלְכָךְ בְּיוֹם שֵׁנִי נַעֲשָׂה רָקִיעַ מַבְדִּיל בֵּין מַיִם לָמָיִם, שֶׁהַיִּרְאָה הוּא הַכָּרַת הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁאֵין חֶשְׁקוֹ בִּשְׁלֵימוּת כְּמוֹ הַמַּיִם עֶלְיוֹנִים שֶׁהוּא רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַמַּשְׁפִּיעַ.
connections.quote: “And God said: ‘Let there be a firmament in the midst of the waters, and let it divide between water and water.’”

connections.hePhrase: וְהַהֶבְדֵּל כִּמְלֹא נִימָא, וּפֵירֵשׁ בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן יט) שֶׁהוּא הַסּוֹד דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם.
connections.quote: “The upper waters are the Written Torah; the lower waters are the Oral Torah. The hair between them is Yesod, which is the secret of Torah and the foundation and root of both.”
connections.context: The preceding passage describes the separation as a hair’s breadth. This sentence gives the interpretation needed here: that hair is the secret of Torah, joining the Written and Oral Torah. Rav Tzadok invokes it to explain the extremely fine distinction he has just described.

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לא.): אִי יִרְאַת ה' הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ וְכוּלֵי, מוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ – שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא נִפְגָּע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
connections.quote: see note 1590 (Vol. I).
connections.context: The grain represents acquired learning and the preservative represents fear of Heaven. Rav Tzadok cites the warning that learning without the disposition that preserves and guides it can fail to benefit its possessor.

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לא.): אִי יִרְאַת ה' הִיא אוֹצָרוֹ וְכוּלֵי, מוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ – שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא נִפְגָּע חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל;
connections.quote: “Without this, they said in Shabbat: “It would have been better had you not brought it up.” This means that, Heaven forbid, it may become a deadly poison, as stated in Yoma, for the inclination grows stronger in a Torah scholar, as stated in Sukkah. Such a person too is called a Torah scholar, just as Doeg and Achitofel are called Torah scholars everywhere. When he lacks fear of sin with which to overcome the inclination, he may, Heaven forbid, become like Acher, of whom our Sages said in Chagigah: “Books of heretics,” and so forth, and “Greek song,” and so forth. That is, all his wisdom resembled the study of an external wisdom, pursued merely as wisdom and not to complete his deficiency, which is the essential meaning of the name Torah.”

connections.hePhrase: [רטז] בְּכָל יוֹם יֵשׁ חִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה, שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְחַדֵּשׁ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Berekhiah, Rabbi Chiyya, and the Sages there said in Rabbi Yehuda’s name: There is no day on which the Holy One, blessed be He, does not introduce a new halakhah in the heavenly court. What is the scriptural basis? “Listen attentively to the thunder of His voice and the utterance that goes from His mouth.” “Utterance” means Torah, as it is said, “You shall meditate upon it day and night.” Even those halakhot were known to Abraham.”

connections.hePhrase: וּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית הוּא עַל יְדֵי הַתּוֹרָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרֵישׁ בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה, וּמִסְּתָמָא גַּם הַחִדּוּשׁ הוּא עַל יְדֵי חִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה.
connections.quote: see note 869 (Vol. I).

connections.hePhrase: וּלְכָךְ אַחַר בִּרְכַּת יוֹצֵר הַמְּאוֹרוֹת, שֶׁהוּא הַהַכָּרָה בְּחִדּוּשׁ מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית בְּכָל יוֹם, תִּקְּנוּ בְּרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁהוּא כְּמוֹ בִּרְכַּת הַתּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (יא:), שֶׁמְּבַקֵּשׁ לֵידַע הַחִדּוּשֵׁי תוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא עַל יְדֵי חִדּוּשֵׁי מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית
connections.quote: “Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel: One who rose early to study before reciting Shema must recite a blessing. After reciting Shema he need not recite a blessing, for he has already been exempted through “Ahavah Rabbah.””
connections.context: The blessing before Shema includes a request for Torah and can serve as its blessing in the case discussed. That is the connection between prayer and Torah needed here; the Temple watch’s blessing is a different discussion on this page.

connections.hePhrase: וְאַשְׁרֵי מִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה אַחַר כָּךְ בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, שֶׁהוּא הַלִּמּוּד תּוֹרָה הַקָּבוּעַ בְּכָל יוֹם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְנָחוֹת צט:) דִּבִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שַׁחֲרִית וְעַרְבִית קִיֵּים "לֹא יָמוּשׁ" (יְהוֹשֻׁעַ א, ח).
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai: Even if a person recites only the Shema in the morning and evening, he has fulfilled ‘It shall not depart.’ It is forbidden to say this in the presence of unlearned people. Rava said: It is a mitzvah to say it in the presence of unlearned people.’

connections.hePhrase: וּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע – דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, תְּפִלָּה – אֵינוֹ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרָכוֹת כא.), כִּי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּשִּׂיגוּ בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁהוּא מִצְוַת "לְדַבֵּר בָּם וְגוֹמֵר", עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה יַשִּׂיג הַחִדּוּשִׁין שֶׁל כָּל יוֹם.
connections.quote: “Rather, Shema and the blessing after food are from the Torah, whereas prayer is rabbinic.”
connections.context: The Gemara is distinguishing obligations in its discussion of a person who has experienced a seminal emission. This is the explicit contrast in legal status that Rav Tzadok uses; the later discussion of doubt about reciting Shema cites a different position.

connections.hePhrase: וּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע – דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, תְּפִלָּה – אֵינוֹ דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרָכוֹת כא.), כִּי רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁיַּשִּׂיגוּ בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע שֶׁהוּא מִצְוַת "לְדַבֵּר בָּם וְגוֹמֵר", עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה יַשִּׂיג הַחִדּוּשִׁין שֶׁל כָּל יוֹם.
connections.quote: “And you shall teach them to your children, to speak of them (ledaber bam), when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up.”

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ (תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר תִּיקּוּן כב): לְבוּשִׁין דִּלְבַשׁ בְּצַפְרָא וְכוּלֵי, שֶׁאֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה תְּפִלָּה לַחֲבֶרְתָּהּ.
connections.quote: “He said to him: Rabbi, it is like a king sitting in his palace, with many people entering to see him. Some look at his garments, some at his person, and some at his deeds. Certainly, through his deeds it is known what the king is. In his garments he changes in many ways: the garments he wears in the morning he does not wear in the evening; the garments he wears one day he does not wear the next. So on every day, month, year, Shabbat, and festival, he changes his garments.”
connections.context: The source’s image is the king’s changing garments. Rav Tzadok applies it to the changing divine revelation expressed in each prayer. The source does not speak here of a person’s soul weaving a new garment of light at every prayer; that would be an added interpretation, not a quotation.

connections.hePhrase: וּבָא שַׁבָּת בָּא מְנוּחָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קיט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב): בְּמָטוּתָא מִינַּיְיכוּ לָא תְּחַלְּלוּנִי; גַּם עַל יְדֵי לִמּוּד תּוֹרָה בִּיגִיעָה נִקְרָא חִלּוּל, כִּי אָז הוּא מְנוּחָה וּמֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁנֶּהֱנִין מִזִּיו מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם.
connections.quote: “The Exilarch asked Rav Hamnuna: What does the verse mean, ‘And call Hashem’s holy day honored’? He answered: This is Yom Kippur, on which there is neither eating nor drinking. The Torah says: Honor it with clean clothing. As for ‘You shall honor it,’ Rav said: By eating earlier; Shmuel said: By eating later. The sons of Rav Pappa bar Abba asked Rav Pappa: For people like us, who have meat and wine every day, how should we make it different? He told them: If you usually eat early, eat later; if you usually eat late, eat earlier. In summer Rav Sheshet seated the scholars where the sun would reach them; in winter he seated them where the shade would reach them, so that they would get up promptly. Rabbi Zeira would seek out scholars studying in pairs and say to them, ‘Please do not profane Shabbat by neglecting its enjoyment.’”

connections.hePhrase: וּבָא שַׁבָּת בָּא מְנוּחָה, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (קיט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב): בְּמָטוּתָא מִינַּיְיכוּ לָא תְּחַלְּלוּנִי; גַּם עַל יְדֵי לִמּוּד תּוֹרָה בִּיגִיעָה נִקְרָא חִלּוּל, כִּי אָז הוּא מְנוּחָה וּמֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא, שֶׁנֶּהֱנִין מִזִּיו מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּעַצְמוֹ מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָהֶם.
connections.quote: “Shabbat too is called a statute, as stated in the Mekhilta cited above: “A statute”—this is Shabbat. This means that on Shabbat one merits the Oral Torah’s being engraved upon the heart without toil. The Jerusalem Talmud states: Shabbatot were given only for eating and drinking, and so forth; another says: Shabbatot were given only for engaging in words of Torah. The Pesikta states that they do not disagree: the statement about Torah study concerns laborers, while the statement about delight concerns Torah scholars.”

connections.hePhrase: וּבַיּוֹם עַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא הוּא מִדַּת אַיִן, פֵּירוּשׁ הֶעְדֵּר הַחֵשֶׁק, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח (נב עַמּוּד ב) עַל "מַה תִּצְעַק אֵלָי" – בְּעַתִּיקָא תַּלְיָא, שֶׁהוּא הַשְׁפָּעָה בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ נֶפֶשׁ הָאָדָם שֶׁלְּמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגוֹת הַמּוּרְגָּשׁוֹת בְּחָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ וְחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב.
connections.quote: ‘Then it is written: ‘Hashem said to Moses: Why do you cry out to Me?’ It was taught in Sifra diTzniuta: ‘To Me’ (21a)—specifically. Everything depends on the Ancient One. At that moment the Holy Ancient One was revealed, and favor was present in all the upper worlds. Then the light of all things shone.’

connections.hePhrase: וּבִסְעוּדָה שְׁלִישִׁית שֶׁהוּא עִם הַיְצִיאָה, אָז זְעֵיר אַנְפִּין שֶׁהוּא מִדַּת קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא הַמְּמַלֵּא לַחֵשֶׁק, וְהוּא אָז הַשֶּׁפַע הַיּוֹרֵד לְצוֹרֶךְ כָּל יְמֵי הַשָּׁבוּעַ גַּם כֵּן.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Elazar said to his father: How are these meals arranged? He said to him: Concerning Shabbat night it is written, “I shall cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth.” On that night the Queen and the entire field of apples are blessed, a person’s table is blessed, and an additional soul is given. That night is the Queen’s joy, and a person should rejoice in her joy and eat the Queen’s meal. On Shabbat day, at the second meal, it is written, “Then you shall delight above Hashem”—“above Hashem,” indeed. For at that time the Holy Ancient One is revealed, and all the worlds are in joy. We celebrate the completion and joy of the Ancient One, and the meal is certainly His. At the third meal of Shabbat it is written, “I shall feed you the inheritance of Jacob your father.” This is the meal of Zeir Anpin, who is in a state of completeness. All six days are blessed from that completeness. A person should rejoice at his meal and complete these meals, which are the meals of the complete faith of the holy seed of Israel, who belong to the supernal faith. For it is theirs, and not that of the nations who worship stars and constellations. Therefore it says, “Between Me and the children of Israel.””

connections.hePhrase: וְתִקְּנוּ עַל זֶה שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת, כִּי הַמַּאֲכָל קִיּוּם הַחַיִּים, וְעַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילוֹת כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵם נִכְנָסִים בַּלֵּב, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִסַּד הַמַּאֲכָל לְקִיּוּם חַיֵּי הָאָדָם, בְּוַדַּאי יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ חַיּוּת הַמְחַיֶּה לוֹ.
connections.quote: “The Sages taught: How many meals is a person obligated to eat on Shabbat? Three. Rabbi Chidka says: Four. Rabbi Yochanan said: Both expounded the same verse: ‘And Moses said: Eat it today, for today is a Shabbat to Hashem; today you shall not find it in the field’ (Exodus 16:25).”

connections.hePhrase: וְתִקְּנוּ עַל זֶה שָׁלֹשׁ סְעוּדוֹת, כִּי הַמַּאֲכָל קִיּוּם הַחַיִּים, וְעַל יְדֵי הָאֲכִילוֹת כִּרְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הֵם נִכְנָסִים בַּלֵּב, מֵאַחַר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ יִסַּד הַמַּאֲכָל לְקִיּוּם חַיֵּי הָאָדָם, בְּוַדַּאי יֵשׁ בּוֹ כֹּחַ חַיּוּת הַמְחַיֶּה לוֹ.
connections.quote: “In truth, even physical eating and drinking give vitality to the human soul, yet the soul’s vitality comes only through words of Torah, as it is said, “For it is your life,” and it is written, “Choose life.” They said: “If this is so in the place of our life,” and so forth, “we too,” and so forth. That is, words of Torah are the place of our life, like water for fish. Necessarily, then, food and drink contain the vitality of words of Torah. This is the well-known interpretation of the verse, “Not by bread,” and so forth, “but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of Hashem,” and so forth: it means what proceeds from Hashem’s mouth within the bread.”

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם בְּמַאֲכָל דְּחוֹל יֵשׁ שַׁיָּיכוּת, כִּדְאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (עא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): הַאי דְּלָא אֲמָרִי לָךְ מֵאוֹרְתָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אֲכַלִי בִּשְׂרָא דְּתוֹרָא.
connections.quote: “The next morning he said to him: “The Merciful One said ‘five cattle’—even five half-cattle. The reason I did not tell you this last night is that I had not eaten beef.””
connections.context: Rav Nachman supplies the legal answer after having failed to give it the previous evening. His explanation about not eating beef illustrates the connection Rav Tzadok draws between ordinary nourishment and the ability to clarify Torah. The sentence begins on 71b and finishes on 72a.

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם בְּמַאֲכָל דְּחוֹל יֵשׁ שַׁיָּיכוּת, כִּדְאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (עא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): הַאי דְּלָא אֲמָרִי לָךְ מֵאוֹרְתָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אֲכַלִי בִּשְׂרָא דְּתוֹרָא.
connections.heRef: תוספות על בבא קמא ע״ב א:א׳
connections.quote: ““Because I had not eaten beef”: He had been fasting.”

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם בְּמַאֲכָל דְּחוֹל יֵשׁ שַׁיָּיכוּת, כִּדְאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (עא סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): הַאי דְּלָא אֲמָרִי לָךְ מֵאוֹרְתָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא אֲכַלִי בִּשְׂרָא דְּתוֹרָא.
connections.quote: “Oil, which alludes to wisdom—the clear knowledge and recognition that “I am your God”—comes after proper eating, suitably directed toward God, to sustain one’s soul. Such eating then adds wisdom and knowledge of God. By contrast, gross eating like an animal dulls the heart and mind. This is like their saying in Bava Kamma: “The reason I did not tell you ... was that I had not eaten ox meat.””
connections.explanation: Et HaOchel adds the distinction between nourishment directed toward sustaining life for God and animal-like overeating. Its concluding image of oil as clear recognition specifies the effect of the former and the obstruction caused by the latter, clarifying why food’s influence on Torah understanding depends on its direction.
connections.headline: Receiving Torah’s renewal through the life carried by food

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ (מְכִילְתָּא רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח): לֹא נִיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא לְאוֹכְלֵי מָן, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁהוּא לֶחֶם שֶׁמַּלְאֲכֵי הַשָּׁרֵת אוֹכְלִין, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ חַיּוּת רוּחָנִי עָצוּם מְאֹד, וְעַל יָדוֹ זוֹכֶה לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַרְבֵּה.
connections.quote: “The Sages taught: “A man ate the bread of mighty ones”—bread that the ministering angels eat; these are Rabbi Akiva’s words. When these words were reported to Rabbi Yishmael, he said to them: Go and tell Akiva: Akiva, you have erred! Do the ministering angels eat bread? Has it not already been said, “I did not eat bread and I did not drink water”? Rather, how do I interpret “mighty ones”? Bread that is absorbed into the two hundred and forty-eight limbs.”

connections.hePhrase: וּמִסְּתָמָא כָּל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הָעוֹסְקִים בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לָהֶם, הֵם אוֹכְלֵי מָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: כָּל הַמְּקַבֵּל עוֹל תּוֹרָה מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּת וְעוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וּפַרְנָסָתוֹ הוּא דּוּגְמַת מָן, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ וַדַּאי אוֹתוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה לְהַכְנִיס בַּלֵּב חַיּוּת מֵאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַשִּׂיג דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵאֲמִיתַּת חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
connections.quote: “Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah says: Whoever takes upon himself the yoke of Torah, the yoke of government and the yoke of worldly occupation are removed from him; and whoever casts off the yoke of Torah, the yoke of government and the yoke of worldly occupation are placed upon him.”

connections.hePhrase: וּמִסְּתָמָא כָּל תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הָעוֹסְקִים בַּתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִּיתְּנָה תּוֹרָה לָהֶם, הֵם אוֹכְלֵי מָן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ: כָּל הַמְּקַבֵּל עוֹל תּוֹרָה מַעֲבִירִין מִמֶּנּוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּת וְעוֹל דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ, וּפַרְנָסָתוֹ הוּא דּוּגְמַת מָן, וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ וַדַּאי אוֹתוֹ קְדוּשָּׁה לְהַכְנִיס בַּלֵּב חַיּוּת מֵאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁעַל יְדֵי זֶה מַשִּׂיג דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מֵאֲמִיתַּת חָכְמָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ
connections.quote: “The Zohar therefore describes Netzach and Hod as garments of the Holy One. A garment covers and somewhat dims the strength of what is clothed, so that through it we can look upon what is clothed. They are also called the heavens that grind manna: the nourishment of the righteous, their delight in apprehending Hashem's radiance, as described in Berakhot. Thus Yoma calls manna the bread eaten by ministering angels, and Shemot Rabbah says that they are nourished by the radiance of the Shechinah. This delight occurs when the Shechinah is joined with her Beloved, and comes through the supporting powers that limit apprehension and grind it finely until it is fit as food and nourishment.”
connections.explanation: Kometz HaMinchah explains why the Zohar describes powers of limitation as grinding manna. Their concealment does not merely obstruct the light; it makes the illumination approachable as nourishment. This illuminates the present siman's movement from heavenly life to Torah received through eating, while preserving the need for a suitable form of reception rather than identifying food with unbounded divine light without mediation.
connections.headline: Manna as light made into nourishment

connections.hePhrase: [וּמִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמָּן: "בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי לֶחֶם יוֹמָיִם" (שְׁמוֹת טז, כט), נִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם לְעִנְיַן הַשְׁפָּעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁפַע כָּפוּל, וְהוּא טְעִימָה מֵהַשְׁפָּעַת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּם כֵּן לִטְעוֹם הַמַּאֲכָלוֹת דְּשַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת; וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי כֵּן בַּזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח סא עַמּוּד ב, עַיֵּין שָׁם]:
connections.quote: “See that Hashem has given you the Shabbat; therefore He gives you on the sixth day the bread of two days. Let every man remain in his place; let no man go out of his place on the seventh day.”

connections.hePhrase: [וּמִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמָּן: "בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי לֶחֶם יוֹמָיִם" (שְׁמוֹת טז, כט), נִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם לְעִנְיַן הַשְׁפָּעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁפַע כָּפוּל, וְהוּא טְעִימָה מֵהַשְׁפָּעַת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּם כֵּן לִטְעוֹם הַמַּאֲכָלוֹת דְּשַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת; וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי כֵּן בַּזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח סא עַמּוּד ב, עַיֵּין שָׁם]:
connections.quote: “Rabbi Shimon said: Many people in this time are nourished from it. Who are they? The companions who engage in Torah day and night. Could you suppose that they receive that very food? No; rather, something like that very food, which is worth two for one.”

connections.hePhrase: [וּמִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמָּן: "בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי לֶחֶם יוֹמָיִם" (שְׁמוֹת טז, כט), נִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם לְעִנְיַן הַשְׁפָּעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁפַע כָּפוּל, וְהוּא טְעִימָה מֵהַשְׁפָּעַת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּם כֵּן לִטְעוֹם הַמַּאֲכָלוֹת דְּשַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת; וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי כֵּן בַּזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח סא עַמּוּד ב, עַיֵּין שָׁם]:
connections.quote: “The five days rule on their own days, and each contains what it received; the sixth day contains more. This accords with Rabbi Elazar’s statement: Why does Scripture say “the sixth day,” which is not said of the other days? They explained: “The sixth”—the Queen is joined to it to prepare the table for the King. Therefore two portions are found in it: one for that day and one for preparation, in the joy of the King with the Queen.”
connections.context: Two passages clarify the reference. Zohar II 61b describes the special nourishment of Torah scholars; II 63b explicitly describes the sixth day’s double portion. The first supports the preceding discussion of spiritual nourishment, while the second fits the sentence about Friday. Both are quoted here so the reader can follow Rav Tzadok’s whole argument.

connections.hePhrase: [וּמִמַּה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּמָּן: "בַּיּוֹם הַשִּׁשִּׁי לֶחֶם יוֹמָיִם" (שְׁמוֹת טז, כט), נִרְאֶה כִּי גַּם לְעִנְיַן הַשְׁפָּעַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הוּא בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבַּת קֹדֶשׁ שֶׁפַע כָּפוּל, וְהוּא טְעִימָה מֵהַשְׁפָּעַת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב גַּם כֵּן לִטְעוֹם הַמַּאֲכָלוֹת דְּשַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת; וְשׁוּב מָצָאתִי כֵּן בַּזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח סא עַמּוּד ב, עַיֵּין שָׁם]:
connections.quote: “It is a mitzvah to taste the cooked dishes, and one should taste every dish on the eve of Shabbat (the Writings).”

connections.hePhrase: וְכַנּוֹדָע מִטַּעַם הַזֹּהַר מִשְׁפָּטִים (צה עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת ח, ט), וְעַל זֶה מְבַקְּשִׁין: "חַלְּצֵנִי ה' מֵאָדָם רָע" (תְּהִלִּים קמ, ב).
connections.quote: ‘This is a mystery higher than all the others. On the pillar that stands for weighing, within the blowing air, there is one balance on this side and another balance on that side. On this side are just scales, and on that side are deceitful scales. This balance is never at rest. Souls rise and descend, enter and return, and there are souls held captive when one man rules over another, as it is written: ‘At a time when one man ruled over another to his own harm’—to his own harm indeed.’

connections.hePhrase: וְכַנּוֹדָע מִטַּעַם הַזֹּהַר מִשְׁפָּטִים (צה עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת ח, ט), וְעַל זֶה מְבַקְּשִׁין: "חַלְּצֵנִי ה' מֵאָדָם רָע" (תְּהִלִּים קמ, ב).
connections.quote: “All this I saw, setting my heart to every deed done under the sun: a time when one person rules over another, to his harm.”
connections.context: The pronoun in “to his harm” allows the homiletic reading cited from the Zohar: domination ultimately harms the dominator. Rav Tzadok uses that reversal to explain deliverance from the “evil man.”

connections.hePhrase: וְכַנּוֹדָע מִטַּעַם הַזֹּהַר מִשְׁפָּטִים (צה עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "עֵת אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַט הָאָדָם בְּאָדָם לְרַע לוֹ" (קֹהֶלֶת ח, ט), וְעַל זֶה מְבַקְּשִׁין: "חַלְּצֵנִי ה' מֵאָדָם רָע" (תְּהִלִּים קמ, ב).
connections.quote: ‘Rescue me, Hashem, from an evil person; guard me from a violent man.’

connections.hePhrase: וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו.): וְקָיְימֵי עֲלַן וְכוּלֵי, כָּל חַד מִינַּן אַלְפָּא מִשְּׂמָאלֵיהּ וְרִבְבָתָא מִימִינֵיהּ.
connections.quote: ‘Rav Huna said: Each and every one of us has a thousand [demons] on his left and ten thousand on his right.’

connections.hePhrase: וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ו.): וְקָיְימֵי עֲלַן וְכוּלֵי, כָּל חַד מִינַּן אַלְפָּא מִשְּׂמָאלֵיהּ וְרִבְבָתָא מִימִינֵיהּ.
connections.quote: “The land too will perceive the depth and have eyes to recognize who truly serves Hashem. No soul of Israel will consequently be lost, for in the depth of Israel's heart they are full of willingness and service. Although great concealment is sometimes found within Israel, it is in the garment; in the depth of the heart they are pure. The land will therefore understand that even when impurity and concealment appear within Israel, these concern the garment, while inwardly they are connected with the light of His will. This is ‘the land will not vomit you out’: no individual soul of Israel will be lost.”
connections.explanation: Tiferet Yosef describes the land acquiring eyes to recognize inward service rather than judging by the garment alone. This clarifies the distinction behind ‘rescue me from an evil man’: the obstructing configuration of thoughts is real, but it does not exhaust the soul's root. The enduring inward connection supplies the possibility of release; it does not make the work of removing the garment unnecessary.
connections.headline: An enclosing garment does not exhaust the soul's identity

connections.hePhrase: "מִימִינוֹ" – פֵּירוּשׁ: תַּאֲווֹת וְחֶמְדוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, זֶהוּ "רִבְבוֹת" לְשׁוֹן רִבּוּי, שֶׁהוּא בְּתוֹקֶף עָצוּם, כִּי זֶהוּ עִיקַּר הַיֵּצֶר הָרָע שֶׁבְּלֵב בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בְּטַעַם דִּמְצוֹרָע מִשְׁתַּלֵּחַ חוּץ לַמַּחֲנֶה יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלֹא הַזָּב.
connections.displayRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Numbers, Nasso 4
connections.linkedRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Numbers, Nasso 4
