connections.quote: “He covers His palms with light and commands it concerning the one it is to strike.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל לְשׁוֹן "מַפְגִּיעַ בִּתְפִלּוֹת", וּ"מַפְגִּיעַ אֵין בְּיָדֵינוּ", וּבְפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּתַעֲנִית (ח.) עַל פָּסוּק "וַיְצַו עָלָיו כִּמְפַגִּיעַ" (אִיּוֹב לו, לב), דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּמוֹ פָּגַע, שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב וְלָלֶכֶת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן רַק שֶׁיַּעֲנֵהוּ, וַהֲרֵי זֶה כְּאוֹחֵז בִּבְגָדוֹ וְאוֹמֵר: אֵינִי מַנִּיחֲךָ.
connections.quote: “If he prayed quietly and was not answered, what is his remedy? Let him go to a pious person of the generation, who will increase prayer on his behalf, as it says, “He commands it through entreaty.” And entreaty means prayer.”
connections.context: The Gemara reads bemafgia as prayer or entreaty. Rav Tzadok develops the related sense of persistent encounter, as though the petitioner holds on and refuses to depart without an answer. This is the interpretive connection that an ordinary translation of Job’s lightning imagery does not reveal.

connections.quote: “He seized him by the corner of his cloak. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said to him: I swear that I will not come.”
connections.context: The Angel of Death takes hold of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s cloak to bring him out of the Garden of Eden, and he swears that he will not go: an image of holding fast and refusing to be moved.

connections.hePhrase: וְהוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל לְשׁוֹן "מַפְגִּיעַ בִּתְפִלּוֹת", וּ"מַפְגִּיעַ אֵין בְּיָדֵינוּ", וּבְפֶרֶק קַמָּא דְּתַעֲנִית (ח.) עַל פָּסוּק "וַיְצַו עָלָיו כִּמְפַגִּיעַ" (אִיּוֹב לו, לב), דִּרְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר כְּמוֹ פָּגַע, שֶׁאֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לָשׁוּב וְלָלֶכֶת מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּשׁוּם אֹפֶן רַק שֶׁיַּעֲנֵהוּ, וַהֲרֵי זֶה כְּאוֹחֵז בִּבְגָדוֹ וְאוֹמֵר: אֵינִי מַנִּיחֲךָ.
connections.quote: “The prayer of Jacob our father, of blessed memory, is described as an encounter: it is forceful prayer, in the manner of the teaching in Taanit 23a and Pesikta Rabbati, chapter 3, that a righteous person decrees and the Holy One, blessed be He, fulfills. This is called “interceding”; see Taanit 7b. It is alluded to in Shabbat 77b: the lion’s fear of the mafgi’a. Concerning this we say, “For our strength is exhausted, and there is no intercessor on our behalf”—one who comes with the force and strength of our hand, as in “You shall decree a matter, and it shall be established for you.” This is called voice, as it is written, “The voice is the voice of Jacob,” and, “Hear, O Lord, the voice of Judah.” These are the voices at the giving of the Torah, heard from within the fire. Isaac is the fire that gives birth to the voice, and Jacob is the voice itself; his bed is complete, for he encompasses the congregation of Israel, who are the very substance of Torah: “Truth to Jacob,” attached to the living God. He lives forever, as Taanit 5b says that he did not die, for he ate from the tree of life. The tree of life is none other than Torah, as Tanna Devei Eliyahu Rabbah, chapter 1, says, from “It is a tree of life,” and he is the very substance of Torah.”

connections.hePhrase: [רכג] דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הִיא דּוּגְמַת חֶרֶב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (ה.): בִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע כְּאִלּוּ אוֹחֵז חֶרֶב שֶׁל שְׁתֵּי פִּיּוֹת.
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Yitzchak said: Anyone who recites Shema upon his bed is as though he holds a double-edged sword in his hand, as it says: ‘The praises of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hand.’ How does this imply it? Mar Zutra said—and some say Rav Ashi: From the beginning of the passage, where it is written: ‘Let the pious rejoice in glory; let them sing upon their beds.’ Immediately afterward it is written: ‘The praises of God are in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hand.’’

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (כְּתוּבּוֹת עז:): רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִיכָּרֵךְ בְּבַעֲלֵי רָאָתָן וְעָסֵיק בַּתּוֹרָה, אָמַר וְכוּלֵי.
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Yochanan would proclaim: ‘Beware of the flies of those suffering from ra’atan.’ Rabbi Zeira would not sit downwind of them. Rabbi Elazar would not enter their tent. Rabbi Ammi and Rabbi Assi would not eat eggs from that alley. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi would draw close to them and occupy himself with Torah. He said: ‘A loving doe and a graceful gazelle’—if Torah bestows grace on those who study it, does it not protect them?’

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי, דְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדוּשַׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאֲוִיר אֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים נִפְלָט מִתּוֹכוֹ לְגַמְרֵי מִכָּל צַד עַל יְדֵי הַחֶרֶב דִּשְׁתֵּי פִּיּוֹת, וְנִכְנָס אֲוִיר קָדוֹשׁ דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ אֲוִיר אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלָכֵן מַחְכִּים, כְּמִדַּת הַתּוֹרָה מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי.
connections.quote: “The Torah of Hashem is perfect, restoring the soul; the testimony of Hashem is sure, making wise the simple.”

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי, דְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדוּשַׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאֲוִיר אֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים נִפְלָט מִתּוֹכוֹ לְגַמְרֵי מִכָּל צַד עַל יְדֵי הַחֶרֶב דִּשְׁתֵּי פִּיּוֹת, וְנִכְנָס אֲוִיר קָדוֹשׁ דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ אֲוִיר אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלָכֵן מַחְכִּים, כְּמִדַּת הַתּוֹרָה מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי.

connections.quote: ““Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen.” Jacob our father was afraid to go outside the Land, as the Gemara, Ketubot 110b, says: Anyone who dwells in the Land of Israel is like one who has a God, and so forth. God told him: Wherever you are is holy with the holiness of the Land of Israel. This explains “Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen”: even in the land of Egypt he was close to God, and it was a sanctified place, for Goshen is an expression of drawing near.”

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי, דְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת שֶׁל הֲלָכָה קָדוֹשׁ בִּקְדוּשַׁת אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁאֲוִיר אֶרֶץ הָעַמִּים נִפְלָט מִתּוֹכוֹ לְגַמְרֵי מִכָּל צַד עַל יְדֵי הַחֶרֶב דִּשְׁתֵּי פִּיּוֹת, וְנִכְנָס אֲוִיר קָדוֹשׁ דְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, שֶׁזֶּהוּ אֲוִיר אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּלָכֵן מַחְכִּים, כְּמִדַּת הַתּוֹרָה מַחְכִּימַת פֶּתִי.
connections.quote: “Torah scholars who labor in Torah are called Shabbatot, as stated in Zohar III, 29b and 124b. Through Torah’s power they can continually attain a foretaste of the World to Come, like Shabbatot, and “they shall inherit the Land forever”: they merit eating in this world from the Land of Israel’s holiness. This is the connection of covenant and Torah to the blessing for the Land.”
connections.explanation: Tu BiShvat explains how the power of Torah allows a talmid chacham to receive a foretaste associated with Shabbat and the Land even within this world. This develops the present siman’s description of the four amos of halakhah as a place whose atmosphere is changed by Torah. The claim concerns an enacted holiness of learning, not simply a geographical comparison: the person enters the air of Torah by turning toward its words.
connections.headline: Torah makes a foretaste of sacred place available within present life

connections.hePhrase: רַק צָרִיךְ לְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ לְהִתְרַחֵק מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת, וְאָז עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה יוּכַל לִפְעוֹל לְהַכְנִיס בְּעֹמֶק הַלֵּב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת וּלְהָרוֹג הָרָע מִמֶּרְחָק, כְּעִנְיַן "חֵץ שָׁחוּט לְשׁוֹנָם" (יִרְמְיָה ט, ז), שֶׁהַלָּשׁוֹן דּוּגְמַת הַחֵץ לַהֲרוֹג מֵרָחוֹק, וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַתְּפִלָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (סוֹף תִּיקּוּן יג וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת) דְּזָרֵיק בֵּיהּ גִּירָא בָּתַר גִּירָא.
connections.quote: ‘Their tongue is a sharpened arrow; it speaks deceit. With his mouth a person speaks peace to his fellow, but within himself he sets an ambush for him.’

connections.hePhrase: רַק צָרִיךְ לְכַוֵּין אֶת לִבּוֹ לְהִתְרַחֵק מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת, וְאָז עַל יְדֵי תְּפִלָּה יוּכַל לִפְעוֹל לְהַכְנִיס בְּעֹמֶק הַלֵּב מַחֲשָׁבוֹת קְדוֹשׁוֹת וּלְהָרוֹג הָרָע מִמֶּרְחָק, כְּעִנְיַן "חֵץ שָׁחוּט לְשׁוֹנָם" (יִרְמְיָה ט, ז), שֶׁהַלָּשׁוֹן דּוּגְמַת הַחֵץ לַהֲרוֹג מֵרָחוֹק, וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי הַתְּפִלָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (סוֹף תִּיקּוּן יג וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת) דְּזָרֵיק בֵּיהּ גִּירָא בָּתַר גִּירָא.
connections.quote: “The bow is the tongue of the mouth; the bow’s nut is the mouth; the scarlet thread is the lip, the cord of the bow, through which the righteous one shoots arrows—the utterances of prayer—toward the serpent.”
connections.context: The image makes the words of prayer into arrows directed against the serpent. It explains Rav Tzadok’s claim that prayer can strike at evil from a distance and implant holy thoughts deep in the heart.

connections.hePhrase: וְתַרְגּוּם "אֲשֶׁר לָקַחְתִּי מִיַּד הָאֱמֹרִי בְּחַרְבִּי וּבְקַשְׁתִּי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית מח, כב) – בִּצְלוֹתִי וּבְבָעוּתִי.
connections.quote: “I have given you one portion more than your brothers, which I took from the hand of the Amorite by my prayer and my supplication.”
connections.context: Onkelos renders “my sword and my bow” as “my prayer and my supplication.” Rav Tzadok uses these two Aramaic terms to distinguish arranging praise from asking for one’s needs. The note therefore quotes the Targum itself.

connections.hePhrase: וְתַרְגּוּם "אֲשֶׁר לָקַחְתִּי מִיַּד הָאֱמֹרִי בְּחַרְבִּי וּבְקַשְׁתִּי" (בְּרֵאשִׁית מח, כב) – בִּצְלוֹתִי וּבְבָעוּתִי.
connections.displayRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 31:7
connections.canonicalRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 31:7
connections.quote: “His descendants followed him in recognizing that Hashem's life is found even in all this world's garments, and brought Heaven's honor into all worldly affairs. As the Zohar says (Vayishlach 173b), ‘Yaakov is the completion of the forebears; he grasps all sides, and called his name Israel…’ It is written of him (Genesis 48:22), ‘Which I took from the Emorite with my sword and bow.’ But, as the Sages explained, is it not written (Psalms 44:7), ‘I do not trust in my bow, and my sword will not save me’? He meant his power of prayer, as Bava Batra 123a explains, cited by Rashi, and as Onkelos translates, ‘With my prayer and supplication.’ He possessed the inward aspect of everything, including sword and bow, for the principal aspect of each thing is its inwardness (as explained in Vayechi, section 51).”
connections.explanation: Beit Yaakov raises the apparent contradiction between Yaakov's sword and bow and the psalm's denial of trust in weapons. It resolves this through their inward force, prayer and supplication. This clarifies the register in which the siman develops its more detailed distinction between nearby and distant spiritual work.
connections.headline: The inward power of the sword and bow

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ: "תְּפִלָּה" הַיְינוּ סִדּוּר שְׁבָחָיו שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, וּ"בַקָּשָׁה" הוּא בַּקָּשַׁת צְרָכָיו, כִּמְפוֹרָשׁ בִּבְרָכוֹת (לא.): רִנָּה זוֹ תְּפִלָּה וְכוּלֵי.
connections.quote: “Might a person ask for his needs and then pray? This has already been explained by Solomon, as it is said: ‘To listen to the song and to the prayer.’ ‘Song’—rinnah—is prayer; ‘prayer’—tefillah—is a request. One does not recite a request after Emet Veyatziv. After the prayer, however, one may recite even a confession like the order recited on Yom Kippur.”

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "רִנָּה", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז) עַל פָּסוּק "קוּמִי רֹנִּי בַלַּיְלָה" (אֵיכָה ב, יט) – אֵין רִנָּה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, כִּי הוּא סִדּוּר שְׁבָחָיו, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁילְהֵי הוֹרָיוֹת (יג:) עַל פָּסוּק "מִי יְמַלֵּל גְּבוּרוֹת ה' יַשְׁמִיעַ כָּל תְּהִלָּתוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קו, ב) – עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
connections.quote: ‘Rise, cry out in the night, at the beginning of the watches. Pour out your heart like water before the Lord. Lift your palms toward Him for the lives of your little children, who faint from hunger at the head of every street.’

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "רִנָּה", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז) עַל פָּסוּק "קוּמִי רֹנִּי בַלַּיְלָה" (אֵיכָה ב, יט) – אֵין רִנָּה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, כִּי הוּא סִדּוּר שְׁבָחָיו, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁילְהֵי הוֹרָיוֹת (יג:) עַל פָּסוּק "מִי יְמַלֵּל גְּבוּרוֹת ה' יַשְׁמִיעַ כָּל תְּהִלָּתוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קו, ב) – עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
connections.quote: “Nevertheless, Rabbi Yochanan acknowledged that the song of Torah is only at night, as it says, “Arise, sing at night”; and similarly, “She rises while it is still night.””
connections.context: The Midrash explicitly calls Torah study rinah, song, reading Lamentations 2:19 in that sense. Rav Tzadok uses the designation to connect Torah with arranging Hashem’s praise. The larger discussion addresses study by day and by night; this excerpt supplies the particular term he cites.

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "רִנָּה", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז) עַל פָּסוּק "קוּמִי רֹנִּי בַלַּיְלָה" (אֵיכָה ב, יט) – אֵין רִנָּה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, כִּי הוּא סִדּוּר שְׁבָחָיו, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁילְהֵי הוֹרָיוֹת (יג:) עַל פָּסוּק "מִי יְמַלֵּל גְּבוּרוֹת ה' יַשְׁמִיעַ כָּל תְּהִלָּתוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קו, ב) – עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
connections.quote: ““Who can recount Hashem’s mighty deeds, make all His praise heard?” For whom is it fitting to recount Hashem’s mighty deeds? For one who can make all His praises heard.”
connections.context: Rabbi Meir invokes this verse in the discussion of mastery of Torah, proposing to test Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel in Uktzin. Rav Tzadok draws from that application the identification of Torah with recounting divine praise.

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִקְרָא "רִנָּה", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שְׁמוֹת רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז) עַל פָּסוּק "קוּמִי רֹנִּי בַלַּיְלָה" (אֵיכָה ב, יט) – אֵין רִנָּה שֶׁל תּוֹרָה וְכוּלֵי, כִּי הוּא סִדּוּר שְׁבָחָיו, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שִׁילְהֵי הוֹרָיוֹת (יג:) עַל פָּסוּק "מִי יְמַלֵּל גְּבוּרוֹת ה' יַשְׁמִיעַ כָּל תְּהִלָּתוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קו, ב) – עַל דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
connections.quote: ‘Who can recount the mighty deeds of Hashem, make all His praise heard?’

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן גַּם קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע נִקְרָא "צְלוֹתָא" כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתְבוּ תּוֹסָפוֹת שַׁבָּת (יא. דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל "כְּגוֹן"), כִּי סִדּוּר שְׁבָחָיו הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה, וְזֶהוּ חֶרֶב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
connections.quote: ““Such as Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai and his companions”: As for the statement later, on 33b, that when the time of prayer arrived he dressed, covered himself, and prayed—that “prayed” means reciting Shema.”
connections.context: Tosafot explicitly explains an occurrence of “prayed” as Shema. This is the linguistic support for Rav Tzadok’s statement that Shema too can be called tzelota.

connections.hePhrase: וְלִהְיוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי אָז בָּאָרֶץ שֶׁהוּא הַגָּרוּעַ מִכָּל הָאֻמּוֹת, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תּוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים אַחֲרֵי מוֹת פָּרָשָׁה ט), וּשְׁכֶם גָּרוּעַ מִכָּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קב.) דְּהוּא מָקוֹם מוּכָן לְפֻרְעָנוּת;
connections.quote: “And Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, to the terebinth of Moreh; and the Canaanite was then in the land.”

connections.hePhrase: וְלִהְיוֹת הַכְּנַעֲנִי אָז בָּאָרֶץ שֶׁהוּא הַגָּרוּעַ מִכָּל הָאֻמּוֹת, כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (תּוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים אַחֲרֵי מוֹת פָּרָשָׁה ט), וּשְׁכֶם גָּרוּעַ מִכָּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּפֶרֶק חֵלֶק (סַנְהֶדְרִין קב.) דְּהוּא מָקוֹם מוּכָן לְפֻרְעָנוּת;
connections.heRef: ספרא, אחרי מות, פרשה ח ד׳
connections.quote: “From where do we learn that no nation among the nations made its deeds more abominable than the Canaanites? Scripture says, “According to the conduct of the land of Canaan … you shall not act.” From where do we learn that the last generation made its deeds more abominable than all the others? Scripture says, “According to the conduct of the land of Canaan … you shall not act.” From where do we learn that the place where Israel came and conquered made its deeds more abominable than all the others? Scripture says, “To which I am bringing you.” From where do we learn that Israel’s coming occasioned all these deeds for them? Scripture says, “To which I am bringing you, you shall not act.””

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן יַעֲקֹב נִתְחַזֵּק נֶגֶד אוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם בְּיִחוּד, וְשָׁם מִשְׁכַּן הַחִוִּי – חִוְיָא, שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנָּחָשׁ.
connections.quote: “And Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her; and he took her, and lay with her, and afflicted her.”

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמַר "מִיַּד הָאֱמֹרִי" וְלֹא הַחִוִּי, הוּא כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּסֵפֶר מַעֲשֵׂה ה' כִּי אֱמוּנָתָם הָיְתָה אֱמוּנַת הָאֱמֹרִי, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם;
connections.quote: “Concerning the mention of the Amorite rather than the other nations, Ramban wrote that it was the strongest among them. But this is not so, for the Land of Israel is always named after Canaan: “The land of Canaan, the portion of your inheritance,” and the Canaanite was the principal one. It seems possible to me, however, that the Amorite was the first to begin that evil belief, and the seven nations were drawn after that belief. Therefore it says “the iniquity of the Amorite,” for it began that iniquity. Likewise, Joshua says, “If it is evil in your eyes to serve the Lord, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: whether the gods your fathers served beyond the river, or the gods of the Amorite in whose land you dwell,” and so forth. They were already dwelling in the land of the seven nations, yet he mentioned only the Amorite. This indicates that the worship of all seven nations was derived from the Amorite.”

connections.hePhrase: וְיַצִּיבָא מִילְּתָא מִלְּשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בְּכָל מָקוֹם "דַּרְכֵי הָאֱמֹרִי" עַל חֻקֵּי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁלָּהֶם.
connections.quote: “One may go out with a locust egg, a fox’s tooth, or a nail from the crucified, for healing; these are the words of Rabbi Meir. The Sages forbid it even on weekdays, because of the ways of the Amorite.”

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם נִתְחַזֵּק נֶגֶד הָאֱמֹרִי, שֶׁהוּא תֹּקֶף כֹּחַ אֱלֹהוּתָם הַמִּתְגַּבֵּר בַּאֲוִירָם לְהַכְנִיס הִרְהוּרִים וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת בַּלֵּב, שֶׁעַל זֶה טִהֵר בְּנֵי בֵיתוֹ אַחַר כָּךְ.
connections.quote: “Then Jacob said to his household and to all who were with him: Put away the foreign gods that are among you, and purify yourselves, and change your garments.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהַנִּצּוּחַ הַזֶּה הוּא "בִּצְלוֹתִי" מִקּוֹדֶם בַּחֶרֶב לַהֲרוֹג סְבִיבוֹתָיו, דִּלְעוֹלָם יְסַדֵּר שִׁבְחוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם וְאַחַר כָּךְ יִתְפַּלֵּל (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת לב.), דְּלוּלֵי כֵן אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִיכָּנֵס לִתְפִלָּה דְּבַקָּשָׁה כְּלָל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Simlai expounded: A person should always arrange the praise of the Holy One, blessed be He, and afterward pray. From where is this derived? From Moses: “I pleaded with Hashem at that time”; then, “Hashem God, You have begun to show Your servant Your greatness and Your mighty hand, for what power in heaven or earth can do Your deeds and Your mighty acts?” After that it is written, “Let me cross over and see the good land.””
connections.context: The source establishes the sequence of praise before petition, which Rav Tzadok associates with sword before bow.

connections.hePhrase: וּקְרָא זֶה אָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהוּא דַּרְגָּא דִּתְפִלָּה, כְּטַעַם "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" (שָׁם, ד), שֶׁלָּזֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי רִבּוּי הַתְּפִלּוֹת וְהַבַּקָּשׁוֹת לְסַיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב:): אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: A person’s inclination grows stronger against him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says, “The wicked watches for the righteous and seeks to kill him.” Without the Holy One, blessed be He, helping him, he could not overcome it, as it says, “Hashem will not leave him in its hand, nor condemn him when he is judged.””
connections.context: The statement concerns the divine help needed to withstand the inclination. Rav Tzadok cites it to explain repeated prayer for heavenly assistance; the marker belongs at that citation.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ פָּרָשָׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה דִּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, הֲגַם דִּבְפָרָשָׁה שְׁנִיָּה אַחַר כָּךְ נֶאֱמַר: "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ" (דְּבָרִים יא, יד), שֶׁלָּמְדוּ מִזֶּה בִּבְרָכוֹת (לה:): הַנְהֵג בָּהֶן מִנְהַג דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ;
connections.quote: ‘I will give rain for your land at its proper time, the early rain and the late rain, and you will gather your grain, your wine, and your oil.’

connections.hePhrase: וּלְכָךְ לֹא נֶאֱמַר שָׁם "בְּכָל מְאֹדְךָ", שֶׁפֵּירוּשׁוֹ מָמוֹנְךָ – לְהַפְקִיר הַכֹּל, שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ לָרַבִּים דִּצְרִיכִים לִנְהוֹג בְּמִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וּלְהַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל מָמוֹנָם גַּם כֵּן לִהְיוֹת בַּמֶּה לְהִתְפַּרְנֵס וְקִיּוּם חַיּוּתָם.
connections.quote: “And you shall love Hashem your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might (me’odekha).”

connections.hePhrase: וּלְכָךְ לֹא נֶאֱמַר שָׁם "בְּכָל מְאֹדְךָ", שֶׁפֵּירוּשׁוֹ מָמוֹנְךָ – לְהַפְקִיר הַכֹּל, שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ לָרַבִּים דִּצְרִיכִים לִנְהוֹג בְּמִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ וּלְהַשְׁגִּיחַ עַל מָמוֹנָם גַּם כֵּן לִהְיוֹת בַּמֶּה לְהִתְפַּרְנֵס וְקִיּוּם חַיּוּתָם.
connections.quote: “‘With all your might’—with all your money.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם וְעוֹל תּוֹרָה, כְּאוֹתוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּעֵירוּבִין (כב.): מִי שְׁלִימוּ קוֹרְמֵי, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת סג.): אֵין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִתְקַיְּימִין אֶלָּא בְּמִי שֶׁמֵּמִית וְכוּלֵי, וּבְמִי שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה אַכְזָרִי וְכוּלֵי (עֵירוּבִין שָׁם).
connections.quote: ‘Rava said: In one who makes himself as cruel as a raven toward his children and his household. Thus Rav Adda bar Mattana was going to the study hall. His wife said to him: ‘What am I to do with your children?’ He answered: ‘Have the reeds in the marsh run out?’’

connections.hePhrase: וְכָל אֶחָד צָרִיךְ גַּם כֵּן לוֹמַר פָּרָשָׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה גַּם כֵּן, שֶׁתְּחִלַּת קַבָּלָתוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם עוֹל מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת בְּעִנְיָן זֶה, גַּם לִהְיוֹת מוּפְקָר אִם יִהְיֶה רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ כָּךְ.
connections.quote: “But for someone unable to withstand this trial, Rava himself said, “In the days of Nisan and the days of Tishrei, do not appear before me ….” Although they were amoraim and sages, his students, since he knew that a lack of food would distract them, he instructed them to attend to their livelihood in Nisan and Tishrei. This is the subject of the passage, “If you indeed listen to My commandments … you shall gather your grain …”: they perform God’s commandments, resting on Shabbat and in the sabbatical year as He commanded. But they do not perform the Omnipresent’s will of being free solely for the toil of Torah. This is “their work is performed by themselves.” One who merits to be a vessel for Torah’s toil, free solely for it according to the Omnipresent’s will, has his work performed by others. Not everyone merits this. Thus the Talmud says: “Many acted … according to Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai and did not succeed.””
connections.explanation: Lech Lecha gives a practical case of the present siman’s distinction between total willingness to surrender and the form of service suited to one’s actual vessel. Rava directed his talmidim to work in the relevant seasons because he knew that deprivation would disturb their learning. This is why reciting both paragraphs of Shema matters: unreserved allegiance to Hashem must also be carried into the sustaining conduct that permits Torah and mitzvot to endure in embodied life.
connections.headline: Rava’s instruction to earn a livelihood makes the limits of imitation concrete

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן אֲפִילּוּ אוֹתָם הַיְחִידִים צְרִיכִים גַּם כֵּן שֶׁיֹּאמְרוּ פָּרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ", כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ לְרַשְׁבִּ"י בְּשַׁבָּת (לג:) שֶׁיַּחֲזוֹר לַמְּעָרָה, כִּי אִי אֶפְשָׁר לִהְיוֹת כֵּן רַק בַּמְּעָרָה וְחוּץ לָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
connections.quote: see note 1935 (Vol. I).

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא רוֹצֶה בְּיִשּׁוּב הָעוֹלָם, וְ"לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ" (יְשַׁעְיָה מה, יח).
connections.quote: see note 2620.

connections.hePhrase: רַק בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה שֶׁהוּא בִּכְלִי הַגּוּף הַמַּגְדִּיר, אָמְרוּ (תַּעֲנִית כב:): נְשָׁמָה שֶׁנָּתַתִּי בְּךָ הַחֲיֶיהָ, וְלֹא יַפְקִיר לְגַמְרֵי לָצֵאת מִגְּבוּל כְּלִי הַגּוּף;
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Yosei says: An individual may not afflict himself by fasting, lest he come to need other people and they show him no mercy. Rav Yehuda said in Rav’s name: What is Rabbi Yosei’s reason? For it is written: ‘The human being became a living soul’—keep alive the soul that I have placed within you.’

connections.hePhrase: וְיָדוּעַ מֵהָאֲרִ"י זַ"ל דִּבְפָרָשָׁה רִאשׁוֹנָה יֵשׁ שֵׁם מַ"ב, וּבְפָרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ" שֵׁם עַ"ב.

connections.quote: “He should intend that in the paragraph “Hear, O Israel” there are forty-two words, corresponding to the forty-two-letter Name, Avgitatz, and so forth. He should intend that he makes his head a chariot for that forty-two-letter Name, and that his head clothes itself in it to ascend above through it, as stated. In the paragraph “And it shall be, if you surely listen,” which has seventy-two words until the word “You shall place,” he should direct his intention toward the seventy-two-letter Name emerging from the verses beginning “And he journeyed,” “And he came,” and “And he stretched out.” He should make his arms and his body down to his belly a chariot for this Name, and intend that they clothe themselves in it, as stated.”

connections.hePhrase: וְנוֹדַע דְּשֵׁם מַ"ב הוּא לָעוֹלִים בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה שֶׁעוֹלִים בּוֹ, וְעָלָיו יִסַּד רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנֶה תְּפִלַּת "אָנָא בְּכֹחַ וְכוּלֵי", וְהַיּוֹרְדִים יוֹרְדִים בְּשֵׁם עַ"ב וְאֵין צָרִיךְ טָהֳרָה כָּל כָּךְ, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שֵׁם מַ"ב צָרִיךְ טָהֳרָה גְּדוֹלָה כִּי הוּא מִצַּד הַגְּבוּרָה כַּנּוֹדָע.
connections.quote: “The reason is that there is no ascent in the worlds except through the forty-two-letter Name. This forty-two-letter Name is what raises all the ascents in all the worlds, because it ascends and does not descend, as stated in the portion Terumah, 132b.”

connections.hePhrase: וְנוֹדַע דְּשֵׁם מַ"ב הוּא לָעוֹלִים בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה שֶׁעוֹלִים בּוֹ, וְעָלָיו יִסַּד רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנֶה תְּפִלַּת "אָנָא בְּכֹחַ וְכוּלֵי", וְהַיּוֹרְדִים יוֹרְדִים בְּשֵׁם עַ"ב וְאֵין צָרִיךְ טָהֳרָה כָּל כָּךְ, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן שֵׁם מַ"ב צָרִיךְ טָהֳרָה גְּדוֹלָה כִּי הוּא מִצַּד הַגְּבוּרָה כַּנּוֹדָע.
connections.quote: “When she is closed, she is called fear: throughout the six weekdays she is closed and guarded by the ten utterances and the thirty-two occurrences of “Elohim,” which are the forty-two letters of Gevurah, where Binah is found. On Shabbat, “The heavens were completed”: “vayekhullu” has the numerical value of “chesed,” the kindness of the right, which encompasses seventy-two names, where Chokhmah is found, as we said: One who wishes to become wise should turn south. Fear applies on the six weekdays: “Each person shall fear his mother and father.” Love applies on Shabbat: “Honor your father and your mother.” When she opens toward her husband, she is called love. From fear and love were given the positive and negative commandments.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהַיְינוּ שְׁתֵּי תְּפִלּוֹת דְּרַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא בֶּן הַקָּנֶה בִּכְנִיסָתוֹ לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ וּבִיצִיאָתוֹ (בְּרָכוֹת כח:)
connections.quote: ‘Mishnah: Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKanah would offer a short prayer upon entering the study hall and upon leaving it. They asked him: ‘What is the occasion for this prayer?’ He answered: ‘When I enter, I pray that no mishap will come about through me. When I leave, I give thanks for my portion.’’

connections.hePhrase: וּמֵאַחַר שֶׁרוֹצֶה לָצֵאת מִמַּדְרֵגָה גּוּפָנִית, צָרִיךְ לִהְיוֹת כְּמַלְאָכִים שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בָּהֶם: עוֹשִׂים בְּאֵימָה וּבְיִרְאָה וְכוּלֵי, בִּקְדוּשָּׁה וּבְטָהֳרָה וְכוּלֵי.

connections.quote: “All are beloved, all are pure, all are mighty, and all perform with dread and awe the will of their Maker; and all open their mouths in holiness and purity, in song and melody.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ פָּרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ": "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ", שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם לה:) תְּחִלָּה שֶׁהִיא לְעוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם וְדֶרֶךְ בְּרָכָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר דְּהַיְינוּ בְּאֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִקְשׁוּ זֶה הַתּוֹסָפוֹת;
connections.quote: “Rabbi Chanina bar Pappa raised a contradiction: It is written, “I shall take back My grain in its season,” and it is written, “You shall gather your grain.” There is no difficulty: Here, when Israel do the will of the Omnipresent; there, when Israel do not do the will of the Omnipresent.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ פָּרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ": "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ", שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם לה:) תְּחִלָּה שֶׁהִיא לְעוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם וְדֶרֶךְ בְּרָכָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר דְּהַיְינוּ בְּאֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִקְשׁוּ זֶה הַתּוֹסָפוֹת;
connections.quote: “Rather, when Israel do the will of the Omnipresent, their work is done by others, as it says, “Strangers shall stand and tend your flocks.” When Israel do not do the will of the Omnipresent, they perform their work themselves, as it says, “You shall gather your grain.””

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ פָּרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ": "וְאָסַפְתָּ דְגָנֶךָ", שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם לה:) תְּחִלָּה שֶׁהִיא לְעוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם וְדֶרֶךְ בְּרָכָה, וְאַחַר כָּךְ אָמַר דְּהַיְינוּ בְּאֵין עוֹשִׂין רְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁל מָקוֹם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁהִקְשׁוּ זֶה הַתּוֹסָפוֹת;
connections.quote: ““Here, when Israel do the will of the Omnipresent, as it says, ‘You shall gather your grain’”: But later this is applied to a time when Israel do not do His will! It may be answered that they certainly do His will, but do not do it to the fullest extent, for they are not completely righteous. Alternatively, this statement disagrees with the later one, which explains the distinction between doing His will and not doing it; the categories used here are relative to one another.”
connections.context: The two applications of “you shall gather your grain” are the very difficulty Rav Tzadok discusses. Tosafot’s first answer distinguishes ordinary obedience from complete righteousness; its second treats the statements as differing interpretations. Rav Tzadok develops his own explanation through the relation between Torah scholars and those who sustain them.

connections.hePhrase: וְחִבּוּר כָּל הָאִילָן הוּא עַלְיָא וְאִתְכַּלְיָא, וְאַלְמָלֵא עַלְיָא וְכוּלֵי (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֻלִּין צב.),
connections.quote: “Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: This nation is compared to a vine. Its branches are the householders; its clusters are the Torah scholars; its leaves are the unlearned; its tendrils are the empty ones of Israel. This is what they sent from there: Let the clusters pray for the leaves, for without the leaves the clusters could not survive.”
connections.context: The final sentence is essential: scholars depend on the surrounding community as grapes depend on leaves. Rav Tzadok uses the whole vine to explain why Torah and the life of ordinary work must be joined.

connections.hePhrase: וְהֵם הָאוֹסְפִים – פֵּירוּשׁ תּוֹמְכֵי אוֹרַיְיתָא וּמַחֲזִיקִים בְּיָדָם לִהְיוֹת הַשֶּׁפַע יוֹרֵד לָרָאוּי לְקַבֵּל, וּ"בְצֵל הַחָכְמָה בְּצֵל הַכָּסֶף" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, יב) כּוּלָּא חַד.
connections.quote: ‘For one who is in the shelter of wisdom is in the shelter of money; yet the advantage of knowledge is that wisdom gives life to those who possess it.’

connections.hePhrase: וּכְשֶׁיּוֹצֵא מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמִתְחַבֵּר לַצִּבּוּר, וּבָהֶם גַּם עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ, אִם אָז גַּם כֵּן דָּבוּק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה, זֶהוּ מַאן דְּעָיֵיל וְנָפֵיק שֶׁשִּׁבְּחוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, קמא סוֹף עַמּוּד א), וְלֹא דְּעָיֵיל וְלָא נָפֵיק;
connections.quote: “It was taught: Rabbi Shimon said, “All these configurations and all these matters I wish to reveal to their masters, who have been weighed in the balance—not to those who entered and did not emerge, but to those who entered and emerged. For anyone who enters and does not emerge would have been better off not being created.””

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁבְּשָׁעָה שֶׁעוֹסֵק בְּדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה וַדַּאי הוּא דָּבוּק בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, רַק אִם נִקְבַּע בַּלֵּב כָּל כָּךְ עַד שֶׁגַּם בִּיצִיאָתוֹ לְהַנְהִיג מִדַּת דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ יִהְיֶה שׁוֹמֵעַ בְּקוֹל ה' וּמִצְווֹתָיו וְלֹא יָזוּז – זֶה מִדַּת רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁיָּצָא בְּשָׁלוֹם, וְעַל זֶה נוֹתֵן הוֹדָאָה עַל חֶלְקוֹ.
connections.heRef: חידושי אגדות על חגיגה י״ד ב:ט׳
connections.quote: ““Rabbi Akiva ascended in peace and descended in peace; of him Scripture says, ‘Draw me after You,’” and so forth: Rabbi Akiva was complete in every kind of perfection. When he reached the boundary beyond which human intellect cannot go, he stopped and did not break through to ascend to God. Therefore it says of him, “Draw me after You,” and so forth: he followed the One drawing him and did not enter beyond the boundary. Although he attained what Acher attained, he did not err as Acher erred, and so forth. Thus far the quoted text.”

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן אַחַר פָּגַע זוֹנָה תְּבָעָהּ, מַה שֶּׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ יֵצֶר הָרָע גָּדוֹל כָּל כָּךְ מִקּוֹדֶם.
connections.quote: “Acher went out to evil ways. He went out, found a harlot, and solicited her. She said to him: Are you not Elisha ben Avuyah? He uprooted a radish from its bed on Shabbat and gave it to her. She said: He is another (acher).”

connections.hePhrase: רַק בְּפָרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ" נֶאֱמַר: "הִשָּׁמְרוּ לָכֶם וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים יא, טז), וְעַל זֶה תִּקְּנוּ פָּרָשַׁת "וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ" לִקְבּוֹעַ אַהֲבַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בַּלֵּב גַּם בִּהְיוֹתוֹ עָסוּק בְּעִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם,
connections.quote: ‘Take care, lest your hearts be enticed and you turn aside, serve other gods, and bow down to them.’

connections.hePhrase: וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאוֹמְרִים: שְׂמֵחִים בְּצֵאתָם וְגוֹמֵר, שֶׁתִּהְיֶה יְצִיאָתוֹ כִּכְנִיסָתוֹ:

connections.quote: “Glad as they go forth and joyous as they return, they do with awe the will of their Maker.”
connections.context: The hymn says this of the heavenly luminaries.

connections.hePhrase: [רכה] דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁעוֹבְרִים דֶּרֶךְ הַלֵּב – פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁהַלֵּב מַרְגִּישׁ וּמִתְפַּעֵל בָּהֶם – הוּא נִקְרָא "עֵץ חַיִּים" וְסַמָּא דְּחַיֵּי.
connections.quote: “Of this it says, “Those who hope for His kindness”: the repair comes through Oral Torah, which is “the Torah of kindness upon her tongue.” We have already said that specifically concerning Oral Torah they taught that it endures only in one whose mind is humble. Oral Torah is compared to liquids—the “wine of Oral Torah,” as explained in the fourteenth discourse—and it endures only in one whose mind is humble and whose heart is broken within him.”
connections.explanation: Chanukah applies the image of liquid to Oral Torah and makes humility the condition for its endurance. This clarifies the present siman’s contrast between understanding an idea intellectually and having Torah pass through the heart. The broken heart is a receptive vessel, not the goal in isolation: it permits the Torah received there to become life, healing, and joy. That is why awe before wisdom can lead to a deeper and more lasting love of Torah.
connections.headline: Humility lets Oral Torah enter as nourishment rather than remain external knowledge

connections.hePhrase: כִּי הַלֵּב מְקוֹר הַחַיּוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "כִּי מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים" (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כג), וְכַאֲשֶׁר הוּא מִתְפַּעֵל, הֲרֵי שׁוֹרֶשׁ חַיּוּתוֹ מִתְפַּעֵל עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה וּמוֹלִידָה חַיּוּת בָּאָדָם.
connections.quote: see note 2467.
connections.context: “Heart” and “outgoings of life” provide the terms for Rav Tzadok’s claim that Torah engaging the heart engages the root of a person’s vitality.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ עַל יְדֵי שֶׁיִּרְאַת חֶטְאוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ, כִּי הַיִּרְאָה בַּלֵּב כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא עב:) עַל פָּסוּק "וְלֶב אָיִן", וְיִרְאָה נוּקְבָא וְתוֹרַת אֱמֶת דְּכַר לְהַשְׁלִים וּלְשַׂמֵּחַ הַלֵּב, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "פִּקּוּדֵי [ה' יְשָׁרִים מְשַׂמְּחֵי לֵב]" (תְּהִלִּים יט, ט), אַחַר הַיִּרְאָה הַמּוֹלֶדֶת לֵב נִשְׁבָּר וְעַצְבוּת.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yonatan’s name: What does the verse mean, “Why is there payment in the fool’s hand to acquire wisdom, when there is no heart”? Woe to the Torah scholars who engage in Torah but have no fear of Heaven.”
connections.context: The Talmud explains “no heart” as the absence of fear of Heaven. This is the precise basis for Rav Tzadok’s statement that fear is in the heart and must precede wisdom.

connections.hePhrase: וְיָדוּעַ כֹּחַ הַבִּישׁוּל לְהַבְלִיעַ, וְהַבָּלוּעַ אֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא עוֹד.
connections.quote: ““It shall be scoured and rinsed”: to expel what it has absorbed. But concerning an earthenware vessel, Scripture teaches you here that it never rids itself of its absorbed taint.”

connections.hePhrase: כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּדוֹאֵג בְּסַנְהֶדְרִין (קו:) דְּשָׁכַח הַכֹּל, מִשּׁוּם דְּרַחֲמָנָא לִבָּא בָּעֵי, שֶׁיִּהְיֶה הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה נִרְגָּשׁ בַּלֵּב, זֶהוּ הָעִיקָּר, שֶׁאָז יֵשׁ בּוֹ חַיּוּת וְהוּא נִבְלָע בּוֹ.
connections.quote: see note 1566 (Vol. I).
connections.context: The discussion joins the failure of learning without inward devotion to Doeg’s loss of his Torah. The first statement is Rava’s conclusion in this discussion; the second is attributed to Rabbi Ami. Neither is a statement of Shammai. Rav Tzadok draws together these passages to explain why Torah must be felt in the heart.

connections.hePhrase: וּבְלָאו הָכִי אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לא.): מוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ, הַיְינוּ כִּי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (עב:), כִּי בְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם הַיֵּצֶר מִתְגַּבֵּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נב.), וְגַם זֶה נִקְרָא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, וּכְמוֹ דוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתֹפֶל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: What is meant by “This is the Torah that Moses placed”? If one merits, it becomes for him a medicine of life; if he does not merit, it becomes for him a poison of death. This is what Rava said: For one who treats it skillfully, it is a medicine of life; for one who does not, it is a poison of death.”
connections.context: The word sam, medicine or poison, is the saying Rav Tzadok cites. In the surrounding discussion, fear of Heaven and inward integrity determine how Torah affects its learner.

connections.hePhrase: וּבְלָאו הָכִי אָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (לא.): מוּטָב שֶׁלֹּא הֶעֱלֵיתָ, הַיְינוּ כִּי חַס וְשָׁלוֹם יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת סַמָּא דְּמוֹתָא כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (עב:), כִּי בְּתַלְמִיד חָכָם הַיֵּצֶר מִתְגַּבֵּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּסֻכָּה (נב.), וְגַם זֶה נִקְרָא תַּלְמִיד חָכָם, וּכְמוֹ דוֹאֵג וַאֲחִיתֹפֶל שֶׁנִּקְרְאוּ תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים בְּכָל מָקוֹם.
connections.quote: see note 323 (Vol. I).

connections.hePhrase: וּכְשֶׁאֵין לוֹ יִרְאַת חֵטְא לְהַגְבִּיר עַל הַיֵּצֶר, אָז יוּכַל לִהְיוֹת חַס וְשָׁלוֹם כְּעִנְיַן אַחֵר שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֲגִיגָה טו:): סִפְרֵי טוֹעִין וְכוּלֵי וְזֶמֶר יְוָנִי וְכוּלֵי, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁכָּל חָכְמָתוֹ הָיָה דּוּגְמַת לִמּוּד חָכְמָה חִיצוֹנִית בְּתוֹרַת חָכְמָה לְבַד, וְלֹא לְהַשְׁלָמַת הַחִסָּרוֹן שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִיקַּר שֵׁם תּוֹרָה.
connections.quote: ‘What about Acher? Greek song never ceased from his mouth. They said of Acher: When he would rise from the study hall, many books of heretics would fall from his bosom.’

connections.hePhrase: וּמִשּׁוּם דְּלֹא הָיָה נָקִי אַגַּב אִמֵּיהּ, כִּידוּעַ דְּאַבָּא וְאִמָּא הֵם מוֹחַ וְלֵב, וְהוּא חָכְמַת מוֹחוֹ מְרוּבָּה רַק דְּלֵב אָיִן, דְּהַיְינוּ אִמָּא.
connections.quote: “Some say: When his mother was pregnant with him, she passed by houses of idolatry and smelled something of that kind. That smell permeated her body like the venom of a serpent.”

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן בִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ מִסְּתָמָא זוֹכִין זֶה כָּל אֶחָד מֵאָב וָאֵם הַגַּשְׁמִיִּים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵדֻיּוֹת סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב מִשְׁנָה ט): הָאָב זוֹכֶה לִבְנוֹ בְּחָכְמָה, וְאָב מַזְרִיעַ לוֹבֶן שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ מוֹחַ, וְאִשָּׁה אֹדֶם שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ בָּשָׂר וָדָם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ נִדָּה לא. לְגִרְסַת שְׁאֵלְתּוֹת), וְהַלֵּב בִּכְלָל.
connections.quote: “The Sages taught: There are three partners in a person: the Holy One, blessed be He, the father, and the mother. The father supplies the white substance, from which come bones, sinews, nails, the brain in the head, and the white of the eye. The mother supplies the red substance, from which come skin, flesh, hair, and the black of the eye. The Holy One, blessed be He, gives spirit, soul, facial appearance, eyesight, hearing, speech, walking, understanding, and intellect.”

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן בִּפְשָׁטֵיהּ מִסְּתָמָא זוֹכִין זֶה כָּל אֶחָד מֵאָב וָאֵם הַגַּשְׁמִיִּים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵדֻיּוֹת סוֹף פֶּרֶק ב מִשְׁנָה ט): הָאָב זוֹכֶה לִבְנוֹ בְּחָכְמָה, וְאָב מַזְרִיעַ לוֹבֶן שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ מוֹחַ, וְאִשָּׁה אֹדֶם שֶׁמִּמֶּנּוּ בָּשָׂר וָדָם (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ נִדָּה לא. לְגִרְסַת שְׁאֵלְתּוֹת), וְהַלֵּב בִּכְלָל.
connections.quote: “From the white substance supplied by the man are formed sinews, bones, brain, nails, and the white of the eyes. From the red substance supplied by the woman are formed skin, flesh, blood, hair, and the black of the eyes.”
connections.context: The Sheiltot explicitly includes blood among the mother’s contributions; the standard printed Niddah passage quoted here omits it. This is why Rav Tzadok carefully specifies “according to the reading of the Sheiltot.” He uses the traditional account symbolically to connect father and wisdom with the brain, and mother and fear with blood and the heart.

connections.hePhrase: וְקֶרִי יוֹצֵא מֵאֵבֶר חַי וְזִיבָה מֵאֵבֶר מֵת, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא עַל יְדֵי הִתְפַּעֲלוּת הַחֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב כְּלָל כַּנּוֹדָע.

connections.quote: “The discharge described in the Torah as zav is seminal fluid arising from an illness of the cavities in which it gathers. When the discharge emerges, it does not emerge with an erection as semen does; its emergence involves neither desire nor pleasure. Rather, it trails out like barley dough, dull in appearance like the white of an unfertilized egg. Semen, by contrast, is white and cohesive, like the white of a fertile egg.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מח:): זָב – מֵרְחַבְעָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "הִתְאַמֵּץ לַעֲלוֹת בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה" (מְלָכִים א יב, יח).
connections.quote: “Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: All the curses David directed at Joab were fulfilled in David’s own descendants: “May Joab’s house never lack one with a discharge, a leper, one who holds a spindle, one who falls by the sword, or one who lacks bread.” “One with a discharge”—from Rehoboam, as it says, “King Rehoboam exerted himself to mount the chariot and flee to Jerusalem,” and it says, “Every chariot upon which the one with a discharge rides shall be impure.””
connections.context: The passage identifies Rehoboam as the descendant affected by the discharge, using the shared word for riding in a chariot. This supplies the detail Rav Tzadok applies to the spiritual separation represented by Rehoboam.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מח:): זָב – מֵרְחַבְעָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בּוֹ: "הִתְאַמֵּץ לַעֲלוֹת בַּמֶּרְכָּבָה" (מְלָכִים א יב, יח).

connections.canonicalRef: Sod Yesharim, The Seventh Night of Pesach 24:1
connections.quote: “‘Moshe took Yosef's bones with him.’ My holy grandfather explained: When Moshe saw that Pharaoh accompanied Israel, he understood that they still had a connection to Egypt. The counsel was therefore to hold to the straightforward mitzvot. Yosef's bones allude to this counsel: his fear of sin preceded his wisdom. After Israel emptied Egypt and took all the good found there, their desire for those good things still required clarification through their service. As long as that clarification was unfinished, they still had a connection to Egypt.”
connections.explanation: Sod Yesharim expands the very received teaching cited here. Moshe recognizes an unresolved connection to Egypt and takes Yosef's bones as an image of holding to straightforward mitzvah observance before every reason has become clear. This explains why awe preceding wisdom is needed precisely when the route seems puzzling: the heart's attachment to the command keeps newly gained understanding from becoming detached knowledge.
connections.headline: Practice can hold the person before understanding is complete

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף" (שְׁמוֹת יג, יט), שֶׁהָעַצְמוּת שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הוּא: יִרְאַת חֶטְאוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ.
connections.quote: ‘Moses took Joseph’s bones with him, for Joseph had solemnly bound the children of Israel by an oath, saying: ‘God will surely attend to you, and you shall bring my bones up from here with you.’’

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "וַיִּקַּח מֹשֶׁה אֶת עַצְמוֹת יוֹסֵף" (שְׁמוֹת יג, יט), שֶׁהָעַצְמוּת שֶׁל יוֹסֵף הוּא: יִרְאַת חֶטְאוֹ קוֹדֶמֶת לְחָכְמָתוֹ.

connections.quote: “It is taught in Avot, chapter 3, mishnah 11: Anyone whose fear of sin precedes his wisdom, his wisdom endures. The meaning is that sometimes God conceals His acts and hides His intention from human beings, and a person does not know God’s will in the matter. This was the situation here: Moses wondered why God had not led them by the way of the land of the Philistines. The counsel for this is that when a person sees God dealing with him in concealment, he should not multiply clever explanations, but engage in the plain practice of the commandments and include himself in the attributes of fear. This is “Moses took the bones of Joseph,” and so forth. For the way of a righteous person is to attribute the deficiency to himself when a doubtful matter comes before him. This is the significance of his taking Joseph’s bones: because he attributed the deficiency to himself, he began to enter the attribute of fear, which Joseph’s bones signify. Joseph the righteous had the attribute of fear, as explained concerning the verse, “Lest He burst forth like fire in the house of Joseph.” This is “Anyone whose fear of sin precedes his wisdom,” and it is the attribute of Joseph the righteous, of blessed memory.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה צָרִיךְ לִיקַּח בְּעֵת שֶׁרוֹאֶה שִׁינּוּי בְּהִתְנַהֲגוּת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵבִין, כְּהָךְ דְּ"וְלֹא נָחָם אֱלֹהִים דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ [פְּלִשְׁתִּים]" (שָׁם, יז).
connections.quote: “And it came to pass, when Pharaoh had let the people go, that God led them not by the way of the land of the Philistines, although it was near; for God said: Lest the people change their minds when they see war, and return to Egypt.”

connections.hePhrase: וְטָהֳרַת הַזָּב הוּא בְּמַיִם חַיִּים, פֵּירוּשׁ עַל יְדֵי חֵשֶׁק שֶׁבַּלֵּב בְּחַיּוּת גָּמוּר לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה.
connections.quote: “When the man with a discharge becomes clean of his discharge, he shall count seven days for his purification, wash his garments, and bathe his flesh in living water, and he shall be clean.”
connections.context: “Living water” means fresh flowing spring water in the law of purification. Rav Tzadok also reads its literal wording as a figure for Torah sought with fully living desire.

connections.hePhrase: מִכָּל מָקוֹם הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מוּכָן לְהַשְׁפִּיעַ תָּמִיד דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה אַף בְּלֹא אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, וְזֶהוּ "הַמְחַדֵּשׁ בְּטוּבוֹ בְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית".

connections.heRef: סידור אשכנז, ימי חול, תפילת שחרית, ברכות קריאת שמע, יוצר אור ח׳
connections.quote: “For He alone performs mighty deeds and makes new things … who in His goodness renews each day, continually, the work of Creation.”

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל זֶה הוּא בִּרְכַּת "יוֹצֵר אוֹר", לְהַשִּׂיג הַחִדּוּשִׁין שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם תָּמִיד, וְזֶה נִקְרָא חָכְמַת מַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
connections.quote: “Every day there are new insights in Torah, for God continually renews the work of creation every day. The work of creation comes through the Torah, as stated at the beginning of Bereshit Rabbah; presumably, its renewal also comes through new insights in Torah.”

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגַלֶּה לְמִי שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר לוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז: הָאָבוֹת הֵן הֵן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה; כִּי מֶרְכֶּבֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַשָּׂם עָבִים רְכוּבוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קד, ג), "ה' רֹכֵב עַל עָב קַל" (יְשַׁעְיָה יט, א).
connections.quote: ““He concluded speaking with him, and God ascended from upon Abraham” (Genesis 17:22). It is taught: One who departs from another person, whether of greater or lesser stature, must take his leave from him. From whom do you derive this? From Abraham. On one occasion, Abraham was speaking with the Holy One blessed be He, when the ministering angels came to speak with him. He said to them: ‘Let me first take my leave from the Divine Presence, which is of greater stature than you, then I will speak with you.’ When he finished saying to the Holy One blessed be He all that he needed [to say], he said before Him: ‘Master of the universe, I must speak [with the angels].’ He said: ‘You may leave in peace.’ That is what is written: “[He concluded speaking with him,] and God ascended from upon Abraham.” Reish Lakish said: The patriarchs are themselves the divine chariot, as it is stated: “God ascended from upon Abraham,” “God ascended from upon him,” (Genesis 35:13) “And behold, the Lord stood upon him” (Genesis 28:13).”

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגַלֶּה לְמִי שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר לוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז: הָאָבוֹת הֵן הֵן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה; כִּי מֶרְכֶּבֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַשָּׂם עָבִים רְכוּבוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קד, ג), "ה' רֹכֵב עַל עָב קַל" (יְשַׁעְיָה יט, א).
connections.quote: ‘He lays the beams of His upper chambers in the waters, makes the clouds His chariot, and travels upon the wings of the wind.’

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגַלֶּה לְמִי שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר לוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז: הָאָבוֹת הֵן הֵן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה; כִּי מֶרְכֶּבֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַשָּׂם עָבִים רְכוּבוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קד, ג), "ה' רֹכֵב עַל עָב קַל" (יְשַׁעְיָה יט, א).
connections.quote: ‘A pronouncement concerning Egypt: Behold, Hashem rides upon a swift cloud and comes to Egypt. The idols of Egypt tremble before Him, and Egypt’s heart melts within it.’

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה הוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מְגַלֶּה לְמִי שֶׁמִּתְעוֹרֵר לוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה מז: הָאָבוֹת הֵן הֵן הַמֶּרְכָּבָה; כִּי מֶרְכֶּבֶת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עַל הַתַּחְתּוֹנִים בְּהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּתָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַשָּׂם עָבִים רְכוּבוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים קד, ג), "ה' רֹכֵב עַל עָב קַל" (יְשַׁעְיָה יט, א).
connections.quote: “and see in Shemot Rabbah 15 and Tanchuma, Chayei Sarah 3 on the verse: “Who makes the clouds His chariot”: a king of flesh and blood rides a horse adorned with silver and gold, but the Holy One rides upon clouds. Silver and gold mean love and awe as is known, which are the primary foundation stones and the chariot for royal Rabbis, servants of Hashem, mortal kings; yet Hashem looks not upon these, but upon the ultimate culmination—the rung of Jacob, the choicest of Patriarchs, and as I wrote elsewhere, that light and darkness correspond to Abraham and Isaac, and the pillar of cloud to Jacob, and this is not the place to elaborate.”
connections.explanation: Kometz HaMinchah contrasts a king’s silver and gold adornment with Hashem’s chariot of clouds, relating the former to love and fear and the latter to Yaakov’s completed truth. This develops the cloud image used here: the decisive issue is not spiritual display or a forceful isolated middah, but the person’s capacity to become a truthful vehicle for the divine presence.
connections.headline: Why the divine chariot is associated with clouds

connections.hePhrase: וּלְכָךְ יְחֶזְקֵאל בְּעֵת הַחוּרְבָּן רָאָה מֶרְכָּבָה, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן יְשַׁעְיָה רָאָה יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסְאוֹ בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים, כִּי אָז שִׁפְעוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ קָבוּעַ וְקַיָּימָא.
connections.quote: “Rava said: Everything Ezekiel saw, Isaiah saw. To what may Ezekiel be compared? To a villager who saw the king. And to what may Isaiah be compared? To a city dweller who saw the king.”

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל כַּאֲשֶׁר הוּא בְּמַדְרֵגַת "וָאֶהְיֶה מִתְהַלֵּךְ מֵאֹהֶל אֶל אֹהֶל" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א יז, ה), כְּמוֹ בַּחוּרְבָּן שֶׁנִּיטְּלָה מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד, וּקְבִיעוּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מִטַּלְטֵל מֵאֹהֶל אֶל אֹהֶל, כָּל אֶחָד בְּדוֹרוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה עַד מַלְכוּת בֵּית דָּוִד גַּם כֵּן בְּשׁוֹפְטִים מִפַּרְנָס לְפַרְנָס וְאֵינוֹ בִּקְבִיעוּת – רְכוּבוֹ הוּא עַל הֶעָבִים: מִי שֶׁמִּשְׁתַּדֵּל וּמֵכִין עַצְמוֹ לְכָךְ, עָלָיו הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ רוֹכֵב וּמִתְהַלֵּךְ.
connections.quote: ‘For I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought Israel up until this day. I have moved from tent to tent and from dwelling place to dwelling place.’

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל זֶה הוּא בְּרָכָה שְׁנִיָּה שֶׁלִּפְנֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, לְהַשִּׂיג הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה דְּחָכְמַת מַעֲשֵׂה מֶרְכָּבָה, שֶׁהוּא מַה שֶּׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שׁוֹפֵעַ לָנוּ בְּיִחוּד: "אֲשֶׁר בְּשֵׁם וְגוֹמֵר בָּטַחְנוּ, נָגִילָה וְנִשְׂמְחָה בִּישׁוּעָתֶךָ", שֶׁאָנוּ מְחַכִּים וּמְצַפִּים לְךָ וּבְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא שֶׁלָּנוּ.
