connections.heRef: סידור אשכנז, ימי חול, תפילת שחרית, ברכות קריאת שמע, אהבת ישראל א׳
connections.quote: “Our Father, our King, for the sake of our fathers who trusted in You, and whom You taught the statutes of life, so be gracious to us and teach us. … Put into our hearts to understand and to discern, to hear, to learn and to teach, to guard, to do and to fulfill all the words of the teaching of Your Torah in love. … For in Your holy, great and awesome Name we have trusted; we will rejoice and be glad in Your salvation.”

connections.hePhrase: וְיֵשׁ שָׁם שְׁמוֹנָה דְּבָרִים, וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּנֶגְדָּם רוֹמְזִים שְׁמוֹנָה בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְפוֹרָשִׁים בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
connections.displayRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Tetzaveh 3
connections.canonicalRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Exodus, Tetzaveh 3
connections.quote: ““These are the garments they shall make: a breastplate, an ephod, a robe, a patterned tunic, a turban, and a sash; they shall make sacred garments,” and so forth. Corresponding to the eight garments, the Men of the Great Assembly established eight requests in the blessing before the Shema: “to understand, to discern, to hear, to learn, to teach, to guard, to do, and to fulfill.””

connections.hePhrase: וְיֵשׁ שָׁם שְׁמוֹנָה דְּבָרִים, וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּנֶגְדָּם רוֹמְזִים שְׁמוֹנָה בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְפוֹרָשִׁים בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
connections.quote: “Then the escort of the bride is needed: he must see that the person does not nullify himself completely, but remains alive in this world. Once a person sees that his service has a place with Hashem and that Hashem desires it, he must remain alive so that he can serve Hashem further. A complete nullification in which no life remains in this world is not Hashem's will.”
connections.explanation: Tiferet Yosef explains the same description of Aharon as the escort of the bride: he safeguards the recipient's living capacity for continued service, alongside Moshe's disclosure of divine nearness. This gives substance to the siman's image of an awakening from below that carries divine presence. The eightfold correspondence here is conceptual: the actual Yom Kippur entry into the Holy of Holies is in four linen garments, specified in Leviticus 16:4, rather than the eight garments of the ordinary high-priestly service.
connections.headline: Aharon's role preserves a living recipient of holiness

connections.hePhrase: וְהַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל הוּא הָעוֹבֵד וִיסוֹד הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, דְּלָכֵן נִקְרָא אַהֲרֹן "שׁוֹשְׁבִינָא דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא" (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג, כ עַמּוּד א).
connections.quote: “Moses was the King’s attendant, and this is Tiferet; from there comes the great Sanhedrin. Aaron was the Queen’s attendant, and this is Malkhut, which we call the small heh.”
connections.context: The Zohar contrasts Moses as the attendant of the King with Aaron as the attendant of the Queen. Rav Tzadok uses Aaron’s association with Malkhut to explain the High Priest’s role in awakening service and desire from below.

connections.hePhrase: וְהַשְּׁמוֹנָה בְּגָדִים הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, שֶׁהוּא בִּקְבִיעוּת הַמָּקוֹם, דְּאָז יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא וְלֹא בְּמֶרְכָּבָה, רַק עַל יְדֵי הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא הַחַיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים נוֹשְׂאִים וְסוֹבְלִים הַכִּסֵּא כָּבוֹד, וְאָז הוּא עִיקַּר הַהַשָּׂגָה בִּשְׁמוֹנָה מַדְרֵגוֹת דִּלְהָבִין וְכוּלֵי.
connections.quote: “He shall wear a sacred linen tunic, and linen breeches shall be upon his flesh; he shall gird himself with a linen sash and wrap himself in a linen turban. They are sacred garments. He shall immerse his body in water and put them on.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהַשְּׁמוֹנָה בְּגָדִים הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּכְנַס לְבֵית קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים, שֶׁהוּא בִּקְבִיעוּת הַמָּקוֹם, דְּאָז יוֹשֵׁב עַל כִּסֵּא וְלֹא בְּמֶרְכָּבָה, רַק עַל יְדֵי הָאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא הַחַיּוֹת שֶׁבַּתַּחְתּוֹנִים נוֹשְׂאִים וְסוֹבְלִים הַכִּסֵּא כָּבוֹד, וְאָז הוּא עִיקַּר הַהַשָּׂגָה בִּשְׁמוֹנָה מַדְרֵגוֹת דִּלְהָבִין וְכוּלֵי.
connections.quote: “This is also why the High Priest's service throughout the year was in golden garments: through his service he illuminated all the garments with the light of Hashem's will. But on Yom Kippur, when he enters the innermost place and Hashem reveals the light of His will explicitly without a garment, the High Priest does not stand before Hashem in such garments and expansion, but in linen garments, indicating that he then surrenders even the receiving vessel to Hashem. Thus the Sifrei says that bad, linen, is stated four times on Yom Kippur: one excludes the breastplate, one the ephod, one the robe, and one the forehead plate.”
connections.explanation: Sod Yesharim expressly distinguishes golden garments from linen at the inward Yom Kippur entry and lists the four additional garments excluded there. The siman's reference to eight garments belongs to its symbolic account of eight modes of understanding; it must not be read as a literal description of wearing all eight in the Holy of Holies. This distinction is also relevant to the later garment discussion in Siman 263.
connections.headline: Eightfold symbolism and the linen garments of inward entry

connections.hePhrase: וְאָז נֶאֱמַר: "וַיֵּשֶׁב שְׁלֹמֹה עַל כִּסֵּא ה'" (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כט, כג), שֶׁהָיָה דּוּגְמַת אָדָם הַיּוֹשֵׁב עַל הַכִּסֵּא כִּבְיָכוֹל.
connections.quote: see note 2828.

connections.hePhrase: כִּי עֲבוֹדַת הַכֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל הָיָה פּוֹעֵל שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ עֲבוֹדָה וְהִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת וְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא, וְהוּא מַדְרֵגַת הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁקּוֹדֵם לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל.
connections.quote: “A king takes precedence over a High Priest, as it is stated: “The king said to them: Take with you the servants of your lord,” and so forth.”

connections.hePhrase: וְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין מח:) דָּרְשׁוּ תֵּיבַת "מֶרְכָּבָה" אַזָּב, שֶׁכָּתוּב בּוֹ "מֶרְכָּב" (וַיִּקְרָא טו, ט), [וְשֶׁמִּפְּנֵי חוּלְשָׁתוֹ אֵין יוֹשֵׁב אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ מֶרְכָּב].
connections.quote: ‘Any riding seat on which a zav (a man with a discharge) rides shall become impure.’

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (פב עַמּוּד א) שֶׁהוּא כְּמַאן דַּחֲמָא בָּתַר כּוֹתְלָא.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Elazar said: Of Israel it is written, “Face to face Hashem spoke.” Of Ezekiel it is written “like the appearance” and “a likeness,” like one who sees behind many walls, like one who sees a person behind a wall.”
connections.context: The contrast is between Israel’s direct encounter at Sinai and Ezekiel’s vision through layers of concealment. This is the precise image Rav Tzadok invokes in explaining the revelation of the chariot during exile.

connections.hePhrase: וְנֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "מַרְאוֹת" (יְחֶזְקֵאל א, א), מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּישַׁעְיָה: "וָאֶרְאֶה וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, א).
connections.quote: ‘It happened in the thirtieth year, in the fourth month, on the fifth of the month: I was among the exiles by the River Kevar, when the heavens opened and I saw visions of God.’

connections.hePhrase: וְנֶאֱמַר בּוֹ "מַרְאוֹת" (יְחֶזְקֵאל א, א), מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בִּישַׁעְיָה: "וָאֶרְאֶה וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה ו, א).
connections.quote: ‘In the year that King Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and exalted, and the train of His robe filled the Temple.’

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם זֶה הָיָה בְּעֵת הַמַּסָּעוֹת כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֲגִיגָה יג:),
connections.quote: ““I saw, and behold, a storm wind came from the north, a great cloud and flashing fire, with brightness around it, and from within it the appearance of chashmal, from within the fire.” Where did it go? Rav Yehudah said in Rav’s name: It went to subdue the whole world under Nebuchadnezzar the wicked. Why to such an extent? So that the nations would not say: The Holy One, blessed be He, delivered His children into the hands of a lowly nation. The Holy One, blessed be He, said: What caused Me to become an attendant to idolaters? Israel’s sins caused it.”
connections.context: The passage describes the movement of the chariot in Ezekiel’s vision as serving the Babylonian conquest. Rav Tzadok cites this setting to distinguish the vision during exile from the fuller revelation associated with Solomon.

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם זֶה הָיָה בְּעֵת הַמַּסָּעוֹת כִּדְרַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (חֲגִיגָה יג:),
connections.quote: “Rav Yehudah bar Idi said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: The Shekhinah traveled ten journeys, derived from Scripture, and corresponding to them the Sanhedrin went into exile, as received by tradition. The Shekhinah’s ten journeys, derived from Scripture, were: from the Ark-cover to a cherub, from one cherub to the other, from a cherub to the threshold, from the threshold to the courtyard, from the courtyard to the altar, from the altar to the roof, from the roof to the wall, from the wall to the city, from the city to the mountain, and from the mountain to the wilderness. From the wilderness it ascended and sat in its place, as it is stated: “I will go; I will return to My place.””

connections.hePhrase: וְרַק בִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם קָיְימָא סִיהֲרָא בְּאַשְׁלָמוּתָא, פֵּירוּשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלוּ לִלְבָנָה, וְהוּא הִשִּׂיג הַשֶּׁפַע הַבָּא עַל יְדֵי אִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא גַּם כֵּן בִּשְׁלֵימוּת גָּמוּר.
connections.quote: “For it was taught: It is written, “Solomon’s wisdom surpassed.” In the days of King Solomon the moon stood in its fullness. This is what is written: “Solomon’s wisdom surpassed the wisdom of all the people of the east.””

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל זֶה חִבֵּר שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים שֶׁהוּא מָלֵא מֵאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא וְהַשֶּׁפַע דִּלְעֵילָא, וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יָדַיִם סוֹף פֶּרֶק ג) שֶׁהוּא קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים וְלֹא הָיָה כָּל הָעוֹלָם כְּדַאי וְכוּלֵי:
connections.quote: ‘A book that has been erased but retains eighty-five letters, corresponding to the passage ‘When the Ark traveled,’ imparts impurity to the hands. A scroll with eighty-five letters written in it, corresponding to the passage ‘When the Ark traveled,’ imparts impurity to the hands. All the sacred Scriptures impart impurity to the hands. Song of Songs and Ecclesiastes impart impurity to the hands. Rabbi Yehuda says: Song of Songs imparts impurity to the hands, but Ecclesiastes is disputed. Rabbi Yosei says: Ecclesiastes does not impart impurity to the hands, but Song of Songs is disputed. Rabbi Shimon says: Ecclesiastes is among the leniencies of Beit Shammai and the stringencies of Beit Hillel. Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai said: I received a tradition from seventy-two elders, on the day they seated Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya in the academy, that Song of Songs and Ecclesiastes impart impurity to the hands. Rabbi Akiva said: Heaven forbid! No one in Israel disputed that Song of Songs imparts impurity to the hands, for the whole world is not worth as much as the day on which Song of Songs was given to Israel. All the Writings are holy, but Song of Songs is the holy of holies. If they disputed anything, they disputed only Ecclesiastes. Rabbi Yochanan ben Yehoshua, the son of Rabbi Akiva’s father-in-law, said: As Ben Azzai stated, so they disputed and so they decided.’

connections.hePhrase: [רכז] כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל יֵשׁ לָהֶם אֱמוּנָה שְׁלֵימָה בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, בִּמְצִיאוּתוֹ וְאַחְדוּתוֹ וְהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (צז.) שֶׁהֵם מַאֲמִינִים בְּנֵי מַאֲמִינִים.
connections.quote: ‘Reish Lakish said: One who suspects upright people is afflicted in his body, as it is written: ‘But they will not believe me,’ and so forth. Yet it was revealed before the Holy One, blessed be He, that Israel would believe. He said to him: ‘They are believers, children of believers, whereas you will ultimately fail to believe.’’

connections.hePhrase: וְזָכָה יַתִּיר, יְהִיבִין לֵיהּ "רוּחַ" (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, צד עַמּוּד ב), הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּזְדַּכֵּךְ הַלֵּב יוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ זֶה בַּלֵּב, וּבָא מִמַּדְרֵגַת אֱמוּנָה לְמַדְרֵגַת אֱמֶת, שֶׁהוּא הַדָּבָר הַבָּרוּר וְנִיכָּר לַלֵּב וְלֹא בֶּאֱמוּנָה לְבַד.
connections.quote: “Come and see: When a person is born, he is given a nefesh from the side of the living creature, from the side of purity, from those called the holy ofanim. If he merits more, he is given a ruach from the side of the holy living creatures. If he merits more, he is given a neshamah from the side of the Throne. These three are the handmaid, servant, and maidservant of the King’s daughter.”
connections.context: This is the first progression from nefesh to ruach and neshamah. The following paragraph describes a further progression at the level of Atzilut. Rav Tzadok’s immediate statement concerns the first transition: ruach is granted as the heart becomes more refined and faith becomes inwardly recognized truth.

connections.hePhrase: וְזָכָה יַתִּיר, יְהִיבִין לֵיהּ "רוּחַ" (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, צד עַמּוּד ב), הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּזְדַּכֵּךְ הַלֵּב יוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ זֶה בַּלֵּב, וּבָא מִמַּדְרֵגַת אֱמוּנָה לְמַדְרֵגַת אֱמֶת, שֶׁהוּא הַדָּבָר הַבָּרוּר וְנִיכָּר לַלֵּב וְלֹא בֶּאֱמוּנָה לְבַד.
connections.quote: “For faith means trust: one believes in the Life of the worlds. Truth, however, is what is clear to the eye and requires no assurance. Of one who attains this, it is inappropriate to say “assured”; rather, this person is a participant in the World to Come, indicated with a finger and visibly recognized.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזָכָה יַתִּיר, יְהִיבִין לֵיהּ "רוּחַ" (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב, צד עַמּוּד ב), הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁנִּזְדַּכֵּךְ הַלֵּב יוֹתֵר עַד שֶׁהוּא מַרְגִּישׁ זֶה בַּלֵּב, וּבָא מִמַּדְרֵגַת אֱמוּנָה לְמַדְרֵגַת אֱמֶת, שֶׁהוּא הַדָּבָר הַבָּרוּר וְנִיכָּר לַלֵּב וְלֹא בֶּאֱמוּנָה לְבַד.
connections.quote: “In the order Hashem established in this world, in proportion to a person's surrender of himself to Hashem, Hashem returns to him a higher level. As the Zohar says (Mishpatim 94b), ‘When a person is born, he is given a soul from the side of the pure creature… If he merits more, he is given spirit.’ When this person can entrust his present level to Hashem, Hashem then trusts him with a higher level.”
connections.explanation: Sod Yesharim cites the same progression from soul to spirit and explains that a person receives a further level by entrusting the present one to Hashem. This develops the relation between effort and gift in the siman without treating the numbered levels as achievements one can claim by intellect alone.
connections.headline: Entrusting the present level before receiving another

connections.hePhrase: כִּי "נְשָׁמָה" לְשׁוֹן נְשִׁימָה, מַה שֶּׁנּוֹשֵׁם הָרוּחַ בְּאַפָּיו, וְעִיקַּר הַחַיּוּת הָרוּחַ, רַק שֶׁצָּרִיךְ בְּכָל פַּעַם לִנְשִׁימַת רוּחַ חָדָשׁ.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Ḥanina: For every single breath a person breathes, he must praise the Creator. What is the reason? “Let every soul praise Yah”—let every breath praise Yah.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהָרוּחַ, כְּעִנְיַן "רוּחַ ה' דִּבֶּר בִּי" (שְׁמוּאֵל ב כג, ב), הוּא לְלוֹמְדֵי תּוֹרָה מִצַּד דְּבַר ה' שֶׁבְּפִיהֶם, מוֹלִיד הַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב לְהַכִּיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ אֱלוֹהַּ וּבוֹרֵא עוֹלָם.
connections.quote: ‘The spirit of Hashem spoke through me, and His word was upon my tongue.’

connections.hePhrase: וְיֵשׁ עוֹד נְשָׁמָה לַנְּשָׁמָה (חַיָּה), וְהַיְינוּ כִּידוּעַ דִּבְכָל דָּבָר יֵשׁ עֶשֶׂר סְפִירוֹת, וְהַתְחָלַת הַהַשָּׂגָה הוּא מֵחָכְמָה, וְכֶתֶר הוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָצוֹן הַנֶּעְלָם.
connections.heRef: תניא, חלק שלישי; אגרת התשובה ד׳:י׳
connections.quote: “For the yod, which is a point alone, alludes to His wisdom, which is hidden and concealed before it comes to the expansion and revelation of comprehension and understanding. The point projecting above the yod alludes to the blessed supernal will, which is far above the level of supernal wisdom, as is known.”

connections.hePhrase: וְכָל מַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו וְהִרְהוּרָיו וּרְצוֹנוֹ בִּלְתִּי לַה' לְבַדּוֹ בִּידִיעָתוֹ וִידִיעַת תּוֹרָתוֹ, שֶׁעַל זֶה אָמְרוּ (סֻכָּה נב:): אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי;
connections.quote: see note 3449.
connections.context: The source explicitly makes divine assistance necessary for overcoming the inclination. Rav Tzadok invokes it while describing the movement of all a person’s thought and desire toward Hashem.

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל אֵלּוּ שָׁלֹשׁ נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא בָרוּחַ ה'", "וְלֹא בָרַעַשׁ", "וְלֹא בָאֵשׁ" (מְלָכִים א יט, יא–יב).
connections.quote: see note 587 (Vol. I).
connections.context: The wind and earthquake are the first two manifestations in Elijah’s vision. Rav Tzadok draws on the repeated statement that the Lord is not identified with them.

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל אֵלּוּ שָׁלֹשׁ נֶאֱמַר: "לֹא בָרוּחַ ה'", "וְלֹא בָרַעַשׁ", "וְלֹא בָאֵשׁ" (מְלָכִים א יט, יא–יב).
connections.quote: see note 588 (Vol. I).
connections.context: This completes the three manifestations cited by Rav Tzadok and supplies the quiet sound that follows them.

connections.hePhrase: כִּי יֵשׁ עוֹד מַדְרֵגָה חֲמִישִׁית הַנִּקְרֵאת "יְחִידָה", וְהוּא "קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה" (שָׁם, יב).
connections.quote: “As we heard from our holy teacher of Izbica, of blessed memory, concerning “The Lord was not in the wind”: that a person has a desire for holiness does not yet establish certainty. “The Lord was not in the tumult”: even when one possesses alacrity and vigor. “The Lord was not in the fire”: even when one has fervor in the pursuit of holy service. None of these yet establishes certainty. Only “after the fire, a still, thin voice”—these three words are the blessed God’s signature upon the three qualities found in the souls of Israel: wind, tumult, and fire. Then a person can trust in the name of the Lord, but cannot rely on anything that comes from himself.”

connections.hePhrase: כִּי יֵשׁ עוֹד מַדְרֵגָה חֲמִישִׁית הַנִּקְרֵאת "יְחִידָה", וְהוּא "קוֹל דְּמָמָה דַקָּה" (שָׁם, יב).
connections.quote: “And in Ra'aya Meheimna (Pinchas 227b) it is explained that these parallel Elijah's vision of the "wind, earthquake, fire, and a still, small voice"; examine it there. The Nogah (translucent glow) represents this aforementioned root; Ezekiel beheld these forces in their chaotic fury during the Babylonian exile, as our Sages expounded: "a stormy wind came out of the north" to subdue the entire world under the hand of Nebuchadnezzar. Elijah, by contrast, beheld them in their rectified state, perceiving that the "still, small voice"—the Nogah surrounding it—is the very Glory of Hashem aligning with His sublime will. And I heard that the "still, small voice" is Hashem's divine seal impressed after human effort (metaphorized by wind, earthquake, and fire); during man's initial striving Hashem is not yet manifestly present, until the still, small voice seals it, revealing that Hashem was immanent within all those efforts in absolute truth; "Voice" is the seal of wind, "silence" is the seal of earthquake, and "thin/subtle" is the seal of fire; mirroring the construction of the Tabernacle, where human labor was categorized as wind, earthquake, and fire, without the Shechinah resting until Moses prayed "May the pleasantness of Hashem...", which was the still, small voice sealing their work with Divine grace; "Hashem our G-d be upon us" is the voice sealing the wind; "establish Thou the work of our hands upon us" is the silence sealing the earthquake; and "the work of our hands establish Thou it" is the subtle quietude sealing the fire, and this clarifies the concept somewhat.”
connections.explanation: Dover Tzedek explicitly calls the still, thin voice Hashem’s seal after the wind, earthquake, and fire of human work. Its example is the completed Mishkan, whose labor awaited the revelation of the Shechinah. This explains why the present siman distinguishes even very refined effort from the final mode of union: the final seal confirms the work’s inner truth rather than simply adding another forceful human movement.
connections.headline: The still voice as Hashem’s seal upon human effort

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ חַיִּים שֶׁלֹּא בְּצַעַר וְשֶׁלֹּא בְּיֵצֶר הָרָע הַנִּזְכָּר בְּתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה (פֶּרֶק ה) שֶׁזָּכוּ לָזֶה הָאָבוֹת וְיִתְרוֹ וְיַעְבֵּץ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
connections.quote: “A measure of life without suffering and without the evil inclination is given to the righteous in this world, a likeness of the World to Come. These are Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Jabez, Jethro, and those like them.”
connections.context: The source describes an anticipatory measure of future life already experienced by these righteous people. Rav Tzadok uses that state to explain the soul’s undivided attachment to God.

connections.hePhrase: [רכח] עִיקַּר צוּרַת הָאָדָם הוּא נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה שֶׁבּוֹ, וְהַגּוּף אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְבוּשׁ הָאָדָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (עו עַמּוּד א).
connections.quote: ‘When Adam was created, what is written of him? ‘You clothe me with skin and flesh,’ and so forth (Job 10:11; Bereshit 20b). If so, what is the human being? If you say that he is nothing but skin, flesh, bones, and sinews, that is not so, for the human being is certainly none other than the soul. These things mentioned—skin and flesh, bones and sinews—are all only clothing. They are a person’s garments, but they are not the human being. When this human being departs, he strips off those garments he was wearing. The skin in which a person is clothed, and all those bones and sinews, are all in the mystery of supernal wisdom, corresponding to what is above. The skin corresponds to what is above, as the Master taught concerning those curtains, for it is written: ‘He stretches out the heavens like a curtain’ (Psalms 104:2), and ‘rams’ skins dyed red and tachash skins’ (Exodus 25:5). These are the garments above, which cover the garment that is the expanse of the heavens, the outer garment. The curtains are the inner garment, and this is the membrane that covers the flesh.’

connections.hePhrase: כָּךְ "זֶה לְעֻמַּת זֶה" חֵלֶק אָדָם רָע גַּם כֵּן בְּה' כֹּחוֹת, וְהֵם ג' קְלִיפּוֹת הַטְּמֵאוֹת הַנִּזְכָּר בִּיחֶזְקֵאל (א, ד).
connections.quote: ‘I saw, and behold, a storm wind was coming from the north, a great cloud and flashing fire, with brightness around it. From its midst appeared something like chashmal, from the midst of the fire.’

connections.hePhrase: נֶפֶשׁ הַטְּמֵאָה – הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה עֲבֵירוֹת בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ, דִּבּוּרוֹ וּמַעֲשָׂיו, זֶה נִקְרָא "רוּחַ סְעָרָה" שֶׁבָּא מִן הַצָּפוֹן, הוּא הַצְּפוֹנִי שֶׁבֶּחָלָל הַשְּׂמָאלִי, וְסָעִיר כּוּלָּא עֵילָא וְתַתָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר וַיַּקְהֵל (רג עַמּוּד א).
connections.quote: “But I will remove far from you the northern one (hatzefoni), and will drive him into a land barren and desolate.”

connections.hePhrase: נֶפֶשׁ הַטְּמֵאָה – הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה עֲבֵירוֹת בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ, דִּבּוּרוֹ וּמַעֲשָׂיו, זֶה נִקְרָא "רוּחַ סְעָרָה" שֶׁבָּא מִן הַצָּפוֹן, הוּא הַצְּפוֹנִי שֶׁבֶּחָלָל הַשְּׂמָאלִי, וְסָעִיר כּוּלָּא עֵילָא וְתַתָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר וַיַּקְהֵל (רג עַמּוּד א).
connections.quote: “Joel called it ‘the northern one,’ as it is said: ‘But I will remove far from you the northern one.’ The Sages taught: ‘But I will remove far from you the northern one’—this is the evil inclination, which is hidden (tzafun) and stands in a person’s heart.”

connections.hePhrase: נֶפֶשׁ הַטְּמֵאָה – הַיְינוּ כְּשֶׁעוֹשֶׂה עֲבֵירוֹת בְּמַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ, דִּבּוּרוֹ וּמַעֲשָׂיו, זֶה נִקְרָא "רוּחַ סְעָרָה" שֶׁבָּא מִן הַצָּפוֹן, הוּא הַצְּפוֹנִי שֶׁבֶּחָלָל הַשְּׂמָאלִי, וְסָעִיר כּוּלָּא עֵילָא וְתַתָּא, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר וַיַּקְהֵל (רג עַמּוּד א).
connections.quote: “Why is it called a storm? Because it agitates everything, above and below. “It comes from the north,” because it comes from that side; the indication is, “From the north evil shall be opened.” Many other sides are joined to that storm wind, and therefore it comes from the north.”
connections.context: The biblical verse quoted within the passage is Jeremiah 1:14. The phrase “agitates everything, above and below” is the wording Rav Tzadok applies to the impure soul and the inclination hidden in the left chamber of the heart.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה יג:): לִכְבּוֹשׁ כָּל הָעוֹלָם תַּחַת יַד נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר, הַיְינוּ מִצַּד הִתְגַּבְּרוּת הָרָע בְּמַעֲשֶׂה, אָז כֹּחַ נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר גּוֹבֵר עַל כָּל הָעוֹלָם;
connections.quote: see note 3523.

connections.hePhrase: וְעַיֵּין שָׁם בַּזֹּהַר: מַה בֵּין עֲנָנָא לַעֲנָנָא?
connections.quote: “This “great cloud” is a cloud of darkness, darkening the whole world. Come and see: What is the difference between one cloud and the other? The cloud of which it is written, “The cloud of the Lord was over them by day,” and “Your cloud stands over them,” is a cloud that shines and radiates, and all lights are seen within that cloud. This cloud, however, is a dark cloud that does not shine at all; it obstructs all the lights, so that they cannot appear before it.”

connections.hePhrase: הַיְינוּ דְּבֶאֱמֶת: "יָשֶׁת חֹשֶׁךְ סִתְרוֹ" (תְּהִלִּים יח, יב), וַ"עֲבִים רְכוּבוֹ" (שָׁם קד, ג), דְּאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגַת אֱמֶת הַכָּרָה בְּרוּרָה רַק עַל יְדֵי הַאֲפָלָה קְצָת, וְעַל יְדֵי הַחֹשֶׁךְ הוּא מַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ נִסְתָּר בּוֹ,
connections.quote: ‘He made darkness His hiding place, His canopy around Him: dark waters and thick clouds of the skies.’

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ מַלְכוּת פָּרַס שֶׁבִּקְּשׁוּ לְהַשְׁמִיד וְכוּלֵי, כִּי הַלֵּב מִמֶּנּוּ תּוֹצְאוֹת חַיִּים, וְכַאֲשֶׁר לֵב אָיִן, הֲרֵי זֶה מְבַקֵּשׁ לַהֲרוֹג.
connections.quote: “And letters were sent by the couriers to all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to slay, and to annihilate all the Jews, young and old, children and women, in one day.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מְגִילָּה יב.): מִפְּנֵי שֶׁנֶּהֱנוּ וְכוּלֵי, הַהֲנָאָה הוּא הַהַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s students asked him: Why did the enemies of Israel in that generation incur destruction? He said: You tell me. They said: Because they enjoyed the feast of that wicked man. If so, those in Shushan should be killed, but those throughout the world should not be killed! They said: Then you tell us. He said: Because they bowed to the image.”
connections.context: “The enemies of Israel” is the Talmud’s euphemism for Israel. Rav Tzadok focuses on the students’ wording “enjoyed,” as an experience registered in the heart. The passage does not leave their proposal unqualified: Rabbi Shimon rejects it as an explanation of the decree against Jews outside Shushan.

connections.hePhrase: רַק בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי" (תְּהִלִּים עג, כו; שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב).
connections.quote: “They said to him: Is there then favoritism in the matter? He said to them: They acted only outwardly; so too, the Holy One, blessed be He, acted toward them only outwardly. This is what is written: “For He did not afflict from His heart.””

connections.hePhrase: רַק בֶּאֱמֶת הֵם לֹא עָשׂוּ אֶלָּא לִפְנִים, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לִבָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "צוּר לְבָבִי" (תְּהִלִּים עג, כו; שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ה, ב).
connections.quote: see note 585 (Vol. I).
connections.context: “Rock of my heart” is the wording Rav Tzadok connects with the Midrash’s identification of God as Israel’s heart. Translating heart only as mind would conceal that connection.

connections.hePhrase: רַק הוּא עַל יְדֵי עָנָן גָּדוֹל הַמַּחְשִׁיךְ לְרֶגַע, וְכַאֲשֶׁר יָשֵׁב רוּחוֹ וְיִתְפַּזְּרוּ הָעֲנָנִים, יֵרָאֶה אוֹר בָּהִיר.
connections.quote: “He sends out His word and melts them; He causes His wind to blow, and the waters flow.”

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן מְנֻמֶּרֶת בִּגְזֵירוֹתֶיהָ וְכוּלֵי כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יג).
connections.quote: “‘I was looking, and behold, another, like a leopard’ (Daniel 7:6)—this is Greece, which imposed its decrees and said to Israel: Write upon the horn of the ox that you have no portion in the World to Come.”
connections.context: Rav Tzadok’s wording “spotted (menameret) in its decrees” plays on the leopard (namer) of Daniel’s vision; the printed Midrash reads “imposed its decrees.”

connections.hePhrase: וְ"נֹגַהּ לוֹ סָבִיב" – יָדוּעַ דִּקְלִיפַּת נֹגַהּ הוּא נֶגֶד דְּבָרִים הַמּוּתָּרִים וְדִבְרֵי רְשׁוּת, וְזֶהוּ נְשָׁמָה לַנְּשָׁמָה (חַיָּה), וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם וְכֶתֶר דְּרַע, שֶׁנֶּגְדּוֹ אֱדוֹם כַּנּוֹדָע,
connections.quote: “‘When God destroyed the cities of the plain, God remembered Avraham and sent Lot out of the overthrow.’ The relation between remembering Avraham and saving Lot is explained by the Zohar: Lot represents the inclination and Avraham the soul. The writings of the Ari identify Lot with the shell of nogah, a mixture of good and evil, as it says, ‘and brightness around it’—it is darkness, with light encamped around it. The soul chiefly comes to this world to clarify this shell and raise it to the highest levels. Nogah signifies all permitted worldly matters. Although these are entirely permitted, they nevertheless require clarification, as the Sages taught: Sanctify yourself within what is permitted to you.”
connections.explanation: Beit Yaakov interprets Lot's rescue through the mixed category of nogah. Its conclusion precisely identifies the sphere at issue: worldly matters that are genuinely permitted, yet whose direction still needs clarification. This makes the siman's counsel against indiscriminate rejection intelligible while keeping its distinction between this mixed sphere and the three prohibited shells.
connections.headline: Permitted things can still require clarification

connections.hePhrase: דְּ"רֵאשִׁית גּוֹיִם עֲמָלֵק" (בַּמִּדְבָּר כד, כ), שֶׁהַהַתְחָלָה הוּא עַל יְדֵי דְּבַר הָרְשׁוּת, לִהְיוֹת נִמְשָׁךְ בְּתַאֲווֹת הָרְשׁוּת וְתַעֲנוּגִים הַמּוּתָּרִים רַק בְּלֹא שׁוּם סֶרֶךְ מִצְוָה, זֶהוּ שׁוֹרֶשׁ דְּיֵצֶר הַמַּסִּית,
connections.quote: ‘He saw Amalek, took up his parable, and said: ‘Amalek is first among the nations, but its end is destruction.’’

connections.hePhrase: וּמִן הַהֶיתֵּר בָּא לְאִיסּוּר כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ן רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת קְדוֹשִׁים.
connections.quote: “The matter is this: the Torah warned against forbidden sexual relationships and forbidden foods, while permitting intercourse between a man and his wife and the eating of meat and wine. A person driven by appetite could therefore find room to be immersed in sexual excess with his wife or his many wives, to be among wine drinkers and gluttonous meat eaters, and to speak as he pleases with every kind of vulgarity, since this prohibition was not specified in the Torah. He would then be a scoundrel with the Torah’s permission. Therefore, after detailing the prohibitions that it forbade entirely, Scripture came with a general command: that we should practice restraint regarding what is permitted.”

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁכָּל נַרַ"נ שֶׁלּוֹ בִּקְדוּשָׁה, הֲרֵי גַּם דִּבְרֵי רְשׁוּת שֶׁלּוֹ: שֻׁלְחָנוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְמִזְבֵּחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק ג דְּאָבוֹת), וּשְׁתִיָּיתָם יַיִן לִנְסָכִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יוֹמָא עא.), וְשִׂיחַת חוּלִין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה כא:), וְכֵן כָּל דִּבְרֵי רְשׁוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם.
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Shimon says: Three who ate at one table and did not speak words of Torah over it are as though they ate from sacrifices to the dead, as it says: ‘For all tables are full of vomit and filth, with no place (beli makom).’ But three who ate at one table and spoke words of Torah over it are as though they ate from the table of the Omnipresent (Makom), blessed be He, as it says: ‘He said to me: This is the table that is before Hashem.’’

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁכָּל נַרַ"נ שֶׁלּוֹ בִּקְדוּשָׁה, הֲרֵי גַּם דִּבְרֵי רְשׁוּת שֶׁלּוֹ: שֻׁלְחָנוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְמִזְבֵּחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק ג דְּאָבוֹת), וּשְׁתִיָּיתָם יַיִן לִנְסָכִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יוֹמָא עא.), וְשִׂיחַת חוּלִין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה כא:), וְכֵן כָּל דִּבְרֵי רְשׁוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם.
connections.quote: ‘‘To you, men—ishim—I call.’ Rabbi Berekhya said: These are Torah scholars, who resemble women and perform mighty deeds like men. Rabbi Berekhya also said: One who wishes to pour a wine libation upon the altar should fill the throats of Torah scholars with wine, as it is said: ‘To you, men—ishim—I call.’’

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ, כִּי הַתַּלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁכָּל נַרַ"נ שֶׁלּוֹ בִּקְדוּשָׁה, הֲרֵי גַּם דִּבְרֵי רְשׁוּת שֶׁלּוֹ: שֻׁלְחָנוֹ דּוֹמֶה לְמִזְבֵּחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ פֶּרֶק ג דְּאָבוֹת), וּשְׁתִיָּיתָם יַיִן לִנְסָכִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יוֹמָא עא.), וְשִׂיחַת חוּלִין דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סֻכָּה כא:), וְכֵן כָּל דִּבְרֵי רְשׁוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם.
connections.quote: “This does not mean, Heaven forbid, that Torah scholars should be eager for eating and drinking, filling their throats as one stuffs a glutton. Rather, the matter follows the intention I have explained: Torah scholars who are holy in their ways and in all their deeds are truly like the Temple and the altar, because the Shekhinah rests upon them as it rested in the Temple itself. What is offered to them is therefore like what is offered upon the altar, and filling their throats takes the place of filling the libation bowls.”

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן הוּא עֵשָׂו שֶׁנִּקְרָא בְּקִדּוּשִׁין (יח.) "יִשְׂרָאֵל מוּמָר".
connections.quote: ‘Rav Chiya bar Avin said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: A non-Jew inherits his father by Torah law, as it is written: ‘For I have given Mount Seir to Esau as an inheritance.’ But perhaps an apostate Israelite is different? Rather, the proof is from here: ‘For I have given Ar to the descendants of Lot as an inheritance.’’

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ הַפְּשָׁט "נֹגַהּ" מַשְׁמָע דְּמַזְהִיר קְצָת, וּבַזֹּהַר וַיַּקְהֵל (רג עַמּוּד ב) דְּאֵין לְבַר נָשׁ לִדְחַיָּיא וּלְאַנְהָגָא קְלָנָא, עַיֵּין שָׁם;
connections.quote: ‘‘And a fire flaring up’—for the fire of harsh judgment never departs from it. ‘And brightness around it’—although all this is present in it, brightness is around it. From here we learn that even though this side is nothing but the side of impurity, brightness is around it, and a person should not push it outside. Why? Because ‘brightness is around it’: the holy side of faith is present in it, and it should not be treated with contempt. Therefore it must be given a share in the holy side of faith.’

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַחֲטָאִים כַּשָּׁנִים הַסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְרֵאשִׁית, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּשַׁבָּת (פט:) "וְכַשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ", וּבֶאֱמֶת סָבִיב מִצַּד הָאוֹר מַקִּיף יֵשׁ לוֹ נֹגַהּ, וְאֵין לִדְחַיָּיא, רַק לִרְאוֹת לְאִתְהַפְּכָא מִנֶּגַע לְעֹנֶג, וּלְהַשִּׂיג הַנֹּגַהּ דְּסָבִיב, שֶׁהוּא מִצַּד שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַנֶּעְלָם דְּיֵצֶר שֶׁהוּא "טוֹב מְאֹד",
connections.quote: see note 1017 (Vol. I).

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קלח עַמּוּד א) דְּעַל יְדֵי הַיֵּצֶר חֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא גַּם כֵּן.
connections.quote: see note 1592 (Vol. I).
connections.context: The actual source is Midrash HaNe’elam, Zohar I 138a, cataloged as Toldot 6:57. Its expression is “the joy of Torah learning”; Rav Tzadok describes this as the desire or sweetness of Torah. In the surrounding discussion the inclination’s future form retains its constructive energy while losing its power to cause sin. This is the basis for seeing a positive root within the inclination.

connections.hePhrase: וּמַדְרֵגַת יְחִידָה שֶׁבַּיֵּצֶר הוּא מִן הַצַּד שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בּוֹרְאוֹ, הוּא כִּמְשַׁל הַזּוֹנָה הַמּוּזְכָּר בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, קסג עַמּוּד א) שֶׁגַּם הוּא עוֹשֶׂה רְצוֹן קוֹנוֹ וּמְיוּחָד בַּאֲמִיתַּת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ.
connections.quote: “Rather, it certainly performs its Master’s will. A king had an only son whom he loved greatly. Out of love, he commanded him not to approach an evil woman, for whoever approached her would be unworthy to enter the king’s palace. The son agreed lovingly to do his father’s will. Outside the king’s house there was a prostitute, beautiful in appearance. One day the king said: I wish to see my son’s devotion to me. He called the prostitute and said: Go and tempt my son, so that I may see his devotion to me. What did she do? She followed the king’s son and began embracing and kissing him and tempting him with many enticements. If the son is upright and obeys his father’s command, he rebukes her, does not heed her, and pushes her away. Then his father rejoices in his son, brings him within the curtain of his palace, and gives him gifts, presents, and great honor. Who brought all this honor to the son? Say: That prostitute. Does she deserve praise for this, or not? Certainly she deserves praise in every respect: first, because she performed the king’s command; second, because she brought the son all that good and all the king’s love for him. Therefore it is written, “Behold, it was very good”: “good” is the angel of life; “very” is the angel of death, which is indeed very good for one who obeys his Master’s commands. Come and see: Without this accuser, the righteous would not inherit the supernal treasures they are destined to inherit in the World to Come.”
connections.context: The king wills the test, while the son fulfills the king’s command by resisting the temptation. The woman serves the king through her assigned role. This distinction explains Rav Tzadok’s claim that, at the level of its divine origin, even the inclination serves its Creator. It does not turn yielding to the inclination into obedience to the command.

connections.hePhrase: זֶהוּ "מִתּוֹכָהּ כְּעֵין הַחַשְׁמַל" (יְחֶזְקֵאל א, ד), שֶׁהוּא חַיּוֹת וְכוּלֵי (חֲגִיגָה יג סוֹף עַמּוּד ב), דְּמֵאֲמִיתַּת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְדִבּוּרוֹ נִתְהַוָּה זֶה.
connections.quote: “What is chashmal? Rav Yehudah said: Living creatures of fire that speak. A baraita teaches: At times they are silent, and at times they speak. When speech issues from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, they are silent; when speech does not issue from His mouth, they speak.”
connections.context: The explanation begins at the end of 13a and continues at the beginning of 13b. It connects the living creatures with divine speech, which is the connection Rav Tzadok develops here.

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר שָׁם (פ עַמּוּד א) דְּה' קוֹלוֹת דְּהַר סִינַי הֵם נֶגֶד ה' דַּרְגִּין דִּיחֶזְקֵאל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רכ"ח, דְּהֵם נַרַנְחַ"י דְּסִטְרָא אָחֳרָא.
connections.quote: “It was taught: Rabbi Yose son of Rabbi Yehudah said: Here Israel saw what Ezekiel son of Buzi did not see, and all of them attached themselves to precious supernal wisdom. Israel saw five levels of voices at Mount Sinai, and through these five levels the Torah was given. The fifth level is that of which it is written, “The sound of the shofar.” Corresponding to them, Ezekiel saw five levels outside these: a storm wind, a great cloud, flashing fire, brightness around it, and the appearance of ḥashmal.”

connections.hePhrase: וְשָׁמַעְתִּי דְּקוֹלוֹת דְּמַתַּן תּוֹרָה הַיְינוּ מִפִּיּוֹת בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, דְּאֵין קוֹל בָּעוֹלָם זוּלַת מֵה' מוֹצָאוֹת הַפֶּה, וְנֶאֱמַר: "נַפְשִׁי יָצְאָה בְדַבְּרוֹ וְגוֹמֵר" (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים ה, ו), שֶׁכָּלְלוּ כָּל חֶלְקֵי נַפְשׁוֹתָם לַהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ אָז.
connections.quote: see note 2763.
connections.context: Rav Tzadok applies “my soul went out when he spoke” to Israel’s response at Sinai: the people gathered all the powers of their souls toward God.

connections.hePhrase: וְעַיֵּין שָׁם דַּף צ' עַמּוּד א דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת הֵם חָמֵשׁ גּוֹ חָמֵשׁ, עַיֵּין שָׁם, וּבְרֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב דְּהֵם נֶגֶד ה' קָלִין הַנִּזְכָּרִים.
connections.quote: “These first five include the other five. Therefore it is written, “From His right hand, a fiery law for them,” for all becomes the right. For this reason the Torah was given through five voices. Rabbi Yehudah said: They were all five within five; corresponding to them are the five books of the Torah.”

connections.hePhrase: וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה וְגוֹמֵר" נֶאֱמַר עַל מַחְשֶׁבֶת הַלֵּב כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָרַמְבַּ"ם (פֶּרֶק א מֵהִלְכוֹת יְסוֹדֵי הַתּוֹרָה), הַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מְבוֹרָר בִּלְבָבְךָ אֲמִיתַּת כֹּחַ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְהַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ בְּכָל דָּבָר, עַד שֶׁלֹּא יַעֲלֶה בְּלִבְּךָ שָׁלְטָנוּת שׁוּם כֹּחַ אַחֵר.
connections.displayRef: Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah 1:6
connections.linkedRef: Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah 1:6
connections.canonicalRef: Mishneh Torah, Foundations of the Torah 1:6
connections.heRef: משנה תורה, הלכות יסודי התורה א׳:ו׳
connections.quote: “Knowing this is a positive commandment, as it is stated: “I am the Lord your God.” Anyone who entertains the thought that there is another god besides Him violates a negative commandment, as it is stated: “You shall have no other gods before Me.” He denies the fundamental principle, for this is the great foundation on which everything depends.”

connections.hePhrase: וְנֶגְדּוֹ "לֹא תִגְנֹב", כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כב) בְּקַיִן: כְּגוֹנֵב דַּעַת הָעֶלְיוֹנָה, שֶׁהַמִּתְחַכֵּם בְּחָכְמַת דְּהַבְלֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה וּלְהַשְׁכִּיחַ מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ – זֶה נִקְרָא גַּנָּב הַמִּתְחַבֵּא מִבַּעַל הַבָּיִת.
connections.quote: ““Cain went out from before the Lord”: Rabbi Yudan said in the name of Rabbi Aivu: He cast the words behind him and went out, like one stealing the knowledge of the Most High. Rabbi Berakhiah said in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon: He went out as one who deceives his Creator.”
connections.context: The Midrash describes Cain attempting to evade or deceive the divine Judge. Rav Tzadok uses its phrase “stealing knowledge” for the person who imagines that inward thoughts can be hidden from God. The section is 22:13.

connections.hePhrase: וּבִשְׁלֹשָׁה אֵלּוּ פָּסֵיק טַעֲמָא דְּאִסּוּר וְשָׁרֵי כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, צג עַמּוּד ב), הַיְינוּ מִשּׁוּם דַּעֲדַיִן לֹא הִשִּׂיג לְאוֹר מַקִּיף לִהְיוֹת כָּל מַעֲשָׂיו וּמַחְשְׁבוֹתָיו בִּלְתִּי לַה' לְבַדּוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא יִכָּנֵס הָרָע כְּלָל גַּם בִּדְבַר הָרְשׁוּת שֶׁהוּא קְלִיפַּת נֹגַהּ,
connections.quote: ““You shall not murder; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not steal.” The cantillation makes a pause after “not” in all three. Without the pause there would be no remedy, and it would be forbidden to take a life at all, even where a person had transgressed the Torah. Because there is a pause, there is a forbidden form and a permitted form. “You shall not commit adultery”: without the pause, even having children or rejoicing with one’s wife in the joy of a mitzvah would be forbidden. Because there is a pause, there is a forbidden form and a permitted form. “You shall not steal”: without the pause, it would be forbidden even to “steal” the mind of one’s teacher in Torah, or of a sage, in order to gain understanding from him; or for a judge deciding a case according to the claims to outwit the deceiver, and both litigants, in order to bring the judgment to light. Because there is a pause, there is a forbidden form and a permitted form.”
connections.context: Pasqa ta’ama refers here to a pause in the cantillation after lo, “not.” The Zohar reads this pause as distinguishing the prohibited act from a different, permitted application of the same general capacity: lawful judgment, marital intimacy, or discerning understanding. The murder example concerns the Torah’s judicial framework, not permission for private violence. Rav Tzadok uses the contrast of forbidden and permitted as an image of a spiritual stage in which ordinary permitted activity has not yet become wholly devoted to Hashem. The relevant passage is Zohar II 93b.

connections.hePhrase: שֶׁהֲרֵי אֲפִילּוּ מִי שֶׁשִּׂיחָה תַּעֲנוּג לוֹ, מְפוֹרָשׁ בְּשֻׁלְחָן עָרוּךְ (אֹרַח חַיִּים סִימָן שז סָעִיף א) דְּהִיא מִכְּלַל עֹנֶג שַׁבָּת.
connections.quote: ‘Laws of Shabbat relating to speech, in twenty-two sections. ‘Speaking a word’—your speech on Shabbat should not be like your speech on a weekday. It is therefore forbidden to say, ‘I will do this particular thing tomorrow,’ or ‘I will buy this particular merchandise tomorrow.’ It is forbidden even to engage excessively in idle conversation. Gloss: People who take pleasure in recounting news and novel matters may recount them on Shabbat as on a weekday. But someone who does not take pleasure in them may not recount them so that his companion will enjoy them (Terumat HaDeshen, section 61).’

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ "מַתָּנָה טוֹבָה יֵשׁ לִי וְכוּלֵי" (שַׁבָּת י:), כִּי דָּבָר זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה לוֹ דִּמְיוֹן, רַק מֵעֵזֶר הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וּמִמַּתְּנָתוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רכ"ז.
connections.quote: “Rava bar Mahseya said in the name of Rav Hama bar Gurya, in the name of Rav: ‘Someone who gives a gift to his fellow must let him know, as it is stated: ‘To know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.’’ It was also taught thus: ‘‘To know that I am Hashem who sanctifies you.’ The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: ‘I have a good gift in My treasury, called Shabbat, and I wish to give it to Israel. Go and tell them.’’ From here Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said: ‘Someone who gives bread to a child must let his mother know.’ What does he do for the child? Abaye said: ‘He rubs him with oil and applies kohl to him.’ And now that we are concerned about witchcraft, what should he do? Rav Pappa said: ‘He smears him with some of that same food.’”

connections.hePhrase: וְנֶגְדּוֹ "לֹא תַעֲנֶה [בְרֵעֲךָ עֵד שָׁקֶר]", כִּי לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נָקִי בָּזֶה דְּ"אִישׁ אֶת רָעַת רֵעֵהוּ אַל תַּחְשְׁבוּ בִּלְבַבְכֶם" (זְכַרְיָה ח, יז), דִּבְלָאו הָכִי לֹא יִמָּלֵט מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת שֶׁאֲחֵרִים מוֹלִידִים בּוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רי"ט.
connections.quote: ‘Do not devise evil against one another in your hearts, and do not love a false oath, for all these are things I hate, declares Hashem.’

connections.hePhrase: וְנֶגְדּוֹ "לֹא תַעֲנֶה [בְרֵעֲךָ עֵד שָׁקֶר]", כִּי לְהַשִּׂיג זֶה צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה נָקִי בָּזֶה דְּ"אִישׁ אֶת רָעַת רֵעֵהוּ אַל תַּחְשְׁבוּ בִּלְבַבְכֶם" (זְכַרְיָה ח, יז), דִּבְלָאו הָכִי לֹא יִמָּלֵט מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת שֶׁאֲחֵרִים מוֹלִידִים בּוֹ כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל אוֹת רי"ט.
connections.quote: “Therefore, my beloved friends, please, please labor with all your heart and soul to implant love of your fellow in your heart. It is written: “Let none of you think evil of his fellow in your hearts.” Let it never enter the heart; and if it does enter, push it from the heart as smoke is driven away, just as one would a thought of idolatry itself.”

connections.hePhrase: וּלְכָךְ בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל בַּתְּחִלָּה: "וְכִפֶּר בַּעֲדוֹ... וּבְעַד בֵּיתוֹ" (וַיִּקְרָא טז, יא) הַקּוֹדֵם, שֶׁמּוֹלִידִים תֹּקֶף הִרְהוּרִים וּמַחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת בְּקִרְבּוֹ;
connections.quote: ‘Aaron shall bring forward his own bull for a sin offering and make atonement for himself and for his household. He shall slaughter his own bull for a sin offering.’

connections.hePhrase: וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּעַד אֶחָיו הַמְקוֹרָבִים לוֹ גַּם כֵּן מוֹלִידִים יוֹתֵר;
connections.quote: ““He shall make atonement for himself,” and so forth: A second confession, for himself and for his fellow priests, all of whom are called his household, as it is stated: “House of Aaron, bless the Lord.” From here we learn that the priests receive atonement through it. Their atonement through it concerns only impurity involving the Sanctuary and its sacred offerings, as it is stated: “He shall make atonement for the sacred place from the impurities,” and so forth.”

connections.hePhrase: וְאַחַר כָּךְ "כַּבֵּד אֶת אָבִיךָ וְאֶת אִמָּךְ" (שְׁמוֹת כ, יב), כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי פֵּירוּשׁ: דְּאַבָּא וְאִימָּא יָדוּעַ דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא תִּדְחֶה שִׂכְלְךָ וּרְצוֹנְךָ גַּם כֵּן.
connections.quote: ‘Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be prolonged upon the land that Hashem your God is giving you.’

connections.hePhrase: וְאַחַר כָּךְ "כַּבֵּד אֶת אָבִיךָ וְאֶת אִמָּךְ" (שְׁמוֹת כ, יב), כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי פֵּירוּשׁ: דְּאַבָּא וְאִימָּא יָדוּעַ דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא תִּדְחֶה שִׂכְלְךָ וּרְצוֹנְךָ גַּם כֵּן.
connections.displayRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Exodus, Yitro 14
connections.canonicalRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume II, Exodus, Yitro 14
connections.quote: ““Honor your father and your mother.” It is stated in the holy Zohar, Kedoshim 82a, that father and mother allude to the thought in the head and the will in the heart. This is why God commanded us to honor them: if a person knows within himself that he is very thoroughly clarified, without any self-interest, then he should not reject his own thought and will, but honor them.”

connections.hePhrase: וְאַחַר כָּךְ "כַּבֵּד אֶת אָבִיךָ וְאֶת אִמָּךְ" (שְׁמוֹת כ, יב), כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי פֵּירוּשׁ: דְּאַבָּא וְאִימָּא יָדוּעַ דְּרָצָה לוֹמַר מוֹחָא וְלִבָּא, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא תִּדְחֶה שִׂכְלְךָ וּרְצוֹנְךָ גַּם כֵּן.
connections.displayRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:22
connections.canonicalRef: Beit Yaakov on Torah, Lech Lecha 14:22
connections.quote: ““Take for Me a threefold heifer” corresponds to honoring father and mother. Honoring father and mother is placed beside Shabbos to teach that if a person errs in the clarification of his handiwork, which is called Shabbos, its repair stands beside it: fulfilling the honoring of father and mother, so that he repairs the deficiency implanted in him from birth, from the root of father and mother. How does he repair it? Through the service he performs, he will perceive meaning even at this depth. This is what the sacrificial services signify: a person dedicates all his deeds to Hashem and afterward receives them from the table on high.”
connections.explanation: Beit Yaakov likewise reads the adjacency of these commandments as repair reaching beyond one’s present acts toward what was received at birth. This helps explain Rav Tzadok’s extension of the commandment to the mind and heart from which a person’s actions are born. The developmental sequence is directed toward dedicating those actions to Hashem and then receiving them anew as a gift.
connections.headline: Kibbud av va’em and repair reaching back to one’s root

connections.hePhrase: וּבִפְשָׁטֵיהּ אָב וָאֵם גַּם כֵּן, כְּטַעַם (סַנְהֶדְרִין קד.): בְּרָא מְזַכֵּי אַבָּא, וְהַיְינוּ כַּאֲשֶׁר מַגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ שֶׁמִּזְדַּכֵּךְ שׁוֹרֶשׁ שָׁרְשׁוֹ הָעֶלְיוֹן, גַּם הַחֵטְא דִּתְחִלַּת בְּרִיאָתוֹ וְ"יֶחֱמַתְנִי אִמִּי" נִתְקָן, וְגַם אָב וָאֵם נִזְדַּכְּכוּ וְהוּא מְכַבְּדָם.
connections.quote: “Why was Amon not included in the list? Out of respect for Josiah. Then Manasseh, too, should not have been included, out of respect for Hezekiah! A son can confer merit upon his father, but a father cannot confer merit upon his son, as it is written, ‘None can rescue from My hand.’ Abraham cannot rescue Ishmael, and Isaac cannot rescue Esau. Now that we have reached this explanation, Ahaz, too, was omitted out of respect for Hezekiah.”

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִדּוּשִׁין לא.): דְּעוֹבְדֵי כּוֹכָבִים הוֹדוּ לָזֶה, וְהַיְינוּ דְּהֵם אוֹמְרִים "כֹּחִי וְעֹצֶם יָדִי" וְשֶׁהַכֹּל בִּידֵי אָדָם וְלֹא בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם, רַק בְּשֵׂכֶל הָאָדָם וּבִינָתוֹ;
connections.quote: “And you say in your heart: My power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth.”

connections.hePhrase: וְיִשְׂרָאֵל מְצַפִּים לְעֶזְרַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, רַק לְבַסּוֹף הוּא "תּוֹרָתוֹ" (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט.) וְ"הָאָרֶץ נָתַן לִבְנֵי אָדָם", זֶהוּ מַדְרֵגָה חֲמִישִׁית דְּ"כַּבֵּד".
connections.quote: ‘Rava also said: At first, the Torah is called by the name of the Holy One, blessed be He; in the end, it is called by the learner’s own name, as it is said: ‘His desire is in Hashem’s Torah,’ and ‘In his Torah he meditates day and night.’’

connections.hePhrase: עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וְאָמְרוּ רַק עַם חָכָם וְנָבוֹן הַגּוֹי הַגָּדוֹל הַזֶּה" (דְּבָרִים ד, ו), שֶׁיּוֹדוּ עַל חָכְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד עַצְמָם, כְּעִנְיַן שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ, שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לָדוּן בְּלֹא עֵדִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כא:), רַק כְּעִנְיַן מָשִׁיחַ דִּ"מוֹרַח וְדָאֵין" (סַנְהֶדְרִין צג:), שֶׁמַּעֲמִיד עַל חָכְמָתוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁכֵּן הוּא הָאֱמֶת גַּם בְּחָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
connections.quote: ‘You shall keep them and do them, for this is your wisdom and understanding in the eyes of the peoples. When they hear all these statutes, they will say: ‘Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.’’

connections.hePhrase: עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וְאָמְרוּ רַק עַם חָכָם וְנָבוֹן הַגּוֹי הַגָּדוֹל הַזֶּה" (דְּבָרִים ד, ו), שֶׁיּוֹדוּ עַל חָכְמַת יִשְׂרָאֵל מִצַּד עַצְמָם, כְּעִנְיַן שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְמַדְרֵגָה זוֹ, שֶׁבִּקֵּשׁ לָדוּן בְּלֹא עֵדִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה כא:), רַק כְּעִנְיַן מָשִׁיחַ דִּ"מוֹרַח וְדָאֵין" (סַנְהֶדְרִין צג:), שֶׁמַּעֲמִיד עַל חָכְמָתוֹ וּרְצוֹנוֹ שֶׁכֵּן הוּא הָאֱמֶת גַּם בְּחָכְמַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ,
connections.quote: “Concerning the Messiah, it is written: “The spirit of Hashem shall rest upon him—a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and fear of Hashem”; and it is written, “His scent shall be in the fear of Hashem.” Rabbi Alexandri said: This teaches that He loaded him with commandments and afflictions like millstones. Rava said: He perceives by scent and judges, as it is written, “He shall not judge by what his eyes see,” and “He shall judge the poor with righteousness and decide equitably for the humble of the land.””
connections.context: Rava’s interpretation gives the exact expression “perceives by scent and judges.” Rav Tzadok uses this as the model of judgment through inward spiritual discernment, following his discussion of Solomon.

connections.hePhrase: וְנֶגְדּוֹ "לֹא תַחְמֹד", דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהִשִּׂיג הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ הַחֵשֶׁק בְּמַדְרֵגַת הַחַשְׁמַל, דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא מַלְאָךְ קָדוֹשׁ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא: שְׁמוֹ לָבָן, דְּאִתְלַבַּן וְכוּלֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קלז עַמּוּד ב), שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לַחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא.
connections.quote: “Rav Huna said: This is the evil inclination and its two daughters, changed from what they were at first. At first it was Lot, cursed and defiled; now it is Lavan, whitened, no longer cursed and defiled in its former filth.”

connections.hePhrase: וְנֶגְדּוֹ "לֹא תַחְמֹד", דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהִשִּׂיג הַיֵּצֶר שֶׁשָּׁרְשׁוֹ הַחֵשֶׁק בְּמַדְרֵגַת הַחַשְׁמַל, דְּהַיְינוּ מִצַּד שֶׁהוּא מַלְאָךְ קָדוֹשׁ, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא: שְׁמוֹ לָבָן, דְּאִתְלַבַּן וְכוּלֵי, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרַשׁ הַנֶּעֱלָם (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א, קלז עַמּוּד ב), שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לַחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא.
connections.quote: “He said to him: By your life, the evil inclination is needed by the world as rain is needed by the world. Were it not for the evil inclination, the joy of Torah learning would not exist. But it will no longer be debased as formerly, so that one sins through it.”
connections.context: Midrash HaNe’elam, Zohar I 137b, plays on Lavan and melubban: white and whitened. The preceding symbolic Lot represents the inclination while defiled, and Lavan represents its future purification. The continuation on I 138a explains why the force itself remains: it gives joy to Torah learning. Rav Tzadok joins these two statements when describing desire purified into longing for Torah. These are allegorical names for the inclination, rather than an endorsement of the biblical Lavan.

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, צג עַמּוּד ב) דְּחָשֵׁיב פְּרָטִין בְּלֹא תַחְמֹד, דַּחֲמִידוּ דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא מוּתָּר;
connections.quote: “Likewise, in “You shall not covet” there is no cantillation pause at all. If you say: Since there is no pause, perhaps even desire for Torah is forbidden—come and see. In the other commandments the Torah speaks generally, but here it gives particulars: “your fellow’s house, his field, and his servant,” and so forth—all worldly matters. Torah, however, is always to be desired: delights, treasures of life, and length of days in this world and in the world to come.”
connections.context: The source explains that the prohibition specifies worldly objects; longing for Torah remains desirable. Rav Tzadok applies this distinction to an inclination so purified that its desire is directed entirely toward Torah.

connections.hePhrase: וְנִסְתַּלֵּק קֻשְׁיַת רַבִּי אַבְרָהָם בֶּן עֶזְרָא: אֵיךְ שַׁיָּיךְ לָאו עַל חֶמְדָּה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם?
connections.quote: “So every understanding person should know that a beautiful wife or wealth will not come to a person through his own wisdom and knowledge, but according to what the Lord has allotted him. Kohelet says, “To a person who did not labor for it, he shall give it as his portion.” The sages said: Children, life, and sustenance depend not on merit but on mazal. For this reason the understanding person will neither desire nor covet. Once he knows that God has forbidden his fellow’s wife to him, she is further beyond his reach than a princess is in the villager’s eyes. He will therefore rejoice in his portion and will not set his heart on coveting and desiring what is not his, for he knows that what God did not wish to give him he cannot take by his strength, thoughts, or schemes. He will therefore trust his Creator to sustain him and do what is good in His eyes.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהֵם ד' מַדְרֵגוֹת שָׂרִים שֶׁחָשַׁב יִתְרוֹ נֶגֶד ד' מַעֲלוֹת שֶׁזָּכַר:
connections.quote: ‘You shall select from all the people capable men who fear God, men of truth who hate unjust gain. Place them over the people as leaders of thousands, leaders of hundreds, leaders of fifties, and leaders of tens.’

connections.hePhrase: "אַנְשֵׁי אֱמֶת" – אֵין אֱמֶת אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה פְּתִיחַת אֵיכָה), וְתַלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים הַמְחַדְּשִׁים חִדּוּשִׁין דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא בְּכָל יוֹם נִקְרְאוּ אַנְשֵׁי אֱמֶת, שֶׁהֵם אֲנָשִׁים לָאֱמֶת.
connections.quote: ““Truth” means Torah, as it is stated: “Acquire truth and do not sell it.””

connections.hePhrase: "וְשׂנְאֵי בָצַע" – פֵּירוּשׁ נְקִיִּים מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת, שֶׁכָּל דִּמְיוֹנוֹת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה מַה שֶּׁחוּץ לַתּוֹרָה נִקְרָא בֶּצַע, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "הַט [לִבִּי אֶל עֵדְוֹתֶיךָ] וְאַל אֶל בָּצַע" (תְּהִלִּים קיט, לו).
connections.quote: ‘Incline my heart toward Your testimonies, and not toward gain.’

connections.hePhrase: וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכַר אַחַר כָּךְ רַק "אֲנָשִׁים חֲכָמִים" (דְּבָרִים א, טו), וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין ק:) דִּנְבוֹנִים לֹא אִשְׁתֲּכַח.
connections.quote: “I took the heads of your tribes, wise and known men, and appointed them as heads over you: officers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and officials for your tribes.”
connections.context: The appointment is reported in verse 15, which mentions wise and known men but omits the “understanding” men requested in verse 13. That omission is the basis of Eruvin 100b and of Rav Tzadok’s distinction.

connections.hePhrase: וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכַר אַחַר כָּךְ רַק "אֲנָשִׁים חֲכָמִים" (דְּבָרִים א, טו), וְהַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין ק:) דִּנְבוֹנִים לֹא אִשְׁתֲּכַח.
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: A woman who seeks marital relations with her husband will have sons whose like did not exist even in Moses’ generation. For concerning Moses’ generation it is written: ‘Provide for yourselves men who are wise, understanding, and known to your tribes,’ and it is written: ‘I took the heads of your tribes, men who were wise and known.’ But men of understanding he did not find.’

connections.hePhrase: וְיָדוּעַ בִּינָה לִבָּא, שֶׁהוּא הַהַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב, וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְלֹא נָתַן ה' לָכֶם לֵב לָדַעַת וְגוֹמֵר עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" (שָׁם כט, ג), כִּי לֹא נִגְאֲלוּ אֶלָּא בִּזְכוּת הָאֱמוּנָה.
connections.quote: “Yet the Lord has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, until this day.”

connections.hePhrase: וְיָדוּעַ בִּינָה לִבָּא, שֶׁהוּא הַהַרְגָּשָׁה בַּלֵּב, וְנֶאֱמַר: "וְלֹא נָתַן ה' לָכֶם לֵב לָדַעַת וְגוֹמֵר עַד הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה" (שָׁם כט, ג), כִּי לֹא נִגְאֲלוּ אֶלָּא בִּזְכוּת הָאֱמוּנָה.
connections.quote: “So too, you find that our ancestors were redeemed from Egypt only through the merit of the faith with which they believed, as it is stated: “The people believed.” It also says: “The Lord preserves the faithful.””

connections.hePhrase: וְעָשָׂה מֵהֶם כָּל הַשָּׂרִים, כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת גַּם מַדְרֵגַת הַמֶּלֶךְ שֶׁהוּא לְמַעְלָה מִכָּל הַשָּׂרִים וְהוּא נֶגֶד מַדְרֵגַת יְחִידָה, הֲרֵי דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם הָיָה דַּרְגָּא דְּנֶפֶשׁ לְבַד כַּנּוֹדָע בַּזֹּהַר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים.
connections.quote: ““He restores my soul”: this is the nefesh of David. David sought to set right only that level of his, as was fitting.”

connections.hePhrase: וּבַזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (פב עַמּוּד א) דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת הֵם מְכֻוָּונוֹת נֶגֶד ה' דַּרְגִּין לִימִינָא וְה' לִשְׂמָאלָא הַנִּזְכָּר בְּפָרָשַׁת "אַתֶּם נִצָּבִים": "רָאשֵׁיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים כט, ט), מְבוֹאָרִים נֶגֶד ה' מַעֲלוֹת בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנִּזְכָּר:
connections.quote: ‘For it was taught: They all stood row upon row, each within their bounds, and each saw what was fitting for them. Rabbi Shimon said: The heads of the people were by themselves, the heads of the tribes by themselves, and the women by themselves. Five levels were on the right and five levels on the left. This is what is written: ‘You stand today, all of you, before Hashem your God: your heads, your tribes, your elders, your officers, every man,’ and so forth (Deuteronomy 29:9). These are five levels on the right. Who are the five levels on the left? This is what is written: ‘Your little ones, your wives, and your stranger who is within your camp, from the hewer of your wood to the drawer of your water’ (Deuteronomy 29). These are five levels on the left.’

connections.hePhrase: וּבַזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (פב עַמּוּד א) דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת הֵם מְכֻוָּונוֹת נֶגֶד ה' דַּרְגִּין לִימִינָא וְה' לִשְׂמָאלָא הַנִּזְכָּר בְּפָרָשַׁת "אַתֶּם נִצָּבִים": "רָאשֵׁיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים כט, ט), מְבוֹאָרִים נֶגֶד ה' מַעֲלוֹת בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנִּזְכָּר:
connections.quote: ‘You are standing today, all of you, before Hashem your God: your tribal leaders, your elders, your officers, every man of Israel.’

connections.hePhrase: וּבַזֹּהַר יִתְרוֹ (פב עַמּוּד א) דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַדִּבְּרוֹת הֵם מְכֻוָּונוֹת נֶגֶד ה' דַּרְגִּין לִימִינָא וְה' לִשְׂמָאלָא הַנִּזְכָּר בְּפָרָשַׁת "אַתֶּם נִצָּבִים": "רָאשֵׁיכֶם וְגוֹמֵר" (דְּבָרִים כט, ט), מְבוֹאָרִים נֶגֶד ה' מַעֲלוֹת בְּהַשָּׂגַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הַנִּזְכָּר:
connections.quote: “This is ‘your heads, your tribes … from your woodcutter to your water-drawer.’ A complete stature is counted here, from the greatest in Israel to the least. Where a complete stature is present, a person recognizes that every individual fulfills His will. This resembles the teaching that Yiftach in his generation is like Shmuel in his generation: one who proceeds in divine service recognizes that each fulfills the will and purpose Hashem seeks from him.”
connections.explanation: Tiferet Yosef interprets the same list used in this siman, from the leaders through the woodcutters and water-drawers. It emphasizes that the completed stature includes each member's particular service. This helps distinguish the present classification of spiritual capacities and appointments from the separate question of belonging to the covenantal whole; one member's role need not be identical to another's for both to participate in its completion.
connections.headline: The different members still form one complete stature

connections.hePhrase: וְזָקֵן – שֶׁקָּנָה חָכְמָה;
connections.quote: “The Rabbis taught: “Before gray hair you shall rise”—could this mean even before an ignorant elder? Scripture therefore says “elder,” and “elder” means a sage, as it is stated: “Gather for Me seventy men of the elders of Israel.” Rabbi Yose the Galilean says: “Elder” means one who has acquired wisdom, as it is stated: “The Lord acquired me at the beginning of His way.””

connections.hePhrase: וְלִשְׂמָאלָא הַיְינוּ בְּהַרְחָקַת הָרָע: "טַף" הוּא שֶׁאֵין לוֹ דַּעַת וְחֶמְדָּה דְּיֵצֶר כְּלָל;
connections.quote: “Your little ones, your wives, and your stranger who is in the midst of your camp, from the hewer of your wood to the drawer of your water.”

connections.hePhrase: וְנָשִׁים – הֲגַם דְּנֶאֱמַר: "אִשָּׁה בְכָל אֵלֶּה לֹא מָצָאתִי" (קֹהֶלֶת ז, כח), פֵּירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ הָאָדָם אֶחָד מֵאֶלֶף, דְּהַיְינוּ שַׂר הָאֶלֶף שֶׁהוּא שׂוֹנְאֵי בָצַע, לִהְיוֹת נָקִי מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת לְגַמְרֵי, כִּי זֶה אִי אֶפְשָׁר רַק עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּנָשִׁים
connections.quote: ‘What my soul still sought, I did not find. One man among a thousand I found, but a woman among all these I did not find.’

connections.hePhrase: מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יז.): הָנֵי נָשֵׁי בְּמַאי זָכְיָין? בְּאַקְרוֹיֵי וְכוּלֵי, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּכֹחָהּ לְהִתְבַּטֵּל לְגַבֵּי הַבַּעַל וְהַבֵּן וּמְבַטֶּלֶת רְצוֹנָהּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ט): אֵיזוֹ אִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁרָה? שֶׁעוֹשָׂה וְכוּלֵי.
connections.quote: “Rav said to Rabbi Hiyya: ‘Through what do women gain merit?’ Through having their children read in the synagogue, having their husbands study in the house of the Sages, and waiting for their husbands until they return from the house of the Sages. When the Sages took leave of Rabbi Ami’s house—and some say Rabbi Hanina’s house—they would say to him: ‘May you see your world in your lifetime, and may your end be the life of the World to Come, and your hope endure for generations upon generations. May your heart ponder understanding, your mouth speak wisdom, and your tongue utter songs. May your eyes look straight before you, your eyes shine with the light of Torah, and your face radiate like the brightness of the firmament. May your lips pour forth knowledge, your inner parts rejoice in uprightness, and your steps run to hear the words of the Ancient of Days.’”

connections.hePhrase: מִכָּל מָקוֹם אָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת יז.): הָנֵי נָשֵׁי בְּמַאי זָכְיָין? בְּאַקְרוֹיֵי וְכוּלֵי, וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּכֹחָהּ לְהִתְבַּטֵּל לְגַבֵּי הַבַּעַל וְהַבֵּן וּמְבַטֶּלֶת רְצוֹנָהּ מִפְּנֵיהֶם, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (תַּנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק ט): אֵיזוֹ אִשָּׁה כְּשֵׁרָה? שֶׁעוֹשָׂה וְכוּלֵי.
connections.quote: “The sages said: Jael was a worthy woman, and she did her husband’s will. From here the sages said: A worthy woman among women is one who does her husband’s will.”
connections.context: The immediate example is Jael, not Jezebel. Rav Tzadok uses the stated quality of setting aside one’s own will in his explanation of the relationship described here.

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ב, לט עַמּוּד ב) דִּבְכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ זָכָר וּנְקֵבָה הַכֹּל נִקְרָא עַל שֵׁם הַדְּכוּרָא, כִּי הִיא בְּטֵלָה לְגַבֵּיהּ, וְעַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ הַבִּיטּוּל הֲרֵי בְּכֹחָהּ לְסַלֵּק עַצְמָהּ מִכֹּל וָכֹל.
connections.quote: see note 2727.
connections.context: The grammatical example illustrates the union of the masculine and feminine aspects under one designation. Rav Tzadok applies this symbolic principle to the self-nullification he is describing.

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת: "אוֹת הִוא בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם" (שְׁמוֹת לא, יג) לְבַד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר פָּרָשַׁת וַיַּקְהֵל (רג עַמּוּד א) דְּאַפֵּיק עֵרֶב רַב מִבֵּינַיְיהוּ בִּנְתִינַת שַׁבָּת.
connections.quote: ‘You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying: ‘You must nevertheless keep My Shabbatot, for it is a sign between Me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am Hashem, who sanctifies you.’’

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת: "אוֹת הִוא בֵּינִי וּבֵינֵיכֶם" (שְׁמוֹת לא, יג) לְבַד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר פָּרָשַׁת וַיַּקְהֵל (רג עַמּוּד א) דְּאַפֵּיק עֵרֶב רַב מִבֵּינַיְיהוּ בִּנְתִינַת שַׁבָּת.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Yitzchak then began: “Moses assembled all the congregation of the children of Israel.” Why did he assemble them? To give them Shabbat as before. At first, before the children of Israel made the calf, he gave them Shabbat, and this was what the mixed multitude did not observe. When they heard “between Me and the children of Israel,” they said: Is this matter withheld from us? Immediately, “The people assembled around Aaron,” and many were drawn after them. After those who died had died, Moses assembled the children of Israel by themselves and gave them Shabbat as before, as it says, “Six days shall work be done.””
connections.context: The Zohar explains why Moses assembled Israel separately to receive Shabbat after the calf. The marker belongs at that Zohar citation, where Rav Tzadok states that the mixed multitude was separated out, rather than at the earlier verse alone.

connections.hePhrase: וּ"מֵחֹטֵב [עֵצֶיךָ עַד שֹׁאֵב מֵימֶיךָ]" – הֵם הַנְּתִינִים שֶׁהֵם עֲבָדִים, דְּאִיתָא כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים דִּפְרוּצִים בַּעֲבֵירוֹת וַחֲשׁוּדִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (מה:) וּבִפְסָחִים (צא סוֹף עַמּוּד א וְרֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) וּבְגִטִּין (סז:) וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת.
connections.quote: “If so, consider the latter clause: Women and slaves who wish to make a joint invitation to recite Grace may not do so. Why not, since there are distinct minds? That case is different because of sexual impropriety.”
connections.context: This is the discussion of a joint zimmun by women and slaves. Rav Tzadok cites its concern about impropriety as one of several passages concerning the moral susceptibility associated with servitude in his symbolic exposition.

connections.hePhrase: וּ"מֵחֹטֵב [עֵצֶיךָ עַד שֹׁאֵב מֵימֶיךָ]" – הֵם הַנְּתִינִים שֶׁהֵם עֲבָדִים, דְּאִיתָא כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים דִּפְרוּצִים בַּעֲבֵירוֹת וַחֲשׁוּדִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (מה:) וּבִפְסָחִים (צא סוֹף עַמּוּד א וְרֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) וּבְגִטִּין (סז:) וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת.
connections.quote: “He said to him, ‘Do we form a group consisting entirely of women? But we learned: One does not form a group of women, slaves, and minors. Does this not mean women by themselves, slaves by themselves, and minors by themselves?’ He answered, ‘No. It means women, slaves, and minors together. Women with slaves are prohibited because of lewdness; minors with slaves, because of sexual misconduct.’”

connections.hePhrase: וּ"מֵחֹטֵב [עֵצֶיךָ עַד שֹׁאֵב מֵימֶיךָ]" – הֵם הַנְּתִינִים שֶׁהֵם עֲבָדִים, דְּאִיתָא כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים דִּפְרוּצִים בַּעֲבֵירוֹת וַחֲשׁוּדִים, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּבְרָכוֹת (מה:) וּבִפְסָחִים (צא סוֹף עַמּוּד א וְרֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) וּבְגִטִּין (סז:) וּשְׁאָר מְקוֹמוֹת.
connections.quote: “The Exilarch said to Rav Sheshet: Why does the master not dine with us? He replied: Because the servants are not reliable; they are suspected of serving a limb taken from a living animal.”
connections.context: The passage concerns Rav Sheshet’s suspicion of the Exilarch’s servants, and illustrates the specific issue for which Rav Tzadok cites this page.

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בַּמִּדְבָּר רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה טז): יֵשׁ שֶׁשְּׁמוֹתֵיהֶם כְּעוּרִים וּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם נָאִים – עוֹלֵי גוֹלָה בְּנֵי סִיסְרָא וְכוּלֵי, עַיֵּין שָׁם, וְהֵם מִן הַנְּתִינִים וּמַעֲשֵׂיהֶם נָאִים.
connections.quote: ““These were the names of the men” (Numbers 13:16). What were their names? They were “Setur son of Mikhael…Naḥbi son of Vofsi…Geuel son of Makhi” (Numbers 13:13–15). There are people whose names are pleasant but their actions are repulsive; their names are repulsive but their actions are pleasant; their names are pleasant and their actions are pleasant; their names and their actions are repulsive. Whose names are pleasant but their actions are repulsive: This is Ishmael and Esau. Ishmael – God listens [shome’a el]; Esau – he performs [oseh] the will of his Maker [osehu]. Their names are repulsive but their actions are pleasant: These are those who ascended from the exile: “The children of Barkos, the children of Sisera, the children of Tamaḥ” (Ezra 2:53). Their names are repulsive and their actions are repulsive, these are the spies: What is written in their regard? “Setur” – He eliminated him [shesetaro] from the world.”

connections.hePhrase: וְ"חֹטֵב עֵצֶיךָ" הַיְינוּ שֶׁנָּקִי בְּתַאֲוָה שֶׁבַּלֵּב, רַק שֶׁאֵין לוֹ חָכְמָה שֶׁבַּמּוֹחַ, שֶׁהֲרֵי אָסוּר לְלַמֵּד עַבְדּוֹ תּוֹרָה (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ כְּתוּבּוֹת כח.).
connections.quote: ‘And ‘that a certain man would leave the school to immerse in order to eat terumah.’ But perhaps he was a priest’s slave? This supports Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: A person is forbidden to teach his slave Torah.’

connections.hePhrase: וּמִצַּד שֶׁהוּא דְּכוּרָא וְיֵשׁ בּוֹ חָכְמָה, הוּא שׁוֹפֵעַ בּוֹ לְרַע, דְּלָכֵן אָסוּר לְלַמְּדוֹ תּוֹרָה, כְּמוֹ לְאִשָּׁה (סוֹטָה כ.) שֶׁאֵין לָהּ דַּעַת, וְזֶה יֵשׁ לוֹ רַק שֶׁהַחָכְמָה אֵינָהּ מְבוֹרֶרֶת כְּלָל בְּעֶבֶד.
connections.quote: “If she has merit, it suspends her punishment. There is merit that suspends it for one year, for two years, or for three years. From here Ben Azzai says: A person is obligated to teach his daughter Torah, so that if she drinks she will know that merit can suspend punishment. Rabbi Eliezer says: Whoever teaches his daughter Torah is as though he teaches her sexual impropriety.”
connections.context: Rav Tzadok invokes Rabbi Eliezer’s position in this Mishnah. The source also records Ben Azzai’s contrary position, which explains the immediate setting of the dispute. The quoted statement belongs to Rabbi Eliezer, not to Rabbi Yehoshua’s separate statement that follows it.

connections.hePhrase: רַק לִשְׂמָאלָא, הַיְינוּ בְּהַגְדָּרָה מֵרָע עַל כָּל פָּנִים עַל יְדֵי בִּיטּוּלָם לַטּוֹב, שֶׁבְּכֹחָם לְבַטֵּל עַצְמָם לְגַמְרֵי שֶׁלֹּא לִהְיוֹת מַהוּת בִּפְנֵי עַצְמוֹ כְּלָל, רַק נִטְפָּל לַטּוֹב, כְּעֶבֶד לָאָדוֹן, וְאִשָּׁה לְבַעְלָהּ, וּבֵן לְאָבִיו, וְגֵר לְיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכוּנֶּה, לִהְיוֹת נִטְפָּל וּבָטֵל לָאֻמָּה הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִית,
connections.quote: “Corresponding to this are “your children, your wives,” and so forth. Although they are not people engaged in Torah study, they too belong to words of Torah, since they assist the Torah. It says, “From the hewer of your wood to the drawer of your water,” instead of simply mentioning servants, for the reason we explained: holiness also exists in a person’s possessions, as with the servant of our father Abraham, and the like.”

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (סִפְרֵי בְּהַעֲלֹתְךָ סוֹף פִּסְקָא עח) שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַשֵּׁבֶט שֶׁיִּדְבַּק יוּכְלַל בּוֹ, וְהוּא הִתְכַּלְלוּת שְׂמָאלָא בִּימִינָא:
connections.quote: ““To the place of which the Lord said, ‘I will give it to you’”—converts have no share in it. How, then, do I fulfill “In the tribe with which the convert resides”? If it does not refer to inheritance, apply it to atonement: if he is in the tribe of Judah, he receives atonement with the tribe of Judah; if in the tribe of Benjamin, with the tribe of Benjamin. Another interpretation: If it does not refer to inheritance, apply it to burial; converts are granted burial in the Land of Israel. “Come with us and we will do good to you”—is there a member of a person’s household to whom one does not do good? The matter follows all the more strongly: if one does good to a member of a person’s household, how much more to a member of the household of the One who spoke and the world came into being. “For the Lord has spoken good concerning Israel”—has no good been spoken concerning Israel until now? The Lord has always spoken good concerning Israel. The Omnipresent commanded Israel to do good to converts and to treat them with humility.”

connections.hePhrase: כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר הַהוּא עַם הָאָרֶץ לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשַׁת צַו פָּרָשָׁה ט), וְכַנּוֹדָע דְּכָל אֶחָד אֲחִיזָתוֹ בְּאוֹת מֵהַתּוֹרָה, וְסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁחָסֵר אוֹת אַחַת פָּסוּל, וְאִם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁזֶּה צָרִיךְ לָזֶה, כָּךְ צָרִיךְ זֶה לָזֶה.
connections.quote: see note 1408 (Vol. I).

connections.hePhrase: כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר הַהוּא עַם הָאָרֶץ לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשַׁת צַו פָּרָשָׁה ט), וְכַנּוֹדָע דְּכָל אֶחָד אֲחִיזָתוֹ בְּאוֹת מֵהַתּוֹרָה, וְסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁחָסֵר אוֹת אַחַת פָּסוּל, וְאִם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁזֶּה צָרִיךְ לָזֶה, כָּךְ צָרִיךְ זֶה לָזֶה.

connections.heRef: משנה תורה, הלכות תפילין ומזוזה וספר תורה י׳:א׳
connections.quote: “You thus learn that there are twenty defects, any one of which invalidates a Torah scroll. If any one of them occurs in it, it is like one of the books of the Torah used to teach children: it does not have the sanctity of a Torah scroll and may not be read publicly. They are: 1. It was written on the hide of an unclean animal. 2. It was written on the hide of a clean animal that was not processed. 3. The hide was processed without the intention that it be used for a Torah scroll. 4. It was written on the wrong writing surface: on the flesh side of whole hide, or on the hair side of parchment. 5. Part of it was written on whole hide and part on parchment. 6. It was written on the inner layer of split hide. 7. It was written without ruled lines. 8. It was written without lasting black ink. 9. It was written in other languages. 10. It was written by a heretic or a similarly disqualified person. 11. The divine names were written without the proper intention. 12. Even a single letter was omitted. 13. Even a single letter was added. 14. One letter touches another. 15. The form of a single letter was spoiled so that it cannot be read at all or resembles another letter, whether in the original writing, through a hole or tear, or through smearing. 16. The space between letters was increased or decreased so that one word appears as two words, or two words as one word. 17. The arrangement of the sections was changed. 18. The arrangement of the songs was changed. 19. Other portions of the text were written in the arrangement of a song. 20. The sheets were sewn with something other than sinews of a clean animal. The remaining requirements are for proper fulfillment, but their absence does not invalidate the scroll.”

connections.hePhrase: כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר הַהוּא עַם הָאָרֶץ לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשַׁת צַו פָּרָשָׁה ט), וְכַנּוֹדָע דְּכָל אֶחָד אֲחִיזָתוֹ בְּאוֹת מֵהַתּוֹרָה, וְסֵפֶר תּוֹרָה שֶׁחָסֵר אוֹת אַחַת פָּסוּל, וְאִם כֵּן כְּמוֹ שֶׁזֶּה צָרִיךְ לָזֶה, כָּךְ צָרִיךְ זֶה לָזֶה.
connections.quote: “I dreamt that the plain meaning was this: sometimes there is contention of the kind described as “The rivalry of scholars increases wisdom” (Bava Batra 21a), and a dispute for the sake of Heaven that is beneficial and from which good things may grow [although Shemot Rabbah, chapter 30, says: “No good thing and no peace emerge from contention”; end of quotation]. But this particular good of peace [which is the joining of completeness and the vessel that holds blessing: an individual cannot be complete in everything; only through their unity is there a joining of all completeness. Shalom, “peace,” has the root shalem, “complete,” and the added letter vav indicates connection everywhere] cannot emerge from contention, even when it is good and for the sake of Heaven.”
