connections.explanation: Divrei Chalomot distinguishes the good gained through rivalry in learning from the particular good called peace. Peace joins contributions that are individually incomplete. This illuminates the present siman’s insistence that even a great scholar lacks the smallest person’s unique portion of Torah. The need for teachers and functional authority in this world remains, but it gives no ground for contempt: no size of one person’s portion makes another’s portion dispensable.
connections.headline: Peace joins portions of Torah that no single learner possesses alone

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה טַעַם (תַּעֲנִית ז.): "וּמִתַּלְמִידַי יוֹתֵר מִכֻּלָּם", כִּי רַב אֵין לָאָדָם רַק אֶחָד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה יט.): כָּל הַלּוֹמֵד תּוֹרָה מֵרַב אֶחָד וְכוּלֵי, גְּמָרָא מֵרַב אֶחָד עָדִיף;
connections.quote: “Rav Chisda said to the Sages: I wish to tell you something, but I fear that you will leave me and go. Anyone who learns Torah from only one teacher never sees a sign of blessing. They left him and went before Rava. He said to them: This applies to reasoning; but for the received teaching, one teacher is preferable, so that the formulations will not conflict.”
connections.context: The qualification about received teaching is essential to Rav Tzadok’s point. Learning reasoning from several teachers can broaden understanding, while one teacher preserves a consistent formulation of the received material. The final words continue onto 19b.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה טַעֲנַת אוֹתוֹ חוֹפֵר שִׁיחִין לְרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי בַּמִּדְרָשׁ, שֶׁגַּם הוּא עוֹסֵק בְּצָרְכֵי צִבּוּר;
connections.quote: “Shimon Sikhna, a man of counsel, used to dig pits, channels, and caves in Jerusalem. He said to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Zakkai: “I am as great as you.” He asked him: “Why?” He replied: “Because I attend to the needs of the public, as you do.” He said: “If someone comes to you for judgment or a legal question, do you say to him, ‘Drink from this cistern, whose waters are clear and cool’? Or if a woman asks you about her menstrual status, do you say to her, ‘Immerse in this cistern, whose waters purify’?” He applied this verse to him: “Drawing near to listen is better than fools offering a sacrifice, for they do not know how to do evil.””

connections.hePhrase: וּמִצַּד זֶה הוּא הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת תַּלְמִיד חָכָם עַל עַם הָאָרֶץ, מִשּׁוּם דִּבְעַם הָאָרֶץ הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁלּוֹ בְּהֶעְלֵם גָּדוֹל, וְהַגָּלוּי רַק מִצְווֹת, וְתַלְמוּד גָּדוֹל.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Tarfon and the elders were once reclining in the upper room of the house of Nitza in Lod. This question was asked before them: “Is study greater, or is action greater?” Rabbi Tarfon answered: “Action is greater.” Rabbi Akiva answered: “Study is greater.” They all answered: “Study is greater, because study leads to action.””

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה לֹא שַׁיָּיךְ בְּדוֹר הַמִּדְבָּר שֶׁהָיוּ דּוֹר דֵּעָה וְכֻלָּם קְדוֹשִׁים, וּבְתוֹכָם בִּפְנִימִיּוּתָם שֵׁם הֲוָיָ"ה שֶׁהוּא קַו אֶמְצָעִי הַמַּבְרִיחַ בְּכָל קַצְוֵי הַבְּרִיאָה כַּנּוֹדָע.
connections.quote: “And the middle bar in the midst of the boards shall pass through (mavriach) from end to end.”

connections.hePhrase: רַק עוֹנְשָׁם הָיוּ דִּבֶּאֱמֶת לֹא הִתְנַשְּׂאוּ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְהָאִישׁ מֹשֶׁה עָנָו" (בַּמִּדְבָּר יב, ג).
connections.quote: ‘The man Moses was exceedingly humble, more than any other person on the face of the earth.’

connections.hePhrase: וְרַק לֶעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר: "וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד... כִּי כֻלָּם יֵדְעוּ אוֹתִי" (יִרְמְיָה לא, לג), אֲפִילּוּ עַם הָאָרֶץ יֵצֵא הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַגָּנוּז אֶצְלָם מִן הַהֶעְלֵם.
connections.quote: see note 562 (Vol. I).
connections.context: The promised knowledge extending to everyone is the point needed here. Rav Tzadok’s citation, Jeremiah 31:33, is correct in the traditional Hebrew numbering. Sefaria numbers the same verse 31:34; the link follows that numbering.

connections.hePhrase: וְרַק לֶעָתִיד נֶאֱמַר: "וְלֹא יְלַמְּדוּ עוֹד... כִּי כֻלָּם יֵדְעוּ אוֹתִי" (יִרְמְיָה לא, לג), אֲפִילּוּ עַם הָאָרֶץ יֵצֵא הַדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה הַגָּנוּז אֶצְלָם מִן הַהֶעְלֵם.
connections.quote: see note 564 (Vol. I).

connections.hePhrase: [עַיֵּין בְּסֵפֶר בְּרִית מְנוּחָה כָּתַב כֵּן עַל מָאוֹר אֶחָד, דְּאִלּוּ יָדְעוּ תָּקְפּוֹ אֶפְשָׁר לָבוֹא לִידֵי קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ, וְזֶהוּ טַעַם: אֵין דּוֹרְשִׁין וְכוּלֵי],
connections.quote: “They said that when people of understanding reached an apprehension of this light, some stood astonished, while others departed from the path and from faith and came to the devastation of the world, as we find among great people.”

connections.hePhrase: [עַיֵּין בְּסֵפֶר בְּרִית מְנוּחָה כָּתַב כֵּן עַל מָאוֹר אֶחָד, דְּאִלּוּ יָדְעוּ תָּקְפּוֹ אֶפְשָׁר לָבוֹא לִידֵי קַלּוּת רֹאשׁ, וְזֶהוּ טַעַם: אֵין דּוֹרְשִׁין וְכוּלֵי],
connections.quote: “Forbidden sexual relationships are not expounded before three students, nor the work of Creation before two, nor the Chariot even before one, unless he is wise and understands through his own discernment.”

connections.hePhrase: וְרַק יִתְרוֹ שֶׁהָיָה גֵּר הִרְגִּישׁ דָּבָר זֶה, שֶׁגַּם לֶעָתִיד אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה צח וְתַנְחוּמָא שָׁם) שֶׁמָּשִׁיחַ יְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה לַגּוֹיִם שֶׁעֲתִידִים לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְנָהֲרוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה ב, ב), כִּי הֵם אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק מְיוּחָד בַּתּוֹרָה, מַה שֶּׁ[יֵּשׁ] לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Chanin said: Israel will not require the teaching of the King Messiah in the future, as it is written, “The nations shall seek him”—not Israel.”
connections.context: The contrast between the nations and Israel is the exact point Rav Tzadok cites. He explains it through Israel’s individual portions in Torah and the need of future converts for instruction. The verse invoked by the Midrash is Isaiah 11:10; Rav Tzadok also brings the nations’ streaming to the mountain in Isaiah 2:2.

connections.hePhrase: וְרַק יִתְרוֹ שֶׁהָיָה גֵּר הִרְגִּישׁ דָּבָר זֶה, שֶׁגַּם לֶעָתִיד אָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה צח וְתַנְחוּמָא שָׁם) שֶׁמָּשִׁיחַ יְלַמֵּד תּוֹרָה לַגּוֹיִם שֶׁעֲתִידִים לְהִתְגַּיֵּיר, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "וְנָהֲרוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (יְשַׁעְיָה ב, ב), כִּי הֵם אֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק מְיוּחָד בַּתּוֹרָה, מַה שֶּׁ[יֵּשׁ] לְיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל.
connections.quote: “In the latter days, the mountain of the Lord’s house shall be established at the head of the mountains and raised above the hills, and all the nations shall stream to it.”
connections.context: “They shall stream” describes the nations coming to the divine teaching. Rav Tzadok cites this movement toward Torah in his discussion of the instruction of future converts.

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן יֵשׁ עִנְיַן עֶבֶד בְּגוֹי, מַה שֶּׁאֵין כֵּן בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל: "עֲבָדַי הֵם וְכוּלֵי" (וַיִּקְרָא כה, מב), רַק עֶבֶד עִבְרִי לְשָׁעָה כְּעִנְיַן הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
connections.quote: ‘For they are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold as a slave is sold.’

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם זֶה רַק בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲרָכִין כט.), שֶׁאָז גַּם גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נוֹהֵג (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם), שֶׁעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵר שֶׁבַע מִצְווֹת לְבַד גַּם הוּא קָרוּי גֵּר.
connections.quote: “They raised an objection: The institution of a Hebrew servant applies only when the Jubilee applies, as it says, “Until the Jubilee year he shall serve with you.””

connections.hePhrase: וְגַם זֶה רַק בִּזְמַן שֶׁהַיּוֹבֵל נוֹהֵג (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ עֲרָכִין כט.), שֶׁאָז גַּם גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב נוֹהֵג (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם), שֶׁעוֹבֵד כּוֹכָבִים שֶׁשּׁוֹמֵר שֶׁבַע מִצְווֹת לְבַד גַּם הוּא קָרוּי גֵּר.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says: The status of a resident alien applies only when the Jubilee applies.”
connections.context: Both institutions mentioned by Rav Tzadok are expressly tied to the Jubilee on this page: the Hebrew servant and the ger toshav. Quoting only the law of a dedicated field would omit the first part of his argument.

connections.hePhrase: לְעֻמַּת זֶה יֵשׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵגַת עַבְדוּת וְשִׁעְבּוּד, וְגַם כֵּן קָרוּי יִשְׂרָאֵל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרְשׁוּת אָדוֹן עָלָיו, דְּזֶהוּ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם לב:) מִכִּבּוּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן דִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁהָיָה כִּבּוּשׁ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבַד, שֶׁלֹּא קִדְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא כְּלָל.
connections.quote: “It was taught: When the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh were exiled, the Jubilees ceased, as it says, “You shall proclaim liberty in the land to all its inhabitants”—when all its inhabitants are upon it, not when some have been exiled. Might the Jubilee apply when they are present but intermixed, Benjamin in Judah and Judah in Benjamin? Scripture says, “To all its inhabitants”—when its inhabitants are arranged properly, not when they are intermixed.”
connections.context: The passage supplies the condition “all its inhabitants upon it” and explains why exile ended the Jubilee. This is the condition Rav Tzadok applies to the status of servitude within Israel.

connections.hePhrase: לְעֻמַּת זֶה יֵשׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵגַת עַבְדוּת וְשִׁעְבּוּד, וְגַם כֵּן קָרוּי יִשְׂרָאֵל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרְשׁוּת אָדוֹן עָלָיו, דְּזֶהוּ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם לב:) מִכִּבּוּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן דִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁהָיָה כִּבּוּשׁ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבַד, שֶׁלֹּא קִדְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא כְּלָל.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Yitzchak said: I heard that offerings are brought in the temple of Onias at the present time. He holds that the temple of Onias is not a house of idolatry, and he holds that the first sanctification sanctified for its time and did not sanctify for the future.”

connections.hePhrase: לְעֻמַּת זֶה יֵשׁ בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן מַדְרֵגַת עַבְדוּת וְשִׁעְבּוּד, וְגַם כֵּן קָרוּי יִשְׂרָאֵל אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁרְשׁוּת אָדוֹן עָלָיו, דְּזֶהוּ כָּל זְמַן שֶׁיּוֹשְׁבֶיהָ עָלֶיהָ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם לב:) מִכִּבּוּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן דִּיהוֹשֻׁעַ, שֶׁהָיָה כִּבּוּשׁ דְּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה לְבַד, שֶׁלֹּא קִדְּשָׁה לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא כְּלָל.
connections.quote: “All the territory taken into possession by those who came out of Egypt and sanctified with the first sanctification lost its sanctity when they were exiled. For the first sanctification, being based solely on conquest, sanctified it for its own time but did not sanctify it for the future. When the exiles returned and took possession of part of the land, they sanctified it with a second sanctification that endures forever, for its own time and for the future.”

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל מֵעֵת גָּלוּת רִאשׁוֹן דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים וּבָטְלָה כְּבִישָׁה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, אָז הֵחֵל צְמִיחַת גְּאוּלָּה וּכְבִישָׁה שְׁנִיָּה, כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי א, נא) וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת (פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ד) דִּבְאוֹתוֹ יוֹם נוֹלַד מָשִׁיחַ.
connections.quote: “An incident occurred with a man who was plowing. His ox lowed. An Arab passed him and said: Unharness your ox and your plow, for the Jews’ Temple has been destroyed. … While he was speaking with him, it lowed again. He said: Harness your ox and your plow, for the Jews’ redeemer has been born. He asked: What is his name? He said: Menachem.”
connections.context: The story explicitly places the redeemer’s birth alongside the destruction of the Temple. Rav Tzadok develops from it the broader principle that the beginning of exile contains the beginning of redemption, then relates that principle to the earlier exile of the ten tribes and the possibility of Hezekiah becoming Messiah.

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל מֵעֵת גָּלוּת רִאשׁוֹן דַּעֲשֶׂרֶת הַשְּׁבָטִים וּבָטְלָה כְּבִישָׁה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, אָז הֵחֵל צְמִיחַת גְּאוּלָּה וּכְבִישָׁה שְׁנִיָּה, כַּיָּדוּעַ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (אֵיכָה רַבָּתִי א, נא) וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת (פֶּרֶק ב הֲלָכָה ד) דִּבְאוֹתוֹ יוֹם נוֹלַד מָשִׁיחַ.
connections.quote: see note 613 (Vol. I).
connections.context: The Jerusalem Talmud places the Messiah’s birth alongside the Temple’s destruction; the parallel in Eikhah Rabbah is quoted in the neighboring note. Rav Tzadok applies the pattern of redemption beginning within exile to the earlier exile of the tribes. That extension is his interpretation, rather than a statement that the story itself occurred during the exile of the ten tribes.

connections.hePhrase: וּמְכֻוָּון לְמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין צד.): בִּקֵּשׁ לַעֲשׂוֹת חִזְקִיָּהוּ מָשִׁיחַ, דְּתֵיכֶף הִתְחִיל נְבִיעַת אוֹתוֹ אוֹר לָעוֹלָם, וְנִסְתַּלֵּק הָעַבְדוּת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְנִתְבַּטֵּל גַּם כֵּן קַבָּלַת גֵּר תּוֹשָׁב מֵאֻמּוֹת,
connections.quote: “‘For the increase of dominion and for peace without end,’ and so forth. Rabbi Tanchum said: Bar Kappara expounded in Tzippori: Why is every mem in the middle of a word open, whereas this mem in lemarbeh is closed? The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to make Hezekiah the Messiah, and Sennacherib Gog and Magog.”

connections.hePhrase: כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בַּגְּמָרָא דְּגֵר עַמּוֹנִי בִּבְרָכוֹת (כח.), שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְבָּרֵר עִנְיַן יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר, אָז גַּם עִנְיַן הָעַכּוּ"ם מִתְבָּרֵר וְנִבְדָּל יוֹתֵר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
connections.quote: “Rabban Gamliel told him: You are forbidden to enter the congregation. Rabbi Yehoshua told him: You are permitted to enter the congregation. Rabban Gamliel said to Rabbi Yehoshua: Is it not already stated, ‘An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter Hashem’s congregation’? Rabbi Yehoshua replied: Are Ammon and Moab still living in their original places? Sennacherib, king of Assyria, already came and mixed up all the nations, as it is said, ‘I removed the boundaries of peoples, plundered their treasures, and cast down the inhabitants with mighty power.’ Whatever separates from a mixture is presumed to come from its majority.”

connections.hePhrase: כְּמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי בַּגְּמָרָא דְּגֵר עַמּוֹנִי בִּבְרָכוֹת (כח.), שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר מִתְבָּרֵר עִנְיַן יִשְׂרָאֵל יוֹתֵר, אָז גַּם עִנְיַן הָעַכּוּ"ם מִתְבָּרֵר וְנִבְדָּל יוֹתֵר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל.
connections.displayRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Berakhot 27b:3
connections.canonicalRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Talmud, Berakhot 27b:3
connections.quote: “The Rabbis taught: A student came before Rabbi Yehoshua and asked him, “Is the evening prayer optional or obligatory?” The evening prayer means crying out and calling to God over Israel’s suffering in exile. He asked “optional or obligatory”: is one obliged to pray because “in all their distress He is distressed,” or is it optional, since at present, before the true clarification is completed, nothing has yet been fully clarified, and therefore prayer is not obligatory? When an Ammonite convert came before them and it was ruled that he could enter the congregation, this was because the clarification was not yet complete. For converts are not accepted in the days of the Messiah; their present acceptance is because the clarification is unfinished and there are still holy sparks that must be gathered. Therefore, at present the ruling is that the evening prayer is optional; in the future, however, it will be obligatory, because the union will then be complete and their suffering will touch the Holy One, blessed be He.”

connections.hePhrase: וּלְכָךְ קָרֵי לַהּ הַזֹּהַר עַל יִתְרוֹ (סח סוֹף עַמּוּד ב): "מִלֵּי דִּהֶדְיוֹטָא", כִּי מַאֲמַר יִתְרוֹ לִהְיוֹת שָׂרִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל עַצְמָן זֶהוּ אֵינוֹ אֱמֶת גָּמוּר וּמִילֵּי דִּהֶדְיוֹט.
connections.quote: ‘Come and see: It was Jethro who advised Moses about establishing the arrangements for judgment; so it needed to be. This is the mystery: He acknowledged the Holy One, blessed be He, and set before him the arrangements for His judgments, to show what is written: ‘For judgment belongs to God’ (Deuteronomy 1:17), and not to the Other Side. Judgments were given to Israel and not to another, as it is written: ‘His statutes and His judgments to Israel’ (Psalms 147:19). Come and see: A person should not treat another with contempt, and the word of an ordinary person also counts as a word. For concerning Moses it is written: ‘Moses listened to the voice of his father-in-law,’ and so forth.’

connections.hePhrase: [רלב] כָּל עִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם וְכָל הַנִּבְרָאִים מַזְכִּירִים לָאָדָם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא,
connections.quote: “Thus I received: the entire world is a book Hashem made. I recall that in my youth I saw [Me’or Einayim] by HaAdomi, citing a book attributed to Chanoch among the nations, and it seems to me that there was some trace of this there: that all the creatures of the world are forms of letters Hashem engraved in His world, which is His book. The Torah is the explanation He made and composed for that book. These are words of truth, for Torah is an offshoot of the letters of thought themselves, embodied and clothed in the forms of written letters, whereas the world is only a trace and indication. Through Torah one can understand the hints contained in that trace and indication in deeds, corresponding to what is in His thought. Nevertheless, all the deeds and creatures of the entire world form a complete book in which He engraved all the letters of thought in great concealment. No creature or created being fails to indicate a particular matter and meaning in His thought. “He did not create it for emptiness”; everything has a particular purpose, for His praise and to reveal the glory of Heaven. As Rabbi Baruch wrote on “the earth is full of Your acquisitions”: it means how to acquire and apprehend Him, blessed be He.”
connections.explanation: Machshavot Charutz describes the world as Hashem’s book and Torah as its explanation. This supplies an important qualification to the siman’s account of encounters that awaken remembrance: the world bears a concealed trace, while Torah teaches how that trace can be understood. Its reminders are therefore joined to learning and the disciplined practice of berachos, rather than arbitrary private interpretations of events. Title clarification: the book abbreviation M.E. refers to Me’or Einayim by Azariah de Rossi (HaAdomi). The supplied Hebrew expands it incorrectly as mitzvot aseh, positive commandments; the translation marks the corrected title in square brackets.
connections.headline: Torah teaches how to read the world’s reminders

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בְּרָכוֹת ו:): כָּל הָעוֹלָם כֻּלּוֹ לֹא נִבְרָא אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל זֶה, פֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁיֵּדַע זֶה עַל יָדָהּ וְיַכִּיר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹרֵא עוֹלָם;
connections.quote: ‘What is meant by ‘For this is the whole of man’? Rabbi Elazar said: The Holy One, blessed be He, said: ‘The entire world was created only for this person.’ Rabbi Abba bar Kahana said: This person is equal in worth to the entire world. Rabbi Shimon ben Azzai says—and some attribute it to Rabbi Shimon ben Zoma: The entire world was created only to be company for this person.’

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל "מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ קִנְיָנֶךָ" (תְּהִלִּים קד, כד), פֵּירוּשׁ לִקְנוֹת עַל יָדָם אוֹתְךָ.
connections.quote: “How numerous are Your works, Lord! You made them all with wisdom; the earth is full of Your possessions.”
connections.context: Kinyanekha means Your possessions or acquisitions. Rav Tzadok reports a homiletic reading of that word: created things provide ways through which a person may “acquire” a bond with their Creator.

connections.hePhrase: וְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ מַזְמִין לָאָדָם בְּכָל יוֹם דְּבָרִים וְעִנְיָנִים שׁוֹנִים, אוּלַי עַל יָדָם יָבוֹא לִזְכִירָה בַּבּוֹרֵא.
connections.quote: “Everything the Holy One, blessed be He, created in His world is so that a person should derive from it instruction for serving the Lord, for He created everything for His glory. As was said in the name of the holy master of Peshischa, of blessed memory, concerning the name Shaddai, “who said to His world: Enough”: it is sufficient for learning to recognize the blessed God. When our father Abraham, of blessed memory, came and saw a palace ablaze, he wondered: Is it possible for the palace to have no governor? Until the Holy One, blessed be He, appeared to him and said: “I am the owner of the palace,” as stated in Bereishit Rabbah, chapter 39. He explained through this the verse “The earth is full of Your possessions”: the whole earth is filled with acquisitions through which a person may acquire knowledge of the blessed God and of what the blessed God wants from him. Everything that comes before a person’s eyes has been deliberately brought before him by particular providence, so that he should learn from it.”

connections.hePhrase: כִּי בֶּאֱמֶת הַהַצָּלָה מִשִּׁכְחָה זֶה אֵינוֹ בְּיַד הָאָדָם, דְּלָכֵן לֹא נֶאֱמַר "אָנֹכִי וְגוֹמֵר" בִּלְשׁוֹן צִוּוּי, שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְצַוּוֹת עַל הַיְדִיעָה דְּאָנֹכִי שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁכַּח.
connections.displayRef: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 6:8
connections.canonicalRef: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 6:8
connections.quote: “Therefore “I am” is not expressed as a command, because the beginning comes from God, who, on His own initiative, gave Torah from heaven to His people Israel. Their effort lies in the Oral Torah, which corresponds to “You shall have no other,” as I have written at length elsewhere.”

connections.hePhrase: רַק צָרִיךְ לְסַיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא, וְהַסַּיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא הוּא עַל יְדֵי "לֹא יִהְיֶה לְךָ וְגוֹמֵר".
connections.quote: “You shall have no other gods before Me.”

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ, "אֱלֹהִים" – כֹּחַ וִיכֹלֶת בְּכָל מָקוֹם, וְהַיְינוּ בְּכָל שִׁימּוּשׁוֹ בְּכֹחוֹתָיו, בְּאֵיזֶה כֹּחַ מִכֹּחוֹת הַגּוּף: רְאִיָּה אוֹ שְׁמִיעָה אוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה אוֹ הִילוּךְ וְכַיּוֹצֵא, יַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה.
connections.quote: “When mentioning Elohim, one should intend that He is mighty and strong, possessing power over the higher and lower realms, for el signifies strength and might, as in “He took the mighty ones of the land.””

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ, "אֱלֹהִים" – כֹּחַ וִיכֹלֶת בְּכָל מָקוֹם, וְהַיְינוּ בְּכָל שִׁימּוּשׁוֹ בְּכֹחוֹתָיו, בְּאֵיזֶה כֹּחַ מִכֹּחוֹת הַגּוּף: רְאִיָּה אוֹ שְׁמִיעָה אוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה אוֹ הִילוּךְ וְכַיּוֹצֵא, יַכִּיר שֶׁהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ הוּא הַנּוֹתֵן לוֹ כֹּחַ זֶה.
connections.displayRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayechi 8
connections.canonicalRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Genesis, Vayechi 8
connections.quote: “‘Naftali is a hind let loose, who gives beautiful words.’ He possessed a great understanding concerning everything in this world, immediately asking, ‘Who created these?’ This is the meaning of ‘who gives beautiful words’: since he recognized Hashem in everything, he gave thanks to Him. Thus Onkelos translates, ‘They will give thanks and bless for them.’”
connections.explanation: Mei HaShiloach gives a concrete form to the siman's movement from encountering the world to recognizing its Giver. Naftali immediately asks who made what he encounters, and recognition becomes thanksgiving. This supports the function of blessings described here without treating forgetting itself as a freely chosen act.
connections.headline: Recognition becomes thanksgiving

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה טַעַם הַבְּרָכָה לִפְנֵי כָּל הֲנָאָה, וּבְלֹא בְּרָכָה – מָעַל (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּרָכוֹת לה.);
connections.quote: ‘The Rabbis taught: A person is forbidden to enjoy anything from this world without a blessing. Anyone who enjoys anything from this world without a blessing has misused sacred property. What is his remedy? Let him go to a sage. Go to a sage?! What can the sage do for him? He has already committed the prohibition! Rather, Rava said: Let him go to a sage beforehand, who will teach him the blessings so that he does not come to misuse sacred property.’

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שָׁם מ:): "לֹא עָבַרְתִּי מִמִּצְוֹתֶיךָ" – בִּבְרָכָה, "וְלֹא שָׁכַחְתִּי" – בְּהַזְכָּרַת הַשֵּׁם;
connections.quote: “Returning to the matter: Rav said, “Any blessing that contains no mention of the Name is not a blessing.” Rabbi Yoḥanan said, “Any blessing that contains no mention of kingship is not a blessing.” Abaye said: Rav’s view is reasonable, for it was taught: “I have not transgressed Your commandments, and I have not forgotten”—“I have not transgressed” by failing to bless You; “I have not forgotten” by failing to mention Your name over it. Kingship, however, is not taught. Rabbi Yoḥanan teaches: “I have not forgotten” by failing to mention Your name and Your kingship over it.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ תַּקָּנַת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת עַל כָּל דִּבְרֵי הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף: בְּמָזוֹן, וּבִרְאִיָּה, וּבִשְׁמִיעָה כְּקוֹל תַּרְנְגוֹל, וּבִבְשׂוֹרוֹת טוֹבוֹת וּלְהֵיפֶךְ, וּבְמַלְבּוּשָׁיו וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
connections.quote: “For rain and for good news one says: “Blessed is He who is good and does good.” For bad tidings one says: “Blessed is the true Judge.””

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ תַּקָּנַת רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה בִּבְרָכוֹת עַל כָּל דִּבְרֵי הֲנָאַת הַגּוּף: בְּמָזוֹן, וּבִרְאִיָּה, וּבִשְׁמִיעָה כְּקוֹל תַּרְנְגוֹל, וּבִבְשׂוֹרוֹת טוֹבוֹת וּלְהֵיפֶךְ, וּבְמַלְבּוּשָׁיו וְכַיּוֹצֵא.
connections.quote: “When one hears the rooster’s voice, one should say: “Blessed … who gave the rooster understanding to distinguish between day and night.” When one opens one’s eyes: “Blessed … who opens the eyes of the blind.” When one straightens up and sits: “Blessed … who releases the bound.” When one dresses: “Blessed … who clothes the naked.” When one stands upright: “Blessed … who straightens the bent.” When one steps onto the ground: “Blessed … who spreads the earth over the waters.” When one walks: “Blessed … who prepares a person’s steps.” When one puts on shoes: “Blessed … who has provided all my needs.” When one fastens a belt: “Blessed … who girds Israel with strength.” When one spreads a cloth over one’s head: “Blessed … who crowns Israel with beauty.””

connections.hePhrase: כִּפְתִיחַת הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב בְּ"אָנֹכִי" וְ"לֹא יִהְיֶה", שֶׁזֶּהוּ כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ, וְאִידַּךְ פֵּירוּשָׁא זִיל גְּמוֹר: עֵצוֹת שׁוֹנוֹת בְּכָל זְמַן וּבְכָל מָקוֹם אֵיךְ לָבוֹא לִזְכִירָה זוֹ.
connections.quote: “He came before Hillel, who converted him. He said to him: What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow. That is the entire Torah, and the rest is its explanation; go and learn.”

connections.hePhrase: אֲבָל הַמְּכֻוָּון בְּכֻלָּם הוּא יְדִיעַת הָאֱלֹהוּת, שֶׁלֹּא יָזוּז מִן הַלֵּב וְלֹא יִשְׁלוֹט בּוֹ הַשִּׁכְחָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם:
connections.quote: “Although, according to this, the principal warning against forgetting concerns concealment from the heart, it is nevertheless no small matter. Great application to remembering this is necessary until it becomes established in the heart and all one’s actions cease to contradict it, as explained. According to all views, a person must strive constantly for this remembrance. Even if we say that remembering twice a day fulfills the obligation of the warning, something similar was said of the commandment of Torah study: by reciting the Shema morning and evening one fulfills “It shall not depart,” as mentioned above; nevertheless, one must also engage in it continually. All the more so here, for this is the whole purpose of the human being.”

connections.hePhrase: כִּי מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת כָּל הַיּוֹם, לֹא יִמָּלֵט גַּם כֵּן מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת בִּתְפִלָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קסד:) דְּעִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה אֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל, וּמַשְׁמָע דְּעַל כָּל אָדָם קָאָמַר.
connections.heRef: תוספות על בבא בתרא קס״ד ב:ט״ז:א׳
connections.quote: “It appears to Rabbi that the harmful “examination of prayer” means that people do not concentrate in prayer. … No person escapes this every day, for no person can direct his prayer perfectly. So the Jerusalem Talmud says: Rabbi Matanyah said, “I am grateful to my head, for when it reaches Modim it bows by itself.””
connections.context: The neighboring note quotes Bava Batra’s list of daily failings. Tosafot explains the meaning of the prayer failing that Rav Tzadok is discussing and relates it to the Yerushalmi. The correct daf is 164b; the former quotation from 164a concerned documents.

connections.hePhrase: כִּי מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת כָּל הַיּוֹם, לֹא יִמָּלֵט גַּם כֵּן מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת בִּתְפִלָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קסד:) דְּעִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה אֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל, וּמַשְׁמָע דְּעַל כָּל אָדָם קָאָמַר.
connections.quote: “Prayer means connection and attachment. This is iyun tefillah, from which no person escapes: even Yaakov is not completely perfected in having every part equal and united without degrees of perfection and attachment. In the future, the Holy One will form a circle for the righteous, as stated at the end of Taanit 31a. A circle means that the level of circles will be revealed, where there are no degrees and everyone is equal in perfection. By contrast, Yaakov's stature is the upright form of a person, with degrees of head, end and extremities, as is known. One cannot escape—that is, attain complete perfection—for this power is not yet perfected until the coming of Mashiach, who will possess complete perfection. ‘As the leader, so the generation’ (Arakhin 17a): the entire generation will be completely perfected. They will then escape iyun tefillah as well, for there will be complete attachment, and consequently they will escape sinful thoughts and the dust of slander, which do not truly belong to the human person's own body.”
connections.explanation: Resisei Layla treats the same statement about unavoidable iyun tefillah as incomplete attachment. It distinguishes the soul's root from surrounding faults while reserving fully equal, uninterrupted attachment for the future. This explains why the siman can speak honestly about an intrusive thought without identifying that thought with the person's essential root.
connections.headline: Degrees of attachment and future completion

connections.hePhrase: כִּי מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ נָקִי מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת כָּל הַיּוֹם, לֹא יִמָּלֵט גַּם כֵּן מִמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת זָרוֹת בִּתְפִלָּה, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (בָּבָא בַּתְרָא קסד:) דְּעִיּוּן תְּפִלָּה אֵין אָדָם נִיצּוֹל, וּמַשְׁמָע דְּעַל כָּל אָדָם קָאָמַר.
connections.quote: “It is difficult to understand such a statement about people of this greatness, particularly Rabbi Chiyya, of whom it is said that when he said ‘He causes the wind to blow,’ the wind blew. One may therefore interpret ‘I did not direct my heart’ to mean that he did not need to. Directing the heart applies to someone subject to imagination and thoughts, whose tongue speaks while his heart is elsewhere. He never needed this, for no other thing was in his thought: Hashem was before his eyes, and he always spoke as someone speaking before the King of kings. ‘One day I wanted to direct my heart’ means he then needed to because troubling thoughts had arisen; perhaps this was the occasion when Eliyahu disturbed them. Then he needed to direct his thoughts properly, but it did not help, since the disturbance had come from Heaven.”
connections.explanation: In Siman 209 Rav Tzadok finds it difficult to attribute ordinary distraction to such great sages and suggests that ‘I did not direct my heart’ means they normally had no need for a separate act of concentration. Here he explicitly says the Yerushalmi can be understood in its plain sense: even their prayer could include a fleeting other thought. These are distinct interpretive proposals. The earlier explanation should not erase the qualification about a flicker of thought stated in the present siman.
connections.headline: Rav Tzadok offers two readings of the same report

connections.hePhrase: פֵּירוּשׁ יְיַשְּׁרוּ הַלֵּב שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בּוֹ שׁוּם נְגִיעָה וְרָצוֹן זוּלַת רְצוֹן הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְאוּלַי בְּשָׁעָה זוֹ יַעַזְרֵהוּ הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ לְנַצֵּחַ בַּקְּרָב וּלְבַטֵּל הַיֵּצֶר מִקִּרְבּוֹ.
connections.quote: see note 3085.

connections.hePhrase: וּמַחְשֶׁבֶת מְנִית פַּרְחַיָּא וְדָמוֹסְיָא, שֶׁהוּא הִרְהוּרִים דִּרְכוּשׁוֹ, הוּא מִצַּד נְגִיעָה דְּתַאֲוַת מָמוֹן.
connections.quote: “Shmuel said: “I counted chicks.” Rabbi Bun bar Ḥiyya said: “I counted courses of stones.””

connections.hePhrase: וּ"מַחֲזִיקְנָא טִיבוּתָא לְרֵישָׁא וְכוּלֵי", דְּמִצַּד הַקִּנְאָה בָּא מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה בְּעֵת "מוֹדִים" שֶׁהוּא הַהוֹדָאָה עַל חַסְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
connections.quote: “Rabbi Matanyah said: I give thanks to my head, for when it reached Modim it bowed of its own accord.”

connections.hePhrase: וּ"מַחֲזִיקְנָא טִיבוּתָא לְרֵישָׁא וְכוּלֵי", דְּמִצַּד הַקִּנְאָה בָּא מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה בְּעֵת "מוֹדִים" שֶׁהוּא הַהוֹדָאָה עַל חַסְדֵי הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ;
connections.quote: “This is ‘to bring you into the covenant of Hashem your God and its oath’: if your understanding is bound to Hashem, and in actual conduct you also accept the awe of punishment, you will consequently be bound to Hashem in action as well. Even without conscious direction you will be drawn after His will. As the Yerushalmi says: Let us acknowledge the goodness of the head, for when it reaches Modim it bows of itself.”
connections.explanation: Tiferet Yosef concludes its distinction between inward willingness and the body's training with the same Yerushalmi statement about the head bowing at Modim. The involuntary motion is thus not offered as a reason to dispense with service; it is the fruit of a bond carried into actual conduct. This clarifies why the present siman can recognize good in the head's response while still examining the other thoughts that accompanied the prayer.
connections.headline: A trained body can carry the bond into action

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (טז.): שִׁדְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּלָא כָּרַע בְּמוֹדִים, דִּרְקַב עֲצָמוֹת קִנְאָה (מִשְׁלֵי יד, ל), וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ הוּא קִנְאָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין נט:) רָאָה וְכוּלֵי וְנִתְקַנֵּא.
connections.quote: “A tranquil heart is the life of the flesh, but jealousy is the rotting of the bones.”
connections.context: Jealousy, rather than passion in general, is the word needed for Rav Tzadok’s connection between the serpent, envy, and the decay of the spine.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (טז.): שִׁדְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּלָא כָּרַע בְּמוֹדִים, דִּרְקַב עֲצָמוֹת קִנְאָה (מִשְׁלֵי יד, ל), וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ הוּא קִנְאָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין נט:) רָאָה וְכוּלֵי וְנִתְקַנֵּא.
connections.quote: “Anyone who has envy in his heart—his bones decay; anyone who has no envy in his heart—his bones do not decay.”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּבָבָא קַמָּא (טז.): שִׁדְרוֹ וְכוּלֵי, וְהָנֵי מִילֵּי דְּלָא כָּרַע בְּמוֹדִים, דִּרְקַב עֲצָמוֹת קִנְאָה (מִשְׁלֵי יד, ל), וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ הוּא קִנְאָה כְּמַאֲמַר רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (סַנְהֶדְרִין נט:) רָאָה וְכוּלֵי וְנִתְקַנֵּא.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Yehudah ben Teima said: Adam was reclining in the Garden of Eden, and ministering angels were roasting meat for him and straining wine for him. The serpent peered at him, saw his honor, and became envious of him.”
connections.context: This is the passage that explicitly identifies the serpent’s envy. Rav Tzadok uses it to explain the serpent as the root of jealousy and the decay of the bones associated with jealousy.

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן הַאֲכָלַת חַוָּה לְאָדָם מִטַּעַם קִנְאָה.
connections.quote: ““She also gave to her husband”: so that she would not die while he lived and married another woman.”

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַבְתִּי לְעֵיל: "וּמִי יַעֲמֹד לִפְנֵי קִנְאָה" (מִשְׁלֵי כז, ד);
connections.quote: ‘Fury is cruel, and anger is a flood; but who can stand before jealousy?’

connections.hePhrase: וּלְפִי שֶׁקִּנְאָה הוּא הַגָּרוּעַ מֵהַכֹּל וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ, שֶׁנֶּגְדּוֹ הַמְּצוֹרָע הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא עַל קִנְאָה שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַשִּׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲרָכִין טז. וּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת מְצוֹרָע), וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ) דְּנָחָשׁ הוּא מְצוֹרָע
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: Afflictions of tzaraat come on account of seven things: harmful speech, bloodshed, a vain oath, forbidden sexual relations, arrogance, robbery, and stinginess. On account of harmful speech, as it is written: ‘One who slanders his fellow in secret—I will cut him off.’’

connections.hePhrase: וּלְפִי שֶׁקִּנְאָה הוּא הַגָּרוּעַ מֵהַכֹּל וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ, שֶׁנֶּגְדּוֹ הַמְּצוֹרָע הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא עַל קִנְאָה שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַשִּׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲרָכִין טז. וּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת מְצוֹרָע), וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ) דְּנָחָשׁ הוּא מְצוֹרָע
connections.quote: ““This shall be the teaching of the afflicted person”: this is what is written, “There are six things the Lord hates, and seven are an abomination to Him.” Rabbi Meir and the Sages differ: Rabbi Meir says, “Six and seven make thirteen.” The Sages maintain seven: the “seven” written here refers to the seventh, which is as severe as all the others. Which is it? “One who sows discord between brothers.” These are they: “Haughty eyes, a lying tongue, hands shedding innocent blood, a heart devising wicked plans, feet hastening to run to evil, a false witness who breathes lies, and one who sows discord between brothers.” Rabbi Yoḥanan said: All of them were afflicted with tzaraat.”

connections.hePhrase: וּלְפִי שֶׁקִּנְאָה הוּא הַגָּרוּעַ מֵהַכֹּל וְשׁוֹרֶשׁ נָחָשׁ, שֶׁנֶּגְדּוֹ הַמְּצוֹרָע הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁהוּא עַל קִנְאָה שֶׁכּוֹלֵל כָּל הַשִּׁבְעָה דְּבָרִים שֶׁחָשְׁבוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲרָכִין טז. וּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת מְצוֹרָע), וּכְאָמְרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה כ) דְּנָחָשׁ הוּא מְצוֹרָע
connections.quote: “Rabbi Hoshaya of Sikhnin said in Rabbi Levi’s name: He cursed it with leprosy; those scales upon it are leprous lesions.”
connections.context: The Midrash interprets the serpent’s scales as the marks of its curse. This is the specific statement Rav Tzadok needs in connecting the serpent, jealousy, and the metzora sent outside Israel’s camp. It appears in section 20:4 of this edition, immediately before the account of the serpent’s legs being removed.

connections.hePhrase: רַק הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה הוּא לְבוּשׁ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵעֶצֶם שׁוֹרֶשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָל, דְּהוּא חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל.
connections.quote: “For the Holy One, blessed be He, is the heart of Israel, as they said in Shir HaShirim Rabbah on the verse “My heart is awake,” from the verse “The Rock of my heart,” and so forth. That is, the depths of their hearts are truly attached to Him. As they said in the second chapter of Berakhot: “It is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will; who prevents us? The leaven in the dough.” This is the evil inclination that dwells at the two openings of the heart—only at the place where the heart opens and becomes manifest.”

connections.hePhrase: דְּזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר מִשְׁפָּטִים (ק עַמּוּד א) דְּמַאן דְּלָא כָּרַע בְּמוֹדִים אֵינוֹ קָם בִּתְחִיַּת הַמֵּתִים, פֵּירוּשׁ דְּהוּא מִשּׁוֹרֶשׁ הָרָע דְּקִנְאָה, וְהוּא מִי שֶׁהוּא חוּץ לְמַחֲנֵה יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּשׁוֹרֶשׁ נַפְשׁוֹ:
connections.quote: “The Holy One, blessed be He, does not withhold the reward of any creature He created, except those who departed from His faith and in whom there was never good, and those who did not bow in Modim. From these the Holy One, blessed be He, makes other creatures, for that body will not be rebuilt in human form and will never rise.”
connections.context: The passage is the source for the statement about one who does not bow in Modim. Rav Tzadok interprets the refusal to bow through the root of jealousy and separation from Israel’s camp. That interpretation follows the quotation; it is not part of the Zohar’s wording.

connections.hePhrase: רַק "לֹא תָתוּרוּ וְגוֹמֵר" (בַּמִּדְבָּר טו, לט) מוֹקְמִינַן בִּבְרָכוֹת (יב:) בְּהִרְהוּר עֲבֵירָה וְלֹא הִרְהוּר בָּטֵל לְבַד.
connections.quote: “For it was taught: ‘After your hearts’ refers to heresy, as another verse says, ‘The fool says in his heart: There is no God.’ ‘After your eyes’ refers to thoughts of sexual sin, as it is said, ‘Samson said to his father: Take her for me, for she is pleasing in my eyes.’ ‘You stray’ refers to thoughts of idolatry, as another verse says, ‘They strayed after the Baals.’”

connections.hePhrase: וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (קִדּוּשִׁין מ.) דְּמַחֲשָׁבָה רָעָה אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מְצָרְפָהּ לְמַעֲשֶׂה, וְרַק בְּמַחֲשָׁבָה דַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
connections.quote: “The Holy One, blessed be He, does not join an evil thought to an action, as it says, “Had I regarded iniquity in my heart, Hashem would not hear.” How, then, do I explain “I shall bring evil upon this people, the fruit of their thoughts”? A thought that produces fruit, the Holy One joins to action; a thought that produces no fruit, He does not join to action. But what of “To seize the House of Israel in their heart”? Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: That is written concerning idolatry, for a master said: Idolatry is so grave that one who rejects it is as though he acknowledges the entire Torah.”
connections.context: The second paragraph gives the exception on which Rav Tzadok’s sentence depends: thoughts of idolatry. His discussion turns on the difference between ordinary evil thoughts and a thought directed against the root of faith.

connections.hePhrase: רַק עַל דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים יֵשׁ עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (יט:).
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Acha says: ‘You shall speak of them’—make them your regular occupation, not an occasional one. Rava said: One who engages in mundane conversation violates a positive commandment, as it says: ‘You shall speak of them’—of them, and not of other things. Rav Acha bar Yaakov said: He violates a prohibition, as it says: ‘All words are wearying; a person cannot speak.’’

connections.hePhrase: רַק עַל דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים יֵשׁ עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (יט:).
connections.quote: “You shall teach them diligently to your children, and you shall speak of them when you sit in your house, when you walk on the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up.”
connections.context: Rava in Yoma 19b reads “of them” as “and not of other things,” a positive commandment against idle talk.

connections.hePhrase: רַק עַל דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים יֵשׁ עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (יט:).
connections.quote: “All things are wearisome; a man cannot utter it. The eye is not satisfied with seeing, nor the ear filled with hearing.”
connections.context: Rav Acha bar Yaakov in Yoma 19b reads “a man cannot utter” as a prohibition against idle talk.

connections.hePhrase: רַק עַל דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים יֵשׁ עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא (יט:).
connections.displayRef: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 7:12
connections.canonicalRef: Ohr Zarua LaTzadik, The Egyptian Exile 7:12
connections.quote: “Just as Yosef was placed in Egypt and in his mistress's house in order to refine him, so King David was placed in a generation full of harmful speech, as the Yerushalmi in Peah and Midrash Tehillim teach on ‘You will preserve them from this generation forever.’ His tongue, however, was filled with songs and praises.”
connections.explanation: Ohr Zarua places David's covenant of speech beside Yosef's trial of covenantal purity. The positive content matters: David's tongue was filled with songs and praise. This illustrates the present siman's counsel to redirect the power of speech toward Torah rather than imagine that a person must have no use for speech at all. The corrective occupation reaches the faculty through which the person is being tested.
connections.headline: The repair gives speech a worthy occupation

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי גַּם כֵּן עַל הַדִּבּוּר עַל פָּסוּק "זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת הַמְּצֹרָע" (וַיִּקְרָא יד, ב), מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲרָכִין טו:) דְּתַקַּנְתֵּיהּ דְּבַעַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע יַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה,
connections.quote: “This shall be the law of the person afflicted with tzaraat on the day of his purification: he shall be brought to the priest.”
connections.context: The Hebrew calls it the torah of the metzora. Arakhin 15b reads metzora together with motzi shem ra, one who brings out an evil report, and uses torah to connect the remedy with Torah study.

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי גַּם כֵּן עַל הַדִּבּוּר עַל פָּסוּק "זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת הַמְּצֹרָע" (וַיִּקְרָא יד, ב), מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (עֲרָכִין טו:) דְּתַקַּנְתֵּיהּ דְּבַעַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע יַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה,
connections.quote: “Rabbi Chama bar Chanina said: What is the remedy for those who speak evil? If he is a Torah scholar, let him engage in Torah, as it says, “A healing tongue is a tree of life.” “Tongue” means evil speech, as it says, “Their tongue is a sharpened arrow”; “tree” means Torah, as it says, “It is a tree of life to those who hold it.” If he is unlearned, let him humble his mind, as it says, “Its perverseness is a broken spirit.””
connections.context: This is Rabbi Chama’s statement that Rav Tzadok quotes. The next opinion, Rabbi Acha’s, restricts the advice to preventing evil speech before it occurs. The distinction matters: the statement quoted here presents Torah as the remedy for the speaker, which Rav Tzadok relates to the restoration of speech.

connections.hePhrase: לְפִי שֶׁהָאָדָם שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּכֹחַ הַדִּבּוּר אִי אֶפְשָׁר לוֹ לַעֲצוֹר עַצְמוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יְדַבֵּר, רַק הָעֵצָה שֶׁיְּדַבֵּר, אֲבָל שֶׁיִּהְיֶה כָּל דִּבּוּרָיו תּוֹרָה.
connections.displayRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Leviticus, Metzora 1
connections.canonicalRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Leviticus, Metzora 1
connections.quote: “This is the allusion in the verse “This shall be the teaching of the afflicted person.” “This” indicates, as a person might say: this very thing that initially seemed to have no connection with Torah will itself later become clarified as belonging to Torah. For tzaraat comes through the sin of harmful speech, and the defect is that a person’s spirit has no restraint, causing him to speak excessively. Its repair “on the day of his purification” does not follow the natural way. According to the natural way, he would need to restrain his spirit and reduce his power of speech. But concerning this it says, “This shall be”: he should not follow the natural way; instead he should see to it that the very power of speech which until now brought him to words contrary to Torah should now be used abundantly to speak words of Torah. Abundant talk of Torah is good.”

connections.hePhrase: וְכָךְ מִי שֶׁנִּבְרָא בְּכֹחַ הַפְּעֻלָּה, וּכְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (שַׁבָּת יד.): סְתָם יָדַיִם עַסְקָנִיּוֹת;
connections.quote: “As for the hands, it is because hands are constantly occupied with things. It was taught: Even hands that have become impure through a sacred scroll render terumah unfit. This is because of Rabbi Parnakh’s teaching, for Rabbi Parnakh said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan: One who grasps the parchment of a Torah scroll with bare hands is buried naked. Can you really mean naked? Rather, Rabbi Zeira said: Bare, without mitzvot. Can you really mean without mitzvot? Rather, say: Bare, without the merit of that mitzvah.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהֲגַם דְּזֶהוּ מִתְעַסֵּק בְּעָלְמָא דְּלָאו מְלָאכָה הוּא לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת כָּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ בְּכַוָּנָה וְלָא מִקְרֵי מַעֲשֶׂה כְּלָל,
connections.quote: “In every human activity, the deed is like a body and the thought like a soul; a body without a soul is nothing. Therefore one acting without awareness of the act is exempt. He is unlike one who acts inadvertently, who at least intends the deed, whereas the unawares actor has no mental intention at all. The exception is forbidden fats and forbidden sexual relations, because he derives pleasure. In human pleasure it is impossible that there should not be at least some concealed degree of intention, for human nature registers pleasure even when the person is not consciously aware of it and does not remember.”

connections.hePhrase: רַק עַל יְדֵי סַיַּעְתָּא דִּשְׁמַיָּא, כְּדֶרֶךְ שֶׁאָמְרוּ (מִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה רֵישׁ פָּרָשַׁת בְּחֻקֹּתַי) בְּדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם: וְהָיוּ רַגְלַי מוֹלִיכוֹת אוֹתִי לְבָתֵּי כְּנֵסִיּוֹת וּבָתֵּי מִדְרָשׁוֹת, שֶׁהָיָה הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ עוֹשֶׂה פְּעֻלּוֹתָיו תַּכְלִיתָן לְשֵׁם שָׁמַיִם.
connections.quote: ““If you walk in My statutes”: this is what is written, “I considered my ways and turned my feet toward Your testimonies.” David said: “Master of the world, every day I would plan and say, ‘I am going to such-and-such a place and such-and-such a dwelling,’ but my feet would bring me to synagogues and houses of study.” This is what is written: “I turned my feet toward Your testimonies.””

connections.hePhrase: רַק דּוֹאֵג שׂוֹנֵא דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְרַתָּא דְּמַלְכָּא דָּא צְלוֹתָא, שֶׁזּוֹ מַדְרֵגָתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, מט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" (תְּהִלִּים קט, ד), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לְעוֹלָם שׁוּם מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה;
connections.quote: “Rabbi Chizkiyah said: “Hearer of prayer”—it should have said “Hearer of prayers.” What is “Hearer of prayer”? Rather, prayer is the Community of Israel, which is prayer, as it is written, “And I am prayer.” David said this on behalf of the Community of Israel. His words “And I am prayer” are all one.”
connections.context: The Zohar identifies the prayer of Psalms 109:4 with the Community of Israel and with David speaking on its behalf. Rav Tzadok uses this identification to describe David’s particular spiritual quality and his wholehearted prayer.

connections.hePhrase: רַק דּוֹאֵג שׂוֹנֵא דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְרַתָּא דְּמַלְכָּא דָּא צְלוֹתָא, שֶׁזּוֹ מַדְרֵגָתוֹ כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק ג, מט רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב) עַל פָּסוּק "וַאֲנִי תְפִלָּה" (תְּהִלִּים קט, ד), וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה לוֹ לְעוֹלָם שׁוּם מַחֲשָׁבָה זָרָה;
connections.quote: see note 1732 (Vol. I).
connections.context: Rav Tzadok relies on “I am prayer” to describe David’s particular spiritual quality. The verse’s expression must be retained; replacing it with standing judgment removes the foundation of the explanation.

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן נֶאֱמַר: "וְאֵת נֶפֶשׁ אֹיְבֶיךָ יְקַלְּעֶנָּה בְּתוֹךְ כַּף הַקָּלַע" (שְׁמוּאֵל א כה, כט).
connections.quote: ‘Though a man rises to pursue you and seek your life, my lord’s life will be bound in the bundle of life with Hashem your God. But the lives of your enemies He will sling away from the hollow of a sling.’

connections.hePhrase: וּבַזֹּהַר בְּשַׁלַּח (נט עַמּוּד א) דְּהוּא עַל מַעֲשִׂים שֶׁאֵינָם לַעֲבוֹדַת הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְהַיְינוּ מַעֲשִׂים בְּטֵלִים.
connections.quote: “Contrariwise, every action which is not done with this purpose becomes a “breath” which floats about in the world, and when the soul of the doer leaves his body, this “breath” rolls about like a stone in a sling, and it “breaks the spirit”. The act done and the word spoken in the service of the Holy One, however, ascend high above the sun and become a holy breath, which is the seed sowed by man in that world, and is called zedakah (righteousness, lovingkindness), as it is written: “Sow for yourselves according to righteousness” (Hos. 10, 12).”

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם הַזֹּהַר עַל פָּסוּק "כָּל הַמַּעֲשִׂים וְכוּלֵי" (קֹהֶלֶת א, יד), שֶׁמִּמַּעֲשִׂים בְּטֵלִים נַעֲשָׂה הֶבֶל, פֵּירוּשׁ זֶהוּ הַמַּחֲשָׁבוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת;
connections.quote: “I saw all the deeds done under the sun, and behold, all is vapor and pursuit of wind.”
connections.context: Hevel, often translated vanity or futility, literally denotes vapor or breath. Rav Tzadok’s explanation of the cited Zohar develops that imagery in relation to empty deeds and the thoughts they generate.

connections.hePhrase: וּמְפָרֵשׁ בְּשַׁבָּת (קנב:): זוֹמְמוֹת וְהוֹלְכוֹת, פֵּירוּשׁ מַחֲשָׁבוֹת וְהוֹלְכוֹת, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר שֶׁמִּתְלַבְּשׁוֹת נֶפֶשׁ, רוּחַ, נְשָׁמָה דִּבְטָלָה הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
connections.quote: “It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says: The souls of the righteous are stored beneath the Throne of Glory, as it says, “May my lord’s soul be bound in the bond of life.” Those of the wicked wander restlessly; one angel stands at one end of the world and another at the other end, and they sling their souls to one another, as it says, “The souls of your enemies He shall sling from the hollow of the sling.””
connections.context: The wording zomemot veholkhot describes the souls’ restless movement. Rav Tzadok reads zomemot through its association with thinking or plotting, and explains that unrest as the continued clothing of the soul in idle thoughts. “Continuously tied up” would obscure the word on which his explanation depends.

connections.hePhrase: זֶהוּ פֵּירוּשׁ כַּף הַקֶּלַע, שֶׁהוּא הֵיפֶךְ "צְרוּרוֹת בִּצְרוֹר הַחַיִּים", שֶׁהוּא הִיפּוּךְ מַחְשְׁבוֹת הֶבֶל שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם חַיּוּת כְּלָל, וְאֵינוֹ דָּבָר קָבוּעַ וּמַחֲשָׁבָה שֶׁקְּבִיעָא וְקַיָּימָא, רַק הִשְׁתּוֹטְטוּת מַחֲשַׁבְתּוֹ בְּכָל אֲשֶׁר תִּפְנֶה, וְזֶהוּ "זוֹמְמוֹת וְהוֹלְכוֹת".
connections.quote: “So too the soul itself, after separating from the body, is drawn toward the two opposing directions we mentioned: upward by its nature and downward by habit. It suffers exceedingly, as though its parts were being separated from one another. Although it has no parts, we speak in this way to give a pictorial understanding: it has two opposing desires and cannot be drawn toward either one alone. This is what our Sages said in tractate Shabbat, in the chapter Shoel: “It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says, The souls of the righteous are stored beneath the Throne of Glory, as it says, ‘The soul of my lord shall be bound in the bundle of life with the Lord your God.’ As for the wicked, one angel stands at one end of the world and another at its other end, and they sling it from one to the other, as it says, ‘The soul of your enemies He shall sling from the hollow of the sling.’” This alludes to the soul’s two opposing desires. The soul of the righteous, which has no desire directed downward, immediately attaches itself to what is natural to it: dwelling beneath the Throne of Glory. Just as the delight is above every imaginable delight, as we said earlier, so the suffering is greater than every imaginable suffering.”

connections.hePhrase: הֲרֵי שִׁכְחָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מֵחֲמַת עַצְלוּת חָשׁוּב אֹנֶס, עַיֵּין בְּמָגֵן אַבְרָהָם (סִימָן קח סָעִיף קָטָן יא), וַהֲרֵי זֶה כְּחִשֵּׁב לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה וְנֶאֱנַס וְלֹא עֲשָׂאָהּ, מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ עֲשָׂאָהּ (בְּרָכוֹת ו.).
connections.quote: ““Because he thought”: For forgetfulness is called a circumstance beyond one’s control.”

connections.hePhrase: הֲרֵי שִׁכְחָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מֵחֲמַת עַצְלוּת חָשׁוּב אֹנֶס, עַיֵּין בְּמָגֵן אַבְרָהָם (סִימָן קח סָעִיף קָטָן יא), וַהֲרֵי זֶה כְּחִשֵּׁב לַעֲשׂוֹת מִצְוָה וְנֶאֱנַס וְלֹא עֲשָׂאָהּ, מַעֲלֶה עָלָיו הַכָּתוּב כְּאִלּוּ עֲשָׂאָהּ (בְּרָכוֹת ו.).
connections.quote: “What is meant by “those who think upon His name”? Rav Ashi said: If a person intended to perform a commandment but was prevented and did not perform it, Scripture credits him as though he performed it.”
connections.context: Magen Avraham supplies the premise about forgetfulness; Berakhot supplies the principle of credit for an intended mitzvah prevented by circumstances. Rav Tzadok expressly qualifies the forgetfulness as not arising from laziness. The note covers both steps of his reasoning.

connections.hePhrase: וְהֲגַם דְּמַאן סָפֵין וּמַאן רָקֵיעַ [שָׁמַעְתִּי פֵּירוּשׁוֹ (בְּמוֹעֵד קָטָן כח.) טָהוֹר וָזַךְ כְּמוֹ הָרָקִיעַ, רְצוֹנוֹ לוֹמַר נָקִי מִנְּגִיעָה לְרָע] לָדַעַת שֶׁאֵינוֹ מֵחֲמַת עַצְלוּת,
connections.quote: “Rava was sitting before Rav Nachman and saw him slipping into sleep. He said to him: Let the master tell him not to torment me. He replied: Is the master not an important person? He answered: Who is important? Who is worthy? Who is esteemed?”
connections.context: The exchange takes place as Rav Nachman approaches death; “him” refers to the Angel of Death. The last Aramaic expression is man rakia. Rav Tzadok reports a homiletic explanation that associates rakia with the firmament and reads it as purity and clarity like the sky. That explanation is distinguished here from the ordinary meaning of the Talmudic exchange.

connections.hePhrase: וְעִיקַּר אַזְהָרַת דְּבָרִים בְּטֵלִים מִ"וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם" (דְּבָרִים ו, ז) – וְלֹא בִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ יוֹמָא יט:);
connections.quote: “Teach them diligently to your children and speak of them when you sit in your house, when you walk on the way, when you lie down, and when you rise.”
connections.context: Yoma 19b emphasizes “speak of them”—these words of Torah—as the basis for its warning against idle speech. Rav Tzadok’s point concerns speech itself, so that verb is retained.

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן בְּלָאו הַבָּא מִכְּלַל עֲשֵׂה, כַּאֲשֶׁר מְקַיֵּים הָעֲשֵׂה דְּ"וְדִבַּרְתָּ בָּם" – תִּיקֵּן הַלָּאו דִּדְבָרִים בְּטֵלִים, וְהוּא מוֹעִיל גַּם כֵּן לְעִנְיַן מַחֲשָׁבוֹת בְּטֵלוֹת.
connections.quote: “It therefore says, ‘The matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it.’ The mouth includes and joins the two: moving the lips is an action, while its essential source is the living spirit within the heart. ‘A living soul’ is translated as ‘a speaking spirit,’ joining nefesh and ruach. ‘The lips of the righteous know desire’ means connection and attachment, and also teaching understanding to the will within the heart. Through spoken words it enters the heart as well, and afterward is carried into action.”
connections.explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains why the lips have a distinctive role: their movement is an action, while their speech emerges from the heart's living spirit. The same verse about righteous lips is therefore read as teaching and joining the will. This gives the present siman's counsel a precise structure; the learner speaks in order that mind and heart also become involved, rather than treating an utterance without any intention to change as sufficient.
connections.headline: Speech joins the heart's life to actual action

connections.hePhrase: וּכְמוֹ שֶׁשָּׁמַעְתִּי עַל פָּסוּק "שִׂפְתֵי צַדִּיק יֵדְעוּן רָצוֹן" (מִשְׁלֵי י, לב), שֶׁכַּאֲשֶׁר מוֹצִיא בִּשְׂפָתָיו דְּבָרִים הַמְּצוּדָּקִים, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהִיא מִן הַשָּׂפָה וְלַחוּץ וְלִבּוֹ בַּל עִמּוֹ, מִכָּל מָקוֹם הֵם יֵדְעוּן – מוֹדִיעִים וּמְלַמְּדִים רָצוֹן לַלֵּב, לִהְיוֹת רְצוֹן הַלֵּב בֶּאֱמֶת כֵּן.
connections.quote: see note 1000 (Vol. I).
connections.context: Rav Tzadok reports a homiletic reading: the lips “make known” or teach ratzon, desire, to the heart. He develops the ordinary wording, “know what is pleasing,” into an account of sincere inward desire being awakened by proper outward speech.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין נד.): "חַיִּים הֵם לְמֹצְאֵיהֶם" (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כב) – לְמוֹצִיאֵיהֶם בַּפֶּה,
connections.quote: “Shmuel said to Rav Yehudah: Sharp one, open your mouth and read; open your mouth and study, so that it will remain with you and your life will be prolonged, as it says, “For they are life to those who find them and healing for all their flesh.” Do not read “to those who find them,” but “to those who bring them forth with the mouth.””
connections.context: The saying is on Eruvin 54a. Its wordplay makes audible articulation the means by which Torah is retained and gives life, exactly the connection Rav Tzadok is explaining.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ (עֵירוּבִין נד.): "חַיִּים הֵם לְמֹצְאֵיהֶם" (מִשְׁלֵי ד, כב) – לְמוֹצִיאֵיהֶם בַּפֶּה,
connections.quote: ‘For they are life to those who find them, and healing for all his flesh.’

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל יְדֵי הוֹצָאַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בַּפֶּה מוֹלִיד חַיּוּת, כִּדְמְתַרְגְּמִינַן: "לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה" – לְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ז), שֶׁעִיקַּר הַחַיּוּת עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר.
connections.quote: “The Lord God formed the human from dust of the ground, breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and the human became a living soul.”

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל יְדֵי הוֹצָאַת דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה בַּפֶּה מוֹלִיד חַיּוּת, כִּדְמְתַרְגְּמִינַן: "לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה" – לְרוּחַ מְמַלְּלָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ז), שֶׁעִיקַּר הַחַיּוּת עַל יְדֵי הַדִּבּוּר.
connections.quote: “The Lord God created Adam from dust of the ground and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life, and it became in Adam a speaking spirit.”
connections.context: The decisive wording is Onkelos’s “speaking spirit,” his rendering of the biblical “living soul.” Rav Tzadok uses that translation to connect human vitality with speech and the spoken words of Torah.

connections.hePhrase: וְכַאֲשֶׁר מִתְעוֹרֵר רוּחַ הַחַיִּים, אָז מְקִיצוֹ מִתַּרְדֵּמַת הָאִוֶּולֶת שֶׁבָּזֶה נִמְשָׁל כַּבְּהֵמוֹת.
connections.quote: “But man does not abide in honor; he is likened to the beasts that perish.”

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן נִקְרָא קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע לְשׁוֹן קְרִיאָה, שֶׁקּוֹרֵא לְעַצְמוֹ שֶׁיִּשְׁמַע וִיקַבֵּל דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ, וְעַל יְדֵי הִתְעוֹרְרוּת זֶה הוּא נִקְבָּע בַּלֵּב, וְיוּכַל אַחַר כָּךְ לִזְכּוֹת לִבְרַתָּא דְּמַלְכָּא צְלוֹתָא בְּכַוָּנַת הַלֵּב:
connections.quote: “This is the secret of the Shema and prayer placed next to one another by day and by night. The Shema is words of Torah, as stated in Menaḥot 99b, “Even,” and so forth. Its purpose is to awaken oneself, in the sense of “Hear, Israel,” and so forth. One must make it audible to one’s own ears: this is the recitation of the Shema, that one awaken and hear this matter. Then the echo arising within oneself in response to the voice of the Shema is the voice of the prayer that follows, born from the Shema. The voice of the prayer that follows corresponds to the voice of the Shema, according to one’s awakening and hearing of the Shema.”

connections.hePhrase: [רלו] אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם כְּלָל לַעֲמוֹד בְּכָל הַיּוֹם כֻּלּוֹ בְּמַדְרֵגָה אַחַת, תָּקוּעַ בִּדְבֵיקוּת כָּרָאוּי, וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "כִּי יִפֹּל לֹא יוּטָל" (תְּהִלִּים לז, כד), וְ"שֶׁבַע יִפּוֹל צַדִּיק וָקָם" (מִשְׁלֵי כד, טז).
connections.quote: ‘Though he falls, he will not be thrown down, for Hashem supports his hand.’

connections.hePhrase: [רלו] אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָאָדָם כְּלָל לַעֲמוֹד בְּכָל הַיּוֹם כֻּלּוֹ בְּמַדְרֵגָה אַחַת, תָּקוּעַ בִּדְבֵיקוּת כָּרָאוּי, וְעַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "כִּי יִפֹּל לֹא יוּטָל" (תְּהִלִּים לז, כד), וְ"שֶׁבַע יִפּוֹל צַדִּיק וָקָם" (מִשְׁלֵי כד, טז).
connections.displayRef: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 13:3
connections.canonicalRef: Likkutei Maamarim, Compositions on the Festivals 13:3
connections.quote: “Rabbenu Tam also mentions this in Sefer HaYashar: a person has times when he desires something and times when he recoils from it; see there. These are the familiar falls referred to by the verse, “A righteous person falls seven times and rises”: a person does not remain at his level without moving away from his service even for a moment. Since he was created with an inclination, if he remained that way it would be impossible to separate evil from good at all. This separation takes place through the power of repentance, and is accomplished through the sleep in between. Afterward he wakes from his sleep, returns, and regrets; through this, evil is gradually separated from good. The good remains by itself, while the evil passes away during the periods of sleep. Without sleep, however, separation is impossible; one could only make the evil good and transform it. This cannot be accomplished completely in this world, in which the evil inclination has already been created. Concerning this they said: “Very good”—this is sleep.”

connections.hePhrase: וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ה): שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַפָּסוּק הַזֶּה זָז מִפִּיךָ: "ה' [צְבָאוֹת עִמָּנוּ] מִשְׂגָּב לָנוּ [אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב סֶלָה]" (תְּהִלִּים מו, ח), וַחֲבֵירוֹ: "ה' [צְבָאוֹת אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם] בֹּטֵחַ בָּךְ" (שָׁם פד, יג), הַיְינוּ לְצוֹרֶךְ נְפִילוֹת הַלָּלוּ – לְהִתְחַזֵּק וְלִבְטוֹחַ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא יְשַׂגְּבֵהוּ.
connections.quote: “Hashem of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah.”

connections.hePhrase: וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ה): שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַפָּסוּק הַזֶּה זָז מִפִּיךָ: "ה' [צְבָאוֹת עִמָּנוּ] מִשְׂגָּב לָנוּ [אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב סֶלָה]" (תְּהִלִּים מו, ח), וַחֲבֵירוֹ: "ה' [צְבָאוֹת אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם] בֹּטֵחַ בָּךְ" (שָׁם פד, יג), הַיְינוּ לְצוֹרֶךְ נְפִילוֹת הַלָּלוּ – לְהִתְחַזֵּק וְלִבְטוֹחַ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא יְשַׂגְּבֵהוּ.
connections.quote: “Rabbi Chizkiyah, Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha, and Rabbi Yisa said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name: Never let this verse depart from your mouth: “Hashem of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah.” Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Avun and Rabbi Abbahu said in Rabbi Yochanan’s name, and the companions likewise: “Hashem of hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You.””
connections.context: This supplies the instruction to keep the verses in one’s mouth, beyond merely quoting Psalms 46:8. The two verses, Psalms 46:8 and 84:13, express divine protection and trust. Rav Tzadok applies their repeated recitation to regaining strength after spiritual falls.

connections.hePhrase: וּבַיְרוּשַׁלְמִי בְּרָכוֹת (רֵישׁ פֶּרֶק ה): שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא הַפָּסוּק הַזֶּה זָז מִפִּיךָ: "ה' [צְבָאוֹת עִמָּנוּ] מִשְׂגָּב לָנוּ [אֱלֹהֵי יַעֲקֹב סֶלָה]" (תְּהִלִּים מו, ח), וַחֲבֵירוֹ: "ה' [צְבָאוֹת אַשְׁרֵי אָדָם] בֹּטֵחַ בָּךְ" (שָׁם פד, יג), הַיְינוּ לְצוֹרֶךְ נְפִילוֹת הַלָּלוּ – לְהִתְחַזֵּק וְלִבְטוֹחַ בַּהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ שֶׁהוּא יְשַׂגְּבֵהוּ.
connections.quote: “Hashem of hosts, happy is the man who trusts in You.”

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל זֶה אוֹמְרִים בְּ"אַתָּה גִּבּוֹר": "סוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים", שֶׁהֵן הֵן גְּבוּרוֹתָיו לְחַזֵּק לַכֹּל, שֶׁגַּם הַחַלָּשׁ יֹאמַר: גִּבּוֹר אָנִי.
connections.displayRef: Siddur, weekday Amidah, blessing Atah Gibbor
connections.linkedRef: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Amidah, Divine Might 7
connections.canonicalRef: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Amidah, Divine Might 7
connections.heRef: סידור אשכנז, ימי חול, תפילת שחרית, עמידה, גבורות ז׳
connections.quote: “He sustains the living with kindness, revives the dead with great mercy, supports the falling, heals the sick, and releases the bound.”

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל זֶה אוֹמְרִים בְּ"אַתָּה גִּבּוֹר": "סוֹמֵךְ נוֹפְלִים", שֶׁהֵן הֵן גְּבוּרוֹתָיו לְחַזֵּק לַכֹּל, שֶׁגַּם הַחַלָּשׁ יֹאמַר: גִּבּוֹר אָנִי.
connections.quote: “Beat your plowshares into swords and your pruning hooks into spears; let the weak say, ‘I am mighty.’”

connections.hePhrase: וְאָז הֵם דְּבָרִים הַפּוֹעֲלִים, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֶּׁבַח אֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ סִפּוּר דְּבָרִים לְבַד שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי "בִּדְבַר ה' שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ" (תְּהִלִּים לג, ו), וְדִבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָשׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה.
connections.quote: ‘By Hashem’s word the heavens were made, and by the breath of His mouth all their host.’

connections.hePhrase: וְאָז הֵם דְּבָרִים הַפּוֹעֲלִים, דְּהַיְינוּ שֶׁהַשֶּׁבַח אֵינוֹ בְּדֶרֶךְ סִפּוּר דְּבָרִים לְבַד שֶׁזֶּה אֵינוֹ אֵצֶל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּי "בִּדְבַר ה' שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ" (תְּהִלִּים לג, ו), וְדִבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ חָשׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה.
connections.quote: see note 157 (Vol. I).
connections.explanation: Dover Tzedek explains the same wind-and-rain examples through the returning voice: the voice of Torah and prayer rises and gives rise to a divine response whose speech is action. This clarifies the siman's use of praise as effective speech. These examples describe that relation; they do not say that every particular request must produce its requested visible result.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶהוּ גַּם כֵּן כֹּחַ הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁהוּא דִּבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל הַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, וְנִקְרָא דִּבּוּר, יְעוּיַּן שָׁם בַּיְרוּשַׁלְמִי עַל "הָלוֹךְ וְדִבַּרְתָּ" דֶּאֱלִישָׁע וּבַגְּמָרָא תַּעֲנִית (י:).
connections.quote: “Elijah, too, parted from Elisha only amid words of Torah: “As they were walking, walking and speaking.” What were they occupied with? Rabbi Achvah son of Rabbi Zeira said: They were occupied with the recitation of Shema, as it says, “You shall speak of them.” Rabbi Yehudah ben Pazi said: They were occupied with the creation of the world, as it says, “By the word of the Lord the heavens were made.” Rabbi Yudan son of Rabbi Aivu said: They were occupied with consolations for Jerusalem, as it says, “Speak to the heart of Jerusalem.” The Rabbis said: They were occupied with the divine chariot, as it says, “And behold, a chariot of fire and horses of fire,” and so forth.”

connections.hePhrase: וּלְכָךְ אָמְרוּ (סַנְהֶדְרִין סה:): אִי בָּעוּ צַדִּיקֵי בָּרוּ עָלְמָא, הַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי עִסְקָם בַּתּוֹרָה בְּמַעֲשֵׂה בְרֵאשִׁית.
connections.quote: “Rava said: If the righteous wished, they could create a world, as it says, “Your iniquities have been separating between you and your God.””
connections.context: The Talmud connects the obstruction to sin. Rav Tzadok explains the creative power through Torah study concerning the work of creation. The source does not say that there is no distinction between God and a righteous human being; that additional assertion is not part of its wording.

connections.hePhrase: וְזֶה כֹּחוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חִיָּיא וּבָנָיו בְּבָבָא מְצִיעָא (פה:) דְּאָמַר מַשִּׁיב הָרוּחַ נָשֵׁיב וְכוּלֵי, הַיְינוּ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ שָׁם דְּעָבֵיד לַתּוֹרָה דְּלָא תִּשְׁתַּכַּח, וּבְסֻכָּה (כ.) דְּנִשְׁתַּכְּחָה תּוֹרָה וְעָלוּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא וּבָנָיו וְיִסְּדוּהָ.
connections.quote: “Reish Lakish said: May I be the atonement of Rabbi Chiyya and his sons. At first, when Torah was forgotten from Israel, Ezra came up from Babylonia and reestablished it. It was forgotten again; Hillel the Babylonian came up and reestablished it. It was forgotten again; Rabbi Chiyya and his sons came up and reestablished it.”
connections.context: This tribute identifies Rabbi Chiyya and his sons as restorers of Torah. Rav Tzadok connects that achievement with their exceptional power in prayer. The subsequent discussion of mats is unrelated to his citation and is therefore outside this excerpt.

connections.hePhrase: וְעִיקַּר סְמִיכַת נוֹפְלִים מִמַּדְרֵגָתָן הוּא עַל יְדֵי דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה שֶׁנּוֹתֶנֶת עֹז וְתוּשִׁיָּה.
connections.quote: “The Gemara says there: nevertheless, David supported them through the holy spirit, as it says, ‘The Lord supports all who fall.’ It is also written, ‘the fallen sukkah of David,’ for a sukkah is a temporary dwelling. Thus, even when it appears fallen, he supports it, continually drawing the attribute of His blessed kingship into the world. The fall is for the sake of ascent, as it says, ‘A righteous person falls seven times and rises.’ Concerning the future it is written, ‘I will raise up the fallen sukkah of David.’”
connections.explanation: Cheshvan explains that the sukkah is supported even while it appears fallen, and that the fall can become the setting of ascent. This gives the present siman’s opening confidence a concrete image. The person need not first recover a full feeling of closeness before speaking truth about Hashem or turning to Torah. Those words are themselves a means of support through which the capacity to rise and pray can return.
connections.headline: Divine support can be present while a person still feels fallen

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן "שֵׁם" הוּא הָרָצוֹן, וְכַנּוֹדָע כִּי "שְׁמוֹ" בְּגִימַטְרִיָּא "רָצוֹן", כִּי כֹּחוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ הַיְינוּ מִדַּת רְצוֹנוֹ.
connections.displayRef: Shenei Luchot HaBerit, Toldot Adam, Beit Hashem 19
connections.linkedRef: Shenei Luchot HaBerit, Toldot Adam, Beit Hashem 19
connections.canonicalRef: Shenei Luchot HaBerit, Toldot Adam, Beit Hashem 19
connections.heRef: שני לוחות הברית, תולדות אדם, 'בית ה י״ט
connections.quote: “But above, in the highest heights, at the root of the roots of the roots, before the revelation of emanation, “He” and “His name” are one essence. There the Great Name is related only to the will, insofar as He wills to bestow goodness so that the modes of being and the names may be apprehended. This will is the source of the modes of being and their names, and He and His name are one: there “He” is His name, and His name is “He.” This is hinted at in the word hu, “He,” whose initial letters signify “He and His name are one.” There the name Y-H-V-H is neither read nor written even in thought, even by Michael the great prince. When we speak there in the highest heights of His essence, we mean the mystery of the will: the concealment beyond the name Y-H-V-H, as stated. This will, in the supreme concealment beyond all concealments, is called “His name,” for shemo, “His name,” has the same numerical value as ratzon, “will.” This alludes to the profound concealment of Y-H-V-H, which amounts to the numerical value of shemo and ratzon. How? Y-H multiplied by Y-H, and V-H multiplied by V-H, amounts to shemo.”

connections.hePhrase: וְכֵן הַתּוֹרָה רְצוֹנוֹתָיו יִתְבָּרַךְ, כִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה: שֶׁאָמַר וְנַעֲשָׂה רְצוֹנוֹ.
connections.displayRef: Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 8:1
connections.linkedRef: Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 8:1
connections.canonicalRef: Tanya, Part II; Shaar HaYichud VehaEmunah 8:1
connections.heRef: תניא, חלק שני; שער היחוד והאמונה ח׳:א׳
connections.quote: “What Rambam, of blessed memory, wrote—that the Holy One, blessed be He, His being, His essence, and His knowledge are all truly one, a simple unity with no composition at all—applies in precisely the same way to all the attributes of the Holy One, blessed be He, and to all His holy names and the descriptions given to Him by the prophets and our Sages, of blessed memory, such as “gracious,” “merciful,” “kind,” and the like. The same applies to His being called “wise,” as it is written, “He too is wise,” and to His will: “The Lord desires those who fear Him,” “He desires kindness,” “He desires the repentance of the wicked and does not desire their death and their wickedness,” and “too pure of eyes to behold evil.” His will, His wisdom, His kindness, His compassion, and His other attributes add no plurality or composition, God forbid, to His being and essence. Rather, His essence and being, His will, His wisdom, His understanding and knowledge, His kindness and might, His compassion and beauty comprising His kindness and might, and likewise all His other holy attributes, are all a truly simple unity, which is His very essence and being.”

connections.hePhrase: כֵּיוָן שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לָזֶה הַנּוֹפֵל לְאִתְעָרוּתָא דִּלְתַתָּא בִּתְפִלָּה, עַל זֶה נֶאֱמַר: "וְאַבִּיט וְאֵין עֹזֵר וְגוֹמֵר וַתּוֹשַׁע לִי [זְרֹעִי וַחֲמָתִי הִיא סְמָכָתְנִי]" (יְשַׁעְיָה סג, ה):
connections.quote: “I looked, but there was no helper; I was astonished, but there was no supporter. My own arm brought Me salvation, and My wrath supported Me.”
connections.context: The verse supplies both independent divine rescue and the support associated with wrath. Rav Tzadok applies it when describing help for someone unable to initiate an ascent through prayer.

connections.hePhrase: לַהֲחֲזִירוֹ לִקְבִיעוּתוֹ.
connections.quote: “Rather, the explanation is that through observing Shabbat one merits awe and fear, as the Jerusalem Talmud says: “The awe of Shabbat rests upon an unlearned person.” Through awe he comes to repentance, as has often been explained from the Talmud: awe and repentance are one, for each depends on the other. This is “the lower Shabbat is awe, and awe rests within it,” as stated in the Zohar. This is the shofar, which signifies fear and awe, as it is said: “If a shofar is sounded in a city, will the people not tremble?””

connections.hePhrase: "וּבַשְּׁבִעִת יֵצֵא לַחָפְשִׁי",
connections.quote: ‘When you buy a Hebrew slave, he shall serve for six years; in the seventh he shall go free without payment.’

connections.hePhrase: כֵּן בַּזְּמַן – יָמִים וְשָׁנִים.
connections.displayRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Leviticus, Behar 3
connections.canonicalRef: Mei HaShiloach, Volume I, Leviticus, Behar 3
connections.quote: ““The land shall rest a Sabbath to the Lord.” The meaning of the sabbatical year is that it is a sign for Israel that “the earth and all that fills it belong to the Lord.” As stated in the holy Zohar, there are large letters and small letters. The small letters signify Shabbat, for Shabbat is a sign to Israel that the blessed God brings about everything and that nothing is accomplished through human actions. The large letters signify the sabbatical year: when seven years have passed, there must be an entire year in which it is shown that the earth belongs to the Lord, and that no person possesses the power of action; it belongs to the Lord alone.”

connections.hePhrase: דְּפֵירוּשׁ כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בִּמְגִילָּה (טו:):
connections.quote: ‘‘And for a spirit of judgment’—this is one who judges his own inclination. ‘And for one who sits in judgment’—this is one who renders a judgment that is true in its fullest sense. ‘And for strength’—this is one who overcomes his inclination. ‘Those who turn back battle’—those who debate in the battle of Torah. ‘At the gate’—(these are Torah scholars) who come early and stay late in synagogues and houses of study.’

connections.hePhrase: עַל "לְרוּחַ מִשְׁפָּט" – זֶה הַדָּן אֶת יִצְרוֹ.
connections.quote: ‘And as a spirit of judgment for the one who sits in judgment, and as strength for those who turn back the battle at the gate.’

connections.hePhrase: וּבָזֶה נֶאֱמַר "אֲשֶׁר תָּשִׂים" – לְהָבִין הַטַּעַם.
connections.quote: ““Which you shall set before them”: The Holy One, blessed be He, said to Moses: Do not think of saying, “I will repeat the chapter and the law to them two or three times, until they have it arranged in their mouths as it was taught, but I will not trouble myself to make them understand the reasons for the matter and its explanation.” Therefore it says, “Which you shall set before them”—like a table set and prepared before a person for eating.”

connections.hePhrase: מַה שֶּׁ"אִלְמָלֵא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא עוֹזְרוֹ אֵין יָכוֹל לוֹ" (קִידּוּשִׁין ל:).
connections.quote: ‘Rabbi Shimon ben Levi said: A person’s inclination grows stronger against him every day and seeks to kill him, as it says: ‘The wicked watches the righteous and seeks to kill him.’ Were the Holy One, blessed be He, not to help him, he could not overcome it, as it says: ‘God will not abandon him into his hand.’’

connections.hePhrase: יֵדַע שֶׁבֶּאֱמֶת עַל נְקוּדָּה יִשְׂרְאֵלִית אֵין הִתְנַשְּׂאוּת כְּלָל
connections.displayRef: Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 2:3
connections.canonicalRef: Sod Yesharim, The First Night of Pesach 2:3
connections.quote: “As stated in the Zohar (Mishpatim 94): ‘If she is from the side of the Shekhinah, which is the seventh, certainly what is written? In the seventh he shall go free without payment.’ A soul from the side of a servant indicates concealment of the light, on account of which a little servitude is borne outwardly. But a soul from the side of the Shekhinah indicates the essential point of Israel, and that point does not bear any servitude at all. At the Exodus, that point's freedom was revealed without any concealment, for the light shone without an intervening screen. Concerning such illumination it says there, ‘But a soul from the side of the Shekhinah, which is the seventh—certainly what is written?
