“The vital, animal soul in Israel that comes from the kelipah and is clothed in a person’s blood, as explained above; the souls of ritually pure domestic animals, wild animals, birds, and fish that may be eaten; the existence and vitality of all inanimate matter and all vegetation that may be consumed; and likewise the existence and vitality of every deed, word, and thought concerning this world that involves no prohibition—neither a root nor a branch of the 365 negative commandments or their biblical or rabbinic extensions—but is not for the sake of Heaven, and instead expresses the body’s will, desire, and appetite: all these belong to the same category. Even if something is actually necessary for the body’s existence and vitality, if one’s intention is not for the sake of Heaven, to serve Hashem with one’s body, these deeds, words, and thoughts are no better than the vital, animal soul itself. All of them alike receive and draw their vitality from the second level among the kelipot and the other side: the fourth kelipah, called kelipat nogah. In this world, called the World of Asiyah, it is almost entirely evil, with only a little good mixed into it. From it come the good traits of the animal soul in Israel, as explained above.

It is an intermediate condition between the three completely impure kelipot and the condition and level of holiness.

Therefore it is sometimes incorporated within the three impure kelipot, as stated in Etz Chayim, Gate 49, at the beginning of chapter 4, in the name of the Zohar. At other times it is incorporated within and ascends to the condition and level of holiness: namely, when the good mixed into it is separated from the evil, prevails, and ascends to become incorporated within holiness.

For example, someone eats rich beef and drinks fragrant wine to broaden his mind for Hashem and His Torah, as Rava said, ‘Wine and fragrance,’ and so forth; or he does so to fulfill the commandment of delighting in Shabbat and the festivals. The vitality of the meat and wine, which had flowed from kelipat nogah, is then refined and ascends to Hashem like a burnt offering and sacrifice.

The same applies to someone who says something humorous to open his mind and gladden his heart for Hashem, His Torah, and His service, which must be undertaken joyfully. This is what Rava did for his students: he first said something humorous before them, and the Sages were cheered.”

connections.hePhrase: שֶׁזֶּה אִי אֶפְשָׁר לְתַקֵּן לְגַמְרֵי בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
connections.quote: “Therefore the Zohar says that repentance does not avail: this means availing completely, according to the full measure of repentance in which deliberate sins become merits, the past is entirely repaired and even becomes a merit. If this were attained here, the guard of the tree of life would be removed and the person could eat and live forever; this is not Hashem's will in this world. The guards prevent a repair and complete return extending to living forever. Nevertheless, “nothing stands in the way of repentance,” and repentance concerning the holy covenant brings a person from death to length of days and years.”
connections.explanation: Takanat HaShavin explains this very qualification of the Zohar. It defines the negation as complete repair that would remove the guard of the tree of life and allow endless bodily life, then explicitly states that nothing stands in the way of repentance. Reading it beside the final siman prevents “repentance does not help” from being detached from the immediately stated meaning of total repair. The siman itself ends by placing that final root repair in divine aid.
connections.headline: Repentance is open; total root repair is a further claim

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב) דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה לְהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
connections.quote: “For we have learned: Whoever emits his seed in vain is called evil and does not see the face of the Divine Presence.”

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב) דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה לְהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
connections.quote: “We learned: Rabbi Yehudah said, there is no sin in the world for which there is no repentance except this one; and no sinners who cannot see the face of the Divine Presence except this one, as it is written: “Evil shall not dwell with You”—at all.”
connections.context: The first passage identifies what “this one” means; the second is the severe statement Rav Tzadok quotes from Zohar I 219b. He immediately explains his use of teshuvah here as complete correction of the root, which in his account would entail the final removal of death. The former note instead quoted the nearby discussion of death being swallowed up and did not contain the statement cited.

connections.hePhrase: וְלָכֵן אָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר (חֵלֶק א, ריט עַמּוּד ב) דְּאֵין מוֹעִיל תְּשׁוּבָה לְהוֹצָאַת זֶרַע לְבַטָּלָה,
connections.quote: “In any event, the understanding shared by them all—that the Zohar’s statement “he has no repentance” concerns forgiveness of the sin and atonement themselves—is certainly astonishing and strange, and everything they wrote to explain it is strained and remote. All the more so is the plain sense that he has no repentance at all certainly impossible: the prohibition of a married woman is unquestionably more severe, as is also explained in Sefer Chasidim, cited by Chelkat Mechokek and Beit Shmuel and mentioned above. Concerning David’s act with Bathsheba, which involved a married woman, they said at the end of Avodah Zarah 4b that he was not suited to it, but it occurred to teach repentance: if an individual sins, and so forth; see there. Thus even the more severe sin involving a married woman admits repentance, and certainly this does. But according to what I explained above concerning the repentance prescribed by the Rokeach and the Ari—that these practices do not prevent atonement but are a gift, each person according to his level—it seems clear to me that the Zohar, too, intends the acceptance achieved through a gift: that one be accepted completely, to ascend and appear before God at lofty levels, like an entirely righteous guardian of the covenant who never sinned. This applies to all transgressions: through complete repentance from love, deliberate sins become merits, and through them he shall live. That is, after the appropriate repentance and the bringing of the gift, he again becomes close and a member of the household as before, with even greater strength, since the sins themselves enter the reckoning of commandments. Concerning this, the Zohar said that for this transgression repentance does not make it into merits or restore one entirely to the former state, even after all the gifts. The Rokeach and the Ari spoke according to their levels: each person’s repentance is effective for the level he apprehended it could achieve. Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s level of apprehension, and what he revealed to his companions, was higher than all of them, as is known from what he said about himself in the holy Zohar and about his entire generation: that there would be no generation like that one, and that such a revelation would not occur again until the coming of Mashiach. In accordance with the level they apprehended, they said that repentance for this sin does not enable one to attain so lofty a level, which can be reached only by an entirely righteous guardian of the covenant who never blemished it.”

connections.hePhrase: כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּעֵץ חַיִּים, שַׁעַר קְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, דְּכָל טִיפַּת קֶרִי הוּא בִּקְלִיפַּת נוֹגַהּ, עַיֵּין שָׁם.
connections.quote: “All the drops of the “plagues of human beings” go there, into the shells of nogah, the female aspect of nogah, and it becomes good and evil; understand this. Concerning this it is said, “I too shall walk with you in the fury of keri,” for fury is the female aspect of nogah. Remember this: in the shell of each of the four worlds there are iniquity, destroyer, anger, and fury, which are Chokhmah, Binah, Zeir Anpin, and the female aspect of nogah. They are not equal, in the manner explained above concerning Samael and Lilith. Wherever keri is found, it belongs to nogah; remember this. See Terumah, page 130. The good within this nogah is the eleven ingredients of the incense. Galbanum is the female aspect of Zeir Anpin of nogah, and therefore its smell is bad, because its evil adheres to it. The shell of nogah is nourished by the smoke of the offerings, for the animal soul within a person and within kosher animals comes from there.”

connections.hePhrase: וְכֶתֶר כְּהֻנָּה הוּא הַזֵּיר דְּמִזְבַּח מִקְטַר קְטֹרֶת כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (יוֹמָא עב:).
connections.quote: see note 520 (Vol. I).

connections.hePhrase: וְהַיְינוּ כִּמְשֶׁאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרָכוֹת מג:) דְּרֵיחַ הַנְּשָׁמָה נֶהֱנֵית מִמֶּנּוּ.
connections.quote: ‘Rav Yehudah said: One who goes out in the days of Nisan and sees trees blossoming says: ‘Blessed is He who has left nothing lacking in His world and has created in it good creatures and good trees for people to enjoy.’ Rav Zutra bar Toviyah said in Rav’s name: From where do we know that a blessing is recited over a fragrance? It is stated: ‘Let every soul praise Yah.’ What is something from which the soul derives pleasure, but the body does not? You must say: It is fragrance.’

connections.hePhrase: כִּי הַנְּשָׁמָה בָּאַף, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב: "נְשָׁמָה בְּאַפּוֹ" (יְשַׁעְיָה ב, כב),
connections.quote: ‘Cease relying on man, whose breath is in his nostrils, for of what account is he?’

connections.hePhrase: וְרֵיחַ בַּמּוֹחַ שֶׁמּוֹשֵׁךְ הָרֵיחָנִי דֶּרֶךְ הָאַף.
connections.quote: “The human body belongs to the lower world, and the higher soul is bound to it. There are intermediaries between the soul and the body: two powers, generally called ruach and nefesh in the holy tongue. The neshamah is wisdom, and its dwelling is in the brain of the head. From it comes the power of all the senses and voluntary movement. The ruach is in the heart, and in it is human life. It seeks dominion, to overcome whatever opposes it, and it possesses anger. Thus Solomon said, “Do not be hasty in your spirit to become angry,” and, “A fool gives vent to all his spirit.” The nefesh is in the liver, and it desires to eat, as it is written, “For your nefesh desires”; sexual desire also comes from it.”

connections.hePhrase: וְהוּא נֶגֶד חַיָּה וִיחִידָה שֶׁהֵם גַּם כֵּן מַקִּיפִים כַּנּוֹדָע.
connections.quote: “Concerning the five internal aspects—nefesh, ruach, neshamah, chayah, and yechidah—and the two encompassing aspects, chayah and yechidah: one must know that even among the five internal aspects each has an encompassing aspect, as with the souls of Nadav, Avihu, and Elijah, of blessed memory. But these two encompassing aspects are different, comprehensive ones, apart from the five encompassing aspects within the internal aspects. A sign of this is that among these internal encompassing aspects there are more than five: an encompassing light, an encompassing light around that encompassing light, and an encompassing light around the two encompassing lights, as mentioned in the section on the Priestly Blessing in the Idra Rabba. Thus all these are distinct from those two comprehensive ones.”

connections.hePhrase: דְּתַמָּן אִימָּא עִילָּאָה מְקַנֶּנֶת
connections.quote: “At that time, “You shall not take the mother together with the young.” Eggs are from the side of the Ofanim; chicks are from the side of the Youth, Metatron; children are from the side of the Throne, which is the shelter of peace, the nest of the Shechinah. For the supernal Mother nests in the Throne with the three upper sefirot. The central pillar encompasses six sefirot, which nest in Metatron. The lower Mother nests in the Ofan, concerning which it is said, “Behold, one wheel on the earth.””

connections.hePhrase: וְצָרִיךְ לִזְבּוֹחַ הַזֶּבַח לְשֵׁם רֵיחַ (כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זְבָחִים מו:).
connections.quote: ‘Mishnah: A sacrifice is slaughtered with six matters in mind: its proper kind of sacrifice, its owner, Hashem, the sacrificial fires, the fragrance, and giving pleasure. The sin offering and the guilt offering are also slaughtered with the particular sin for which they are brought in mind.’

connections.hePhrase: כָּל מִינֵי רֵיחוֹת טוֹבוֹת בְּצֵירוּף הַחֶלְבְּנָה שֶׁרֵיחָהּ רַע גַּם כֵּן
connections.quote: “Rav Chana bar Bizna said in the name of Rabbi Shimon Chasida: Any fast that does not include some of the sinners of Israel is not a fast, for galbanum has a bad smell, yet Scripture counted it among the ingredients of the incense. Abaye said: It is learned from here: “And He founded His gathering upon the earth.””

connections.hePhrase: וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה הִיא קִישּׁוּרָא דְּכוּלָּא,
connections.quote: “Come and see: incense binds bonds and holds together above and below. This removes death, accusation, and wrath, so that they cannot rule in the world, as it is written, “Moses said to Aaron: Take the firepan, place fire upon it from the altar, put incense on it, and bring it quickly,” and so forth. After this it is written, “And (Aaron) ran,” and so forth, “and made atonement for the people”; and it is written, “He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague was stopped.” For none of the evil sides or accusers can stand before incense. Therefore it is the mystery of everything (another reading: the joy of everything) and the binding of everything.”

connections.hePhrase: וַיַּעַן יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמֶר:
connections.quote: “The booklet Divrei Chalomot is completed, with Heaven's help. Yisrael said: I shall bless at the completion, for Hashem enabled me to mark the references in the book Resisei Layla and the booklet Divrei Chalomot. They are enclosed in two round halves, thus: (). May Hashem help us so that our master's words, may the memory of the righteous and holy be a blessing for life in the world to come, enter our hearts to love and revere Hashem, and so that our children and children's children engage in Torah and fear of Hashem all their days. Yisrael, son of my father, our teacher and master, the pious rabbi Yosef Yozel, of blessed memory for life in the world to come, of Lublin.”
connections.explanation: This paragraph is the annotator Yisrael's notice, following the book's closing colophon. Here he distinguishes square-bracketed matter copied from the manuscript from round-parenthesized references he supplied. The Divrei Chalomot epilogue bears the same signature and explicitly uses round parentheses for his references in that work and Resisei Layla. It confirms that convention; it does not extend the square-bracket rule beyond what this notice actually says.
connections.headline: The annotator's reference conventions
